name: 12co-line-flux-modelling
description: Use when synthesising 12CO fluxes for populations of protoplanetary discs (e.g. Lupus, Upper Sco) where running thermochemical codes per disc is prohibitively slow, or when tracing disc surface-area evolution from optically thick CO fluxes.

name: 1f-plus-white-noise-synthesis
description: Use when building simulated polarimeter timestreams (signal-only and signal-plus-noise) to test a destriping pipeline, e.g. with B-Machine-like 1/f noise parameters and ~33.4 Hz sampling.

name: 2d-gp-multiwavelength-surface-modeling
description: Use when you have multiwavelength broadband photometry (e.g., a space-separated CSV like example_data/grb_afterglow.csv with GRB afterglow data) and need a joint, data-driven model over both time and frequency axes rather than fitting each band separately.

name: 3d-model-deviation-comparison
description: Use when you have both a reconstructed 3-D model (from SfM/MVS over rendered or real images) and the original reference model, and need quantitative reconstruction-accuracy metrics such as Gaussian mean and standard deviation of point deviations.

name: absorption-edge-parameter-extraction
description: Use when a raw XAS transmission spectrum (e.g. energy, i0, it columns in an ASCII file like fe.060) must be converted to absorbance and normalized around an absorption edge before XANES/EXAFS processing.

name: accretion-rate-boundary-check
description: Use when a ThompsonAGN disk has been configured with a user-supplied Mdot_out and Rout, and downstream work (e.g. migration-torque profiles) requires proof that Mdot_out < Mdot_c at the outer boundary.

name: accretion-rate-profile-extraction
description: Use when a solved pAGN disk object is available and you need Mdot(R), the outer-boundary Mdot_c/Mdot_out values, or the inner-boundary Mdot at Rin to judge whether the disk can fuel a bright AGN.

name: accuracy-runtime-tradeoff-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing the number of PCA explanatory variables in a gamma-GLM photo-z pipeline when both catastrophic error (|z_phot - z_spec| > 0.10) and compute budget matter.

name: activity-indicator-time-series-derivation
description: Use when you have reduced FITS echelle spectra (e.g. CARMENES VIS/NIR, HARPS, HARPN, EXPRES) and need per-observation radial velocities plus activity indicators assembled into a time-series table via the CCF method.

name: adaptive-ode-solving-with-tsit5
description: Use when a JAX/Equinox neural ODE or neural CDE hidden state must be integrated over an interpolated control path (e.g. Hermite cubic splines over 2D spiral classification data) with adaptive step-size control rather than a fixed grid.

name: adaptive-rung-assignment-via-acceleration-criterion
description: Use when implementing or validating adaptive, individual-particle time-stepping in an N-body cosmology code, or when verifying that per-particle rung assignments keep positions mutually synchronised over a base-step cycle.

name: adiabatic-isothermal-gamma-derivation
description: Use when migration torques must be computed for a black-hole migrator embedded in a solved AGN disk (Sirko & Goodman or Thompson et al. models) and the local surface-density, temperature, and pressure gradients feeding Jiménez & Masset 2017, Masset 2017, and Paardekooper et al.

name: agglomerative-hierarchical-clustering-of-parameters
description: Use when a correlation matrix (Pearson, Spearman, or MIC) of parameters has been computed and you need to reveal multi-level structure among variables via agglomerative hierarchical clustering without pre-specifying the cluster count.

name: agn-disc-model-solving
description: Use when a 1D radial profile (Teff, Sigma, h/r, opacity, Mdot(r)) of an AGN disk is needed from the Sirko & Goodman 2003 or Thompson et al. 2005 models as input to luminosity, torque, or compact-object-formation analyses.

name: agn-disc-structure-modelling
description: Use when a task requires a fully evolved 1D AGN disc model (radial temperature, density, surface-density, scale-height, optical-depth profiles) for a given central BH mass, Eddington ratio or accretion rate, and viscosity alpha.

name: agn-sfg-classification-inference
description: Use when you have a catalog CSV of extragalactic radio-survey sources with multi-band photometric flux densities (in μJy) and redshifts, and need AGN/SFG classifications via a trained LightGBM model.

name: agn-sfg-classification-metrics-computation
description: Use when you have run MBASC on a labelled test set with multi-wavelength fluxes (μJy) and redshifts, and need to evaluate how SFG/AGN precision and recall vary across redshift bins rather than only on the full test set.

name: agn-sfg-supervised-label-classification
description: Use when you have a photometric catalog with multi-band fluxes (optical u-r, NIR JHK, IRAC ch1-ch4, MIPS24, PACS/SPIRE far-IR, 150 MHz radio) and redshifts, and need AGN/SFG labels for extragalactic radio survey sources.

name: agn-starburst-host-galaxy-decomposition
description: Use when a galaxy ultraviolet-to-millimetre SED must be decomposed into or reconstructed from SMART's starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust radiative transfer library components.

name: aips-visibility-data-handling
description: Use when interferometric visibility data (e.g. e-MERLIN UVFITS) must be read into AIPS, flagged or reduced programmatically, and written back out ready for AIPS calibration.

name: airmass-extinction-trend-modeling
description: Use when fitting ground-based transit light curves that show smooth, airmass-correlated brightness trends (e.g. from differential extinction during the night), and you need unbiased transit parameters and per-transit Tmid via MCMC.

name: alp-exclusion-limit-derivation
description: Use when re-analyzing a Fermi-LAT observation (e.g. NGC 1275) to constrain ALP-photon coupling gaγ as a function of ALP mass ma, or when testing how exclusion limits change under different ICMF/GMF magnetic field configurations (turbulent vs regular).

name: alp-exclusion-region-estimation
description: Use when re-analyzing long-baseline Fermi-LAT observations (e.g. 12 years of PKS 2155-304 / 4FGL J2158.8-3013 or NGC 1275) to test whether ALP-induced spectral oscillation structure can be excluded, using irregularity statistics rather than spectral model fitting.

name: alp-parameter-bound-tabulation
description: Use when Fermi-LAT spectra of one or more ALP-sensitive sources are available and you need 95% CL exclusion contours in the (gaγ, ma) grid, especially combining sources for improved bounds.

name: alp-parameter-constraint-visualization
description: Use when re-analyzing Fermi-LAT observations (e.g. NGC 1275) to constrain ALP-photon coupling gaγ as a function of ALP mass ma, or when reproducing a 95% CL exclusion contour such as gaγ > 3×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ at ma ∼ 1 neV.

name: alp-parameter-grid-sampling
description: Use when reconstructing ALP parameter exclusions from Fermi-LAT spectra of NGC 1275-like sources: you need conversion-probability curves P_γ→a(E) on a (g_aγ, m_a) grid spanning couplings down to ~3×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ and ma ∼ 1 neV.

name: alp-photon-conversion-probability-calculation
description: Use when re-analyzing Fermi-LAT spectra of AGN (e.g., NGC 1275, PKS 2155-304) to search for ALP-induced spectral oscillations and need energy-dependent photon–ALP conversion probabilities across a (g_aγ, m_a) parameter grid.

name: amr-refinement-scaling-analysis
description: Use when a task asks to transcribe, reproduce, or validate reported strong-scaling behavior of block-structured AMR codes (Castro Sedov/wdmerger on OLCF Titan, Figure 3) into a table with core counts, threading mix, and compiler fields.

name: analytic-inverse-solution-derivation
description: Use when validating a numerical equilibrium radiative-transfer solver (e.g. rabacus Slab_Pln) against an analytic benchmark, or when a closed-form ionization-fraction-vs-column-depth profile is needed for a uniform pure-H slab under monochromatic plane-parallel illumination.

name: analytic-shock-solution-comparison
description: Use when a code-validation task requires comparing an SPH solution to a known analytic shock solution — specifically when FleCSPH's Noh shock test (2D or 3D) can be generated, evolved with hydro drivers, and checked against the analytic density plateau.

name: analytical-jacobian-verification-against-numerical-differentiation
description: Use when an ODE/perturbation solver provides a symbolically or analytically generated Jacobian and you must prove it is correct before relying on it for implicit integration or AD-based inference.

name: anchor-point-selection-for-latent-interpolation
description: Use when training a spectral surrogate (e.g. an IAE for SUSHI) from a physical emission model such as APEC thermal plasma or power-law synchrotron spectra, and the interpolatory scheme needs anchor points spanning the parameter boundaries.

name: angular-power-spectrum-estimation
description: Use when you have partial-sky CMB polarization maps (HEALPix Q/U FITS) and need to quantify residual noise or signal power, e.g. checking that destriping removed excess correlated-noise power at intermediate angular scales.

name: anisotropic-potential-expansion-interpretation
description: Use when a molscat/BOUND run specifies an anisotropic potential via &POTL (MXLAM, LAMBDA, NTERM, NPOWER, A) and you need to reproduce or replace it with a user-supplied VSTAR routine, or verify the printed POTENL expansion matches documented coefficients.

name: antoine-equation-parameterization
description: Use when estimating a vapour pressure at a temperature below the measured range (e.g. 20°C) for an organometallic compound whose hydrocarbon analogue (Sn→C substitution) has known boiling point data, and no direct measurement is available.

name: aperture-mass-map-generation
description: Use when given a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog (positions and elliptities) and the goal is to produce an aperture mass map over the surveyed field via the Schirmer et al (2007) filter.

name: appendix-table-reproduction
description: Use when a paper publishes an appendix results table (e.g. Table B.1 of the SUSHI paper) and the associated artifact (trained models, validation splits) is released in the companion repository, so the numbers can be regenerated and checked.

name: archival-ps1-cutout-retrieval
description: Use when a pre-transient host-galaxy reference is needed for SEDm scene modeling: downloading PS1 grizy stack cutouts at the transient position to feed per-pixel CIGALE SED fitting or host contamination estimation.

name: arrival-time-histogram-generation
description: Use when you have completed an OSPREI run (single case or nRuns > 1 ensemble) and need to turn its systematic output files into forecaster-facing figures, e.g. arrival-time histograms and profiles.

name: ascii-spectral-data-reading
description: Use when the input is a plain-text, column-delimited XAFS/XAS spectrum (e.g., fe.060 from an xafsdata folder) that must be ingested into a Larch group before pre_edge/autobk/xftf processing.

name: askaryan-trace-to-detector-signal-conversion
description: Use when input is radio field traces propagated to detector positions by NuRadioMC and the goal is detector-level voltage traces and per-station trigger decisions.

name: assembly-bias-validation
description: Decision support for testing whether an empirical halo-assembly model reproduces not only mean halo mass growth but the per-halo diversity of assembly histories, and whether residual assembly-bias correlations remain.

name: ast-channel-text-serialisation
description: Use when you need to generate or validate the human-readable, block-structured AST text description of a Mapping (e.g. a CmpMap of PermMap and ZoomMap) and compare it against a reference listing.

name: ast-frameset-serialisation
description: Use when an AST FrameSet encoding inter-related coordinate systems (pixel↔FITS primary WCS, or VRAD↔FREQ spectral systems) must be persisted to or recovered from a text representation.

name: ast-library-python-binding-usage
description: Use when a task requires modelling, manipulating or storing inter-related coordinate systems with AST — especially building SwitchMap/SelectorMap region-based routing and pushing position tables through route Mappings.

name: ast-mapping-construction
description: Use when you need to build or verify an AST compound Mapping (e.g. a CmpMap over PermMap/ZoomMap components) or check its block-structured Channel text output against a reference listing such as the paper's Section 4 output.

name: ast-skyframe-attribute-manipulation
description: Use when a task requires converting sky coordinates between systems (e.g. ICRS RA,Dec to Galactic l,b) using AST, and the conversion should be obtained as a reusable, serialisable FrameSet Mapping.

name: asteroid-albedo-texturing
description: Use when a plain, undistorted asteroid/small-body mesh must gain realistic surface features (sand flats, rock formations, craters) and surface albedo for photorealistic Cycles rendering in SISPO.

name: asteroid-model-multiview-image-rendering
description: Use when a synthetic image set from multiple viewing angles around a spinning SSSB is needed as input for computer-vision or 3-D reconstruction experiments, given a 3-D shape model and a defined camera/trajectory setup.

name: astrochemical-abundance-feature-design
description: Use when building a neural-ODE surrogate for an astrochemical solver (e.g. 3D-PDR) and you must decide which physical quantities parameterise the ODE vector field versus which quantities are integrated as state features.

name: astrochemistry-emulator-evaluation
description: Use when a trained neural surrogate for PDR chemistry (3D-PDR emulation) must be validated against reference observables — specifically reproducing observable column density maps from predicted chemical abundances and temperatures.

name: astronomical-catalog-flag-filtering
description: Use when a source catalog already ships a per-source morphological classification column (e.g. HSC's extended flag) and only extended (galaxy) sources should be retained before downstream computations such as chance-alignment probability estimates.

name: astronomical-catalog-parameter-clustering
description: Use when a tabular astronomical catalog (CSV/TXT, columns = variables, missing values marked NA) needs unsupervised structure discovery and no number of clusters is known a priori.

name: astronomical-catalog-unsupervised-structure-detection
description: Use when a hierarchical clustering tree built on correlation distance d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)| between catalog variables needs a data-driven choice of how many clusters to cut it into.

name: astronomical-coordinate-systems-model-construction
description: Use when a task must model, manipulate, or verify inter-related coordinate systems (base/intermediate/current Frames connected by Mappings) and needs to confirm that mutating a current Frame through a FrameSet keeps enclosed Mappings consistent.

name: astronomical-data-unit-validation
description: Use when a FITS file has been converted to another format (HDF5/HDFITS) and converted back, and you must prove whether the round trip is lossless at the data-value and header/byte level.

name: astronomical-fits-image-generation
description: Use when a simulation image must be produced without writing Python code — by feeding a YAML config such as demo1.yaml to the galsim executable and writing the rendered galaxy+PSF image to a FITS file.

name: astronomical-follow-up-candidate-selection
description: Use when you have a large photometric source catalogue with per-source classification probabilities (e.g. 3.5 million SDSS+WISE sources scored by SHEEP) and need to flag sources with ambiguous class probabilities for follow-up observations.

name: astronomical-image-colormap-mapping
description: Use when serving tiled floating-point (16/32-bit) astronomical images to an HTML5 web client and the client's Channel Mixing panel requests a pseudocolor colormap, gamma, or per-channel min/max level cuts on full-precision server-held pixels.

name: astronomical-image-cutout-rendering
description: Use when interactive inspection of individual astronomical detections is needed: a catalog or Highcharts plot of point sources exists and, for each selected source, cutouts from same-field images in multiple filters must be rendered alongside a surface plot.

name: astronomical-image-morphology-embedding
description: Use when you have a large collection of unlabelled astronomical FITS images (e.g. ALMA disk observations) and need label-free embeddings that capture morphological differences for clustering, anomaly detection, or similarity-based exploration.

name: astronomical-image-visualization-load-testing
description: Use when comparing elapsed load time and resident memory of a multi-GB HDS/HDF5 dataset opened in a visualization tool (e.g. GAIA) with datMap memory mapping enabled versus disabled.

name: astronomical-mapping-simplification-rules
description: Use when a compound AST Mapping (CmpMap) built by stacking transformations must be reduced to its canonical minimal form, and each class-specific simplification rule must be empirically verified.

name: astronomical-multi-channel-image-ingestion
description: Use when input is a directory of FITS images (single-channel 2D images or multi-channel spectral cubes) that must feed a PyTorch pipeline such as BYOL pretraining.

name: astronomical-multivariate-table-import
description: Use when a high-dimensional astronomical catalog must be loaded into AMADA for PCA/clustering exploration and the source table needs conversion to AMADA's CSV/TXT input format with named columns and NA-coded missing entries.

name: astronomical-parameter-correlation-matrix-export
description: Use when a high-dimensional astronomical dataset (e.g., a galaxy catalog or supernova host-galaxy property table in CSV/TXT with named, space-separated columns) needs pairwise variable correlation matrices under multiple measures for clustering or visualization.

name: astronomical-pipeline-stage-execution
description: Use when a dedispersed time series (one series per DM trial, e.g. 5120 DMs from AMBER's Dedispersion stage) must be downsampled by time integration or another AMBER pipeline stage must be run on many-core hardware before SNR computation.

name: astronomical-sample-count-verification
description: Use when a paper reports inventory-style counts (N spectra, N targets, N RVs) for a public data release and the counts must be independently re-derived from the release metadata and validated against the published values.

name: astronomical-sky-background-median-estimation
description: Use when transcoding FITS science imagery to a browser-friendly TIFF for IIPImage/VisiOmatic and default Smin/Smax display cuts must be derived from the pixel-value histogram and the sky median.

name: astronomical-source-classification
description: Use when you have tabular photometry (e.g. SDSS DR15+WISE magnitudes/fluxes, possibly sparse) for millions of sources and need 3-class classification into galaxies, quasars, and stars with per-class F1 targets.

name: astronomical-time-series-modelling
description: Use when fitting GP models to astronomical time series (time and flux measurements) — e.g. stellar variability, exoplanet transit light curves, transmission spectroscopy — and the covariance structure should be inferred from the data rather than fixed by hand.

name: astronomical-time-series-phase-folding
description: Use when you have sparse astronomical light curves (time, magnitude, measurement uncertainties) with an unknown periodicity, and need to identify the true frequency by folding at trial frequencies on a grid (e.g. np.linspace(0.001, 5, 50000)) and minimising a regression-fit statistic.

name: astronomical-world-coordinate-system-interpretation
description: Use when a buffer of FITS header cards containing WCS keywords (CTYPE/CRVAL/CRPIX-type cards) must be interpreted into an explicit coordinate-system model, i.e. an AST FrameSet whose base Frame is pixel coordinates and whose current Frame is the FITS primary WCS frame.

name: astrophysical-burning-network-benchmarking
description: Use when a paper reports accelerator speedups for ported reaction-network kernels (e.g., Tesla P100 vs. a single Power8 core) and the values must be extracted per network and per grid size into a comparison table.

name: astrophysical-simulation-code-optimization-status-recording
description: Use when reproducing or reporting a performance figure for an AMReX-based astrophysics code on a specific platform (e.g., Castro's wdmerger self-gravity test on NERSC Cori Intel Xeon Phi) and the hardware configuration plus stated optimization status must be recorded as a machine-readable artifact.

name: astrophysical-simulation-result-curation
description: Use when a task requires reproducing the paper's Figure 6 science-results summary — i.e., extracting per-problem qualitative claims (ignition regime, Kolmogorov turbulence, WD-merger masses, sonic-regime restart) with their figure/section citations from the article text.

name: astropy-sky-coordinate-observer-evaluation
description: Use when you need pointwise or timestream zodiacal emission intensities at specific sky coordinates and obstimes from a ZodiPy model (dirbe, planck13/15/18, rrm-experimental, odegard), e.g. to reproduce DIRBE or Planck predictions.

name: astropy-unified-io-registry-usage
description: Use when reading time-domain GW data files (GWOSC HDF5 strain) into GWpy array classes and you need the attached source, t0, duration, sample_rate and unit metadata extracted and validated.

name: astropy-units-handling
description: Use when building inputs for ZodiPy evaluations: any wavelength/bandpass, SkyCoord lon/lat, or obstime that feeds model.evaluate or grid_number_density must be expressed as Astropy Quantities/Time objects to get MJy/sr intensities.

name: asynchronous-gpu-transfer-overlap-scheduling
description: Use when the RIME problem (ntime × na × nchan × npsrc arrays) is too large to fit in a GPU memory budget (e.g. mem_budget=4GB) yet a single χ² scalar must still be produced.

name: asynchronous-mpi-non-blocking-communication
description: Use when a distributed tree traversal (e.g., FleCSPH's parallel octree over SPH particles) encounters nodes owned by other MPI ranks and the traversal must proceed without blocking on remote data.

name: atmospheric-wave-eigenvalue-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or validating stellar/atmospheric wave eigenmode spectra from a stratified atmosphere, checking acoustic frequency spacing and gravity-mode period spacing against theory.

name: atomic-hydrogen-level-population-solving
description: Use when you need level population densities of excited hydrogen states (e.g. the 3p state) or hydrogen recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha) for gas with specified ne, nHI, nHII, and temperature.

name: augmentation-based-contrastive-free-pretraining
description: Use when you need label-free image embeddings from FITS astronomical imaging (e.g. ALMA protoplanetary disks, Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark clouds) to enable clustering, anomaly detection, or similarity-based exploration without manually labelled data.

name: auto-differentiation-of-neural-spectral-decoder
description: Use when fitting a learned (non-analytical) spectral model to hyperspectral/IFU data cubes and gradient descent on the model's latent parameters is needed inside a proximal optimization loop.

name: autodiff-likelihood-fisher-matrix-computation
description: Use when you need cosmological parameter forecast errors from a CMB power-spectrum likelihood (TT/TE/EE, BB, phi-phi, kappa-kappa) and want exact Hessian-based Fisher matrices without finite differences.

name: autoencoder-testing-set-evaluation
description: Use when one or more trained IAE spectral models (e.g. the five SUSHI networks for thermal/synchrotron components) must be validated on held-out testing spectra, with reconstruction residuals compared to published reference values such as Table B.1.

name: automated-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when training SHEEP's gradient-boosted photo-z regressors or galaxy/QSO/star classifiers on SDSS DR15+WISE photometry and tuned hyper-parameters are needed, or whenever the input feature table has changed.

name: automated-imaging-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you have pre-calibrated multi-epoch radio-synthesis visibilities (e.g. AMI-LA measurement sets) and need automated calibration-to-image reduction with source detection, avoiding 'Clean-bias'.

name: automated-source-detection-mask-building
description: Use when imaging pre-calibrated multi-epoch radio-synthesis measurement sets with chimenea/CASA and you need a source mask so per-epoch Clean components are placed only near known steady sources.

name: autotools-build-rule-integration
description: Use when a C library build needs automated wrapper/interface generation wired into GNU Autoconf/Automake, so that generated SWIG interfaces and language bindings are rebuilt as part of the standard configure/build flow.

name: backend-interface-verification
description: Use when a GAMBIT scan (e.g. a DarkBit module-mode run like `gambit -f yaml_files/MSSM7.yaml`) is about to be launched and you must confirm the backends and scanners it depends on are installed and configured.

name: background-cosmology-integration
description: Use when benchmarking stiff ODE integration of a cosmological (or similarly stiff physical) model subsystem against a low-tolerance reference solution, especially to quantify solver stability and accuracy trade-offs across tolerance sweeps.

name: background-rms-estimation-via-sigma-clipping
description: Use when cleaning radio-interferometric dirty/residual maps where a noise threshold must be estimated from an image that is itself not yet clean, and Clean-bias must be avoided.

name: bad-pixel-masking
description: Use when preprocessing raw AAOmega-format (or generic FITS) spectra with flux, variance, and wavelength extensions before redshift matching, and pixels need to be flagged as unreliable.

name: bad-value-handling-in-coordinate-transforms
description: Use when transforming test positions through an AST SwitchMap (or any Region-gated Mapping) and you must classify which route Mapping each input selects and which inputs yield the AST bad value.

name: balmer-paschen-brackett-series-transitions
description: Use when calculating or validating hydrogen recombination line emissivities (Hα, Paschen, Brackett) for a photoionized nebula with given electron/proton densities and temperature, or when benchmarking an atomic model against Cloudy.

name: band-power-bin-width-optimisation
description: Use when designing or tuning the binning of CMB power spectrum band powers (e.g. SPT-3G TT/TE/EE mock data) and you need the bin width that minimises forecast parameter errors via Fisher matrices.

name: barycentric-motion-alignment
description: Use when constructing an S-BART stellar template from multiple HARPS or ESPRESSO S2D observations: spectra taken at different BERV values must first be shifted to a common barycentric frame before order-wise co-addition.

name: baryonic-acceleration-computation
description: Use when cluster-scale hydrostatic mass profiles and baryonic component profiles are available (e.g. X-COP products via hydromass) and you need g_bar(r) from baryonic components to compare against g_obs(r), as in a radial acceleration relation test.

name: baryonic-dark-matter-mass-decomposition
description: Use when hydrostatic mass profiles exist from X-ray (surface brightness + spectroscopic temperature) and SZ pressure data and the goal is radial gravitational-field contributions of baryons vs dark matter, e.g. stellar dominance radii or baryon fraction profiles out to R200.

name: baryonic-feature-identification-in-powerspectrum
description: Use when you have the learned symbolic expression artifact for plin_emulated() and need to demonstrate that individual correction terms carry physical meaning (turnover, spectral index, acoustic/damping, baryonic effects) rather than acting as a black-box fit.

name: baseline-output-file-verification
description: Use when you have just installed galkin and run galkin_data.py under the baseline (default) Galactic parameter setup, and need to check that the generated rotation-curve, positional and raw data files match the reference files shipped with the distribution.

name: baseline-reference-data-comparison
description: Use when galkin has just been installed or reconfigured and you need to verify that galkin_data.py with the default (baseline) Galactic parameters reproduces the reference rotation-curve and tracer position outputs shipped in the distribution.

name: baseline-source-coherency-reduction
description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing the RIME reduction pipeline in which per-antenna Jones terms (A[t,p,s,λ]) must be multiplied into per-baseline source coherencies and model visibilities, then reduced to a single χ² scalar for unit testing against a CPU numpy reference.

name: bayesian-accept-reject-sampling-configuration
description: Use when observed stellar and planetary parameters (e.g. mass, radius, period for small planets of 0.5–15 Earth masses) must be converted into internal-structure posteriors, or when benchmarking runtime across the A1–A3/B1–B3 prior options of plaNETic.

name: bayesian-credible-interval-coverage-analysis
description: Use when a Bayesian model (e.g. gallifrey's SMC-sampled GP posterior) yields parameter posteriors and you must confirm the credible intervals actually cover the true injected values before trusting downstream products like transmission spectra.

name: bayesian-eos-prior-reweighting
description: Use when a Bayesian EOS-inference pipeline (NMMA/bilby) must incorporate radio-timing pulsar mass measurements and NICER mass-radius posteriors as prior likelihoods over a precomputed EOS sample, each with an M-R curve and maximum mass M_TOV.

name: bayesian-evidence-estimation-stepping-stones
description: Use when comparing competing RV models (e.g. number of Keplerians, stellar-activity vs planetary signals) or testing whether ln Z is sensitive to prior choices — specifically when EMPEROR/reddemcee chains exist and evidence must be computed with 'Evidence' as the comparison criterion.

name: bayesian-evidence-model-comparison
description: Use when jointly fitting Keplerian signals to HARPS radial velocities and TESS plus ground-based transit photometry, and competing model variants (eccentric vs circular, drift, GP activity) must be compared by Bayesian evidence.

name: bayesian-evidence-thermodynamic-integration
description: Use when comparing nested radial-velocity orbit models (successive Keplerian counts in EMPEROR's autorun) and you need a Bayesian evidence criterion instead of BIC — e.g. when ln Z sensitivity to priors or tight posteriors matter.

name: bayesian-mcmc-inference-poisson-likelihood
description: Use when an X-ray spectrum (OGIP standard, e.g. an XMM-Newton PHA) needs fully Bayesian parameter estimation for a composite model, especially at low counts where C-stat is preferred over chi-square to avoid biased estimates.

name: bayesian-mcmc-multi-chain-sampling
description: Use when a Bayesian model over real parameter spaces needs MCMC sampling but choosing the scale/orientation of the jumping distribution is difficult, or when comparing DE-MC against WinBUGS-style single-site samplers on posterior percentile accuracy.

name: bayesian-mcmc-posterior-sampling
description: Use when a 1–3 parameter New Physics or cosmology model must be constrained by Bayesian posterior sampling against primordial abundances (Y_p, D/H) with Gaussian priors, and credible contours or upper bounds are the deliverable.

name: bayesian-mcmc-sed-fitting
description: Use when you need to fit multiwavelength (UV-to-millimetre) galaxy SEDs with physically motivated radiative transfer models via Bayesian MCMC, especially for ULIRGs or AGN-hosting galaxies, rather than empirical energy balance templates.

name: bayesian-mcmc-spectral-fitting
description: Use when an X-ray spectrum (OGIP-standard PHA loaded into an ObsConfiguration) must be fitted with a composite additive/multiplicative model and Bayesian posterior constraints (credible intervals, corner plots, PPC) are required rather than a simple -fit statistic.

name: bayesian-nested-sampling-eos-inference
description: Use when you need posterior EOS samples for dense neutron-star matter that fuse nuclear-physics EOS bands with model-based high-density extensions (e.g., pQCD constraints at ~40-50 n_sat), and you must sample the EOS parameter space with nested sampling.

name: bayesian-nested-sampling-inference
description: Use when a transient's photometry or spectrum needs model fitting with posterior samples — e.g. fitting SN2011kl with t0_supernova_extinction or a joint kilonova spectrum+photometry fit like AT2017gfo.

name: bayesian-nonlinear-mixed-effects-modeling
description: Use when a Bayesian nonlinear mixed-effects model has ~40+ parameters (e.g. l Ke, l Ka, l Cl, log(tau2_e/a/c), log(sigma2)) where one-dimensional Gibbs/WinBUGS updates are limited and block MCMC with adaptive jump scale and orientation is needed.

name: bayesian-posterior-sampling
description: Use when you have observed masses (0.5–15 M⊕) and radii plus stellar parameters for small exoplanets and need internal-structure posteriors under multiple water-abundance and Si/Mg/Fe ratio prior choices.

name: bayesian-transient-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting photometric (lightcurve) or spectroscopic observations of an explosive transient with a physical or semi-analytical model, and you need posterior samples and evidence rather than a simple chi-square fit.

name: bayesian-variance-component-posterior-analysis
description: Use when a Bayesian one-way random-effects (variance-component) model needs posterior percentile tabulation and cross-validation of an MCMC sampler against known analytic values or a WinBUGS reference.

name: bayesian-x-ray-spectral-fitting
description: Use when an X-ray spectrum in the OGIP standard (PHA with ARF/RMF responses) must be fitted with a composite spectral model under a fully Bayesian framework with priors over spectral parameters.

name: bbh-mass-distribution-extraction
description: Use when comparing BBH merger-rate yields or mass extremes across COMPAS model variants (e.g. Fiducial vs optimistic CE with surviving Hertzsprung-gap donors) at low metallicities such as Z=10% or 5% solar.

name: bbh-merger-rate-computation
description: Use when quantifying how a COMPAS model-parameter change (e.g. LBV mass-loss rate 1.5e-4 → 1e-3 Msun/yr, common-envelope alpha, or alpha_lambda) alters the total BBH merger rate or the count of specific sub-populations (e.g. LVT151012-like ~90 Msun total-mass mergers) at a given metallicity.

name: bbh-merger-rate-normalization-per-star-formation
description: Use when a COMPAS/STROOPWAFEL double-compact-object output must be expressed as BBHs merging in a Hubble time per 1e9 solar masses of star formation at a given metallicity, or when quantifying rate sensitivity to one varied parameter (e.g. alphalambda 0.1 vs 0.01).

name: bbn-abundance-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or extending Bayesian BBN constraints — e.g. placing credible bounds on NP modifications of weak n↔p conversion rates from primordial Y_p and D/H measurements via emcee sampling of a PRyMordial prediction pipeline.

name: bbn-light-element-abundance-computation
description: Use when the analysis requires predicted BBN mass fractions (Y_P, D/H, He-3, Li-7) as a function of cosmic baryon density eta_B, or a PDG-style abundance plot to compare against deuterium quasar observations and CMB baryon-density bands.

name: bbn-monte-carlo-parameter-inference
description: Use when the analysis goal is marginalizing BBN abundance posteriors over neutron lifetime, baryon density, and nuclear-rate uncertainties — e.g. comparing PRIMAT vs NACRE II rate compilations for the deuterium or lithium problems.

name: bbn-nuclear-network-integration
description: Use when the task requires predicting primordial light-element abundances from a BBN nuclear reaction network, or validating a BBN code's predictions against the PDG plot, quasar deuterium absorption, and CMB-inferred baryon abundance.

name: bbn-thermal-history-solver-configuration
description: Use when a cosmological analysis needs BBN light-element abundances and N_eff from a modified thermal history — e.g. scanning a new relativistic species X (scalar, vector, Majorana, Dirac) over a mass grid with energy exchange to the neutrino bath or electromagnetic plasma.

name: beam-dispersion-measure-parameterization
description: Use when you have SNR detections over an integrated dedispersed time-series for many beams and dispersion measures, and need to convert threshold-exceeding samples into per-candidate records with beam, DM, time, pulse width, and SNR.

name: beam-smearing-mock-observation-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic beam-smeared rotation curves from a galaxy mass model to test MCMC parameter recovery, benchmark against codes like dysmalpy, or create realistic mock data for high-z IFU-style observations.

name: beam-smearing-psf-convolution
description: Use when fitting 1D rotation curves of IFU-observed high-z disk galaxies where beam smearing degrades the observed velocity field, or when generating mock-observed rotation/dispersion curves from a parametric mass model at a given sky orientation and PSF.

name: benchmark-comparison-against-literature-values
description: Use when a newly implemented equilibrium or simulation model must be validated before production runs, and a published reference dataset (e.g. literature condensation temperatures) exists for identical input parameters.

name: benchmark-coupling-table-generation
description: Use when quantifying how RG running and dimension-6 operator mixing change spin-dependent DM-nucleon couplings or direct detection bounds for a vector-mediator simplified model at a chosen benchmark (mediator mass + high-energy couplings).

name: benchmark-result-tabulation
description: Use when comparing measured throughput of a scalar reference routine against an SSE2/AVX2-intrinsics vectorized variant (e.g. precision-reduction rounding of 32-bit integers), or when a speed-up factor must be tabulated and validated against a paper's hypothesis.

name: benchmark-table-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing a published compression benchmark table that compares specific lossless codecs (Rice/FITS, LZF, bitshuffle, GZIP) on synthetic integer arrays and requires cell-by-cell numerical validation.

name: benchmark-timing-data-extraction
description: Use when a paper reports a timing/benchmark table comparing implementations across problem sizes or precision settings, and the numbers must be extracted, structured, and validated against reported speedup figures.

name: bern-model-population-matching
description: Use when observed planetary parameters (radii, masses, periods) for a multi-planet system are available and the goal is to constrain formation history by finding analogues in a synthetic planet-formation population.

name: beta-king-profile-visibility-modelling
description: Use when a sky model requires beta-profile (King) sources in Montblanc's RIME evaluation and GPU-computed per-antenna terms and chi2 must be verified against a trusted CPU reference.

name: bic-based-model-selection
description: Use when fitting RV time series (or joint RV+astrometry) and the number of planetary signals is unknown — decide when to stop adding Keplerians using BIC_old - BIC_new > tolerance or Evidence ratios, without manual model comparison.

name: bin-free-stellar-kinematics-fitting
description: Use when mass-modeling a spherical equilibrium stellar system (dwarf galaxy, star cluster) from discrete tracer positions and individual LOS and/or PM velocities, where binning would discard information and you need the density slope at R1/2.

name: binary-black-hole-mass-ratio-sampling
description: Use when validating a gravitational-wave surrogate model over a parameter range: you need the magnitude of surrogate error (Eq. 31) for randomly drawn q in [1,2] and the q where the largest error occurs.

name: binary-black-hole-merger-rate-normalization
description: Use when comparing how COMPAS model assumptions (e.g. common-envelope survival of Hertzsprung-gap donors) change the number of merging BBHs at a fixed metallicity such as 10% or 5% solar, normalized per 1e9 solar masses of star formation.

name: binary-cross-entropy-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a two-class, per-timestep sequence classification problem (e.g. 2D spiral clockwise vs anticlockwise) must be solved by a neural CDE and its held-out test accuracy reported against a trained checkpoint.

name: binary-evolution-model-variation
description: Use when a BBH formation pathway claimed under a Fiducial COMPAS model needs robustness testing against an alternative prescription (e.g. supernova engine, CE treatment, alpha_lambda, f_LBV mass loss), with outputs compared pathway-by-pathway.

name: binary-file-identity-comparison
description: Use when a file has been converted to another serialization format and back (e.g. FITS through HDFITS), and you must prove whether data values survived exactly and whether the output is byte-identical.

name: binary-population-synthesis-simulation
description: Use when you need to simulate large populations of massive binary stars (Kroupa IMF, m1 up to 100 Msun) and predict compact-remnant merger outcomes as a function of metallicity (e.g. Z=0.002 and Z=0.001).

name: bit-depth-bounded-sampling
description: Use when building benchmark datasets to compare lossless compression ratios or I/O read speeds across file formats (FITS vs HDF5), and you need controlled bit-depth content ranges that are reproducible across runs.

name: bit-matrix-transpose-implementation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or interoperate with Bitshuffle's byte-level rearrangement of typed binary arrays — e.g. verifying an in-house transpose against github.com/kiyo-masui/bitshuffle before applying LZ4/ZSTD/LZF compression.

name: bitshuffle-compression-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify I/O speedups from switching large 3D (e.g. radio-astronomy) integer arrays from FITS to chunked or bitshuffle-compressed HDF5, especially for partial (slice) reads of a large cube.

name: bitshuffle-h5-filter-roundtrip-verification
description: Use when a typed, correlated binary dataset (e.g. radio-interferometry or float32/int arrays) must be stored losslessly in chunked HDF5 and you need to confirm the Bitshuffle+LZ4 filter pipeline round-trips exactly and actually shrinks on-disk storage.

name: black-hole-mass-ratio-statistics
description: Use when you have COMPAS population-synthesis DCO output at multiple metallicities plus observed BBH component masses, and you need median mass-ratio statistics or a formation-feasibility verdict per event.

name: black-hole-migration-torque-calculation
description: Use when you need radial torque profiles (isothermal + thermal) for an embedded BH migrator in a parametric 1D AGN disk model, e.g. a 50 Msun BH with q=5e-6 orbiting a 1e6 Msun central BH.

name: black-hole-progenitor-mass-tabulation
description: Use when you have COMPAS double compact object output (e.g. from the COMPAS Zenodo community) for a fiducial model and need to identify which progenitor binaries match observed GW event parameters and tabulate their initial total masses per metallicity.

name: blackbody-point-source-sphere-modeling
description: Use when reproducing analytic radiative transfer benchmark problems such as a spherical gas distribution with a central point source (e.g., 20 kpc helium sphere), where radial H/He ionization and temperature profiles against Cloudy are needed.

name: blackhole-accretion-parameter-configuration
description: Use when setting up a parametric 1D AGN disk profile in pagn: you must choose Mbh, epsilon, m, xi, Rin, Rout, Mdot_out, alpha, le, b, and the opacity scheme ('combined' or custom) before calling solve_disk.

name: blast-wave-initial-condition-configuration
description: Use when setting up 1D special relativistic shock-tube/blast-wave tests on the domain [0, 1] with a discontinuity at x = 0.5, needing Table 1 left/right states for L1-error convergence checks.

name: blender-cycles-physically-based-rendering
description: Use when synthetic, physically based images of a small solar system body (fly-by or orbiting scenarios) or terrestrial planet surface must be rendered from a 3-D model to support mission design, instrument characterisation, or computer-vision algorithm development such as SfM/MVS 3-D reconstruction.

name: blender-python-scripting
description: Use when a scientific imaging or rendering pipeline must be automated in Blender (mesh loading, procedural shader nodes, displacement, Cycles rendering) rather than done interactively, e.g. simulating images of small solar system bodies.

name: block-wise-metropolis-updating
description: Use when a multi-parameter Bayesian posterior (e.g. nonlinear mixed-effects models like the 43-parameter Theophylline model) mixes poorly under single-parameter Gibbs or one-dimensional updates such as those WinBUGS performs outside GLMs.

name: boiling-point-based-property-correlation
description: Use when you need to predict vapour pressures of tetraalkyl- or tetraalkenylstannanes at temperatures below the experimentally measured range, using only boiling points and hydrocarbon-based estimation methods.

name: boiling-point-data-availability-screening
description: Use when a dataset contains derived enthalpies of vaporization (e.g. from GC-measured vapour pressures) but boiling point coverage is partial, and you must identify which compounds qualify for ΔSvap derivation versus which must be excluded.

name: boltzmann-equation-integration-early-universe
description: Use when a cosmology or BBN analysis requires a first-principles thermal background (N_eff, Omega_nu(rel) h^2, T_gamma/T_nu evolution) with non-instantaneous neutrino decoupling, rather than an assumed instantaneous-decoupling snapshot.

name: boltzmann-level-population-summation
description: Use when you have an ExoMol (or similar) molecular line list with a states file of energy levels and total degeneracies, and need a temperature-resolved partition function table Q(T).

name: boltzmann-reference-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when a fast P(k) emulator or fitting formula must be benchmarked for accuracy against a Boltzmann solver, e.g. verifying the ~0.2% RMS fractional error over k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc at z=0.

name: boltzmann-solver-spectra-computation
description: Use when a w0waCDM/ΛCDM model with given cosmological parameters must be solved for the linear Einstein–Boltzmann equations to produce P(k) and CMB D_l spectra, especially when a CLASS cross-check or differentiable outputs are needed.

name: boosted-potential-binding-energy-evaluation
description: Use when every particle in a cosmological simulation snapshot must be labelled bound/unbound without overdensity thresholds, or when separating halo populations by phase-space distribution, virial ratio (2K/|U|), or density-profile extent.

name: boosted-potential-frame-computation
description: Use when you have a cosmological simulation particle snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) and need the gravitational potential in an accelerated reference frame to classify particles as bound or unbound, or to define haloes by potential-well topology.

name: bootstrap-resampling-error-analysis
description: Use when quantifying uncertainty on 2PCF (or other clustering) measurements from a galaxy catalogue without external mocks, via jackknife/bootstrap sub-region resampling in CosmoBolognaLib.

name: born-limit-phase-space-integration
description: Use when an ab-initio n<->p conversion-rate table for BBN freeze-out must be recomputed or validated beyond the Born approximation, e.g. regenerating PRyMordial's PRyM_evalnTOp rates.

name: bound-state-energy-validation-against-reference-output
description: Use when a BOUND run on an atom–rigid-rotor system must be validated against documented reference energies, e.g. after rebuilding an executable or changing BLAS/LAPACK libraries.

name: bow-shock-plasma-parameterization
description: Use when you must test whether a kinetic plasma model reproduces non-fluid shock physics at bow-shock-scale resolutions, e.g. comparing magnetic compression ratios and downstream ion distribution non-Maxwellianity across grid resolutions.

name: boxcar-baseline-smoothing-comparison
description: Use when smoothing noisy astronomical spectra (e.g. quasar spectra before cross-correlation redshifting) where preserving the position of broad emission features matters, or when deciding between an exponential-decay rolling filter and a boxcar baseline.

name: brown-conrady-radial-tangential-distortion-remapping
description: Use when a rendered or synthetic image must be degraded with realistic lens distortion before downstream computer-vision or 3-D reconstruction tasks, and camera intrinsics plus Brown–Conrady k/p coefficients are available.

name: brownian-motion-path-simulation
description: Use when a task requires generating stochastic Brownian-motion sample paths in JAX, or driving a neural SDE generator with a Brownian control (e.g. diffrax.UnsafeBrownianPath / diffrax.VirtualBrownianTree) to match a reference distribution.

name: browser-javascript-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify the client-side cost of a browser-based pixel operation (tile compositing, channel mixing, filtering) on scientific imagery and must exclude network fetch time from the measurement.

name: burn-in-determination-via-standard-error-comparison
description: Use when parallelised ensemble MCMC chains (e.g. emcee walkers or Metropolis-Hastings chains) must be checked for residual initialisation bias, and a defensible burn-in length must be derived rather than assumed.

name: c-cosmology-library-api-usage
description: Use when a task requires computing a cosmological quantity (e.g. fσ8 at z=1) by calling the cosmobl::Cosmology class from a compiled C++ program that dispatches to an external Boltzmann solver like CAMB.

name: c-header-annotation-generation
description: Use when building language bindings (e.g. Python/Octave) for a C library and you need to automatically enumerate and annotate every exported public constant, function, and class before SWIG's wrapper-generation pass.

name: c-header-parsing-with-swig-xml
description: Use when building language bindings (Python/Octave) for a C library and you need a machine-readable inventory of its public API symbols before writing wrapper or interface code.

name: c-library-unit-testing
description: Use when a C library's documented per-class rules (e.g. Mapping simplification in AST Section 3.1.3) must be empirically validated by constructing representative inputs and asserting the class or value of each result.

name: c-locator-struct-versioning
description: Use when a drop-in HDS replacement must interoperate with legacy HDSv4 files and new HDF5-backed HDS files, so public API calls on HDSLoc locators must be routed to the matching backend implementation.

name: c-test-library-compilation
description: Use when validating SWIG-generated wrappers of a C library: you need a compiled C test library (from SWIGTest.c + SWIGLALTest.h) whose classes and memory-ownership behavior can be instantiated from Python or Octave.

name: calinski-harabasz-index-computation
description: Use when a hierarchical clustering hierarchy (e.g. built on correlation distance d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)|) must be cut at a data-driven number of clusters rather than a user-specified k.

name: calinski-harabasz-optimal-cluster-selection
description: Use when a hierarchical clustering of variables has been built from a correlation distance and you need a data-driven, a-priori-free choice of how many clusters to report and color-code.

name: camb-transfer-function-generation
description: Use when a halo-mass-function or power-spectrum calculation needs a linear CDM transfer function T(k) from CAMB, or when a warm-DM transfer function must be derived by filtering T_CDM(k) with the Bode et al. (2001) form.

name: camera-sensor-noise-modeling
description: Use when rendered space-scene images (e.g. Blender/Cycles renders of the 25143 Itokawa model) must be degraded with realistic lens and sensor artifacts to characterise imaging-instrument performance or validate computer-vision navigation algorithms.

name: carbon-oxygen-ratio-computation
description: Use when interpreting or predicting a giant planet's atmospheric C/O ratio as a tracer of its heavy-element accretion pathway (dust grains vs planetesimals), e.g. when comparing SimAb run_sum(n).txt outputs or planning paired formation scenarios.

name: carmenes-dr1-spectral-data-handling
description: Use when reduced CARMENES VIS/NIR FITS spectra (e.g. car*vis_A.fits from the DR1 GTO sample) must be converted into per-spectrum radial velocities and activity-indicator time series via cross-correlation with a weighted binary mask.

name: casa-command-script-generation
description: Use when a Python pipeline must drive NRAO CASA subroutines non-interactively — e.g. converting a UVFITS input to a measurement set and producing dirty images as part of automated radio-synthesis imaging.

name: casa-subroutine-scripting
description: Use when a Python pipeline must execute CASA subroutines (e.g. Clean for image synthesis) on pre-calibrated multi-epoch radio-synthesis measurement sets without manual interaction with the CASA environment.

name: cascade-decay-monte-carlo-sampling
description: Use when a dark matter model annihilates into a multitude of final states and continuum gamma-ray yields dN/dE per final state are needed on log-spaced photon energy bins.

name: case-a-case-b-recombination-comparison
description: Use when comparing analytic radiative-transfer solutions for a semi-infinite slab (e.g. overdensity Δ=1800, L=4.61 kpc at z=3.0) where you must quantify how case-A/case-B recombination, temperature evolution, and spectral shape affect N_HI and N_HeI.

name: case-b-recombination-atomic-level-population-modelling
description: Use when you need hydrogen recombination line emissivities or excited-state (n, l) level population densities for a gas with known electron/proton/neutral-H densities and temperature, e.g. H ii nebula conditions like ne=100 cm^-3, T=1e4 K.

name: case-b-recombination-cascade-rate-balance
description: Use when you need hydrogen excited-state level population densities or recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha n=3->2) for photoionised gas with known ne, nHI, nHII, and temperature, under Case B assumptions.

name: catastrophic-error-definition-application
description: Use when predicted photometric redshifts must be scored against spectroscopic redshifts using the outlier fraction metric reported in the GLM photo-z article, e.g. benchmarking gamma-family GLM fits on PHAT0 or SDSS DR10 against codes like Le PHARE, BPZ, ANNz, TPZ, or BMA.

name: catastrophic-outlier-rate-evaluation
description: Use when a fitted photo-z model (e.g., gamma-family GLM with log link on PC projections) must be scored by its catastrophic outlier fraction on a test set with spectroscopic redshifts, or when comparing model variants (number of PCs, training-set size) by outlier rate.

name: celestial-coordinate-frame-conversion
description: Use when a task needs to transform astronomical positions between celestial frames — e.g. converting ICRS (RA,Dec) coordinates to Galactic (l,b) — via the Starlink AST Python bindings.

name: center-of-mass-boundary-branch-pruning
description: Use when traversing a distributed SPH/FMM octree where remote-node fetches dominate: particle positions are inserted into a parallel octree, and branches with a center of mass far from the local domain boundary should be skipped during traversal.

name: cfl-adaptive-timestepping
description: Use when an explicit spectral PDE simulation (Dedalus, Fourier periodic domain) develops sharp gradients or shocks that would blow up a fixed timestep, and a CFL-restricted adaptive dt is needed — e.g., the Orszag-Tang vortex MHD test run to t=0.5.

name: chain-mesh-pair-counting
description: Use when measuring angle-averaged two-point or three-point correlation functions from galaxy/simulated halo catalogues and their random catalogues in configuration space, and you need optimised parallel pair/triplet counting.

name: chain-mesh-spatial-indexing
description: Use when a catalogue of extragalactic objects must be searched for neighbours within a separation range to count pairs/triplets for 2PCF/3PCF estimation, and a brute-force O(N^2) scan is too slow.

name: chain-regressor-ensemble-modeling
description: Use when a tabular astronomical catalog (e.g. SDSS+WISE photometry) lacks redshifts but the classification pipeline benefits from redshift as a feature; the photo-z must be estimated prior to classification.

name: chain-rule-jacobian-transformation-hyperbolic-systems
description: Use when evolving a coupled hyperbolic conservative system ∂q/∂t + ∂f/∂x = 0 where inverting q→u analytically (or via a polynomial root-find per cell per step) is expensive, and a direct primitive-variable update is acceptable.

name: chandra-instrument-response-convolution
description: Use when generating spectra from a physical model (e.g. APEC or power-law) as a training set for a learned spectral surrogate like an IAE, and the target data were observed with Chandra so the surrogate must operate in instrumental counts space.

name: chandra-observation-background-subtraction
description: Use when building an X-ray spectral data cube from one or more Chandra ACIS observations (e.g. merged ObsIDs of a supernova remnant) and a background spectrum must be estimated to separate instrumental/sky background from source emission before spectral fitting or unmixing.

name: chandra-xray-data-processing
description: Use when Chandra ACIS observation(s) must be turned into a spatial–spectral cube (e.g. 3.0–8.48 keV band covering continuum and Fe-K) for component separation or parameter mapping.

name: chebyshev-spectral-discretization
description: Use when discretizing a 1D PDE on [-1, 1] with a Chebyshev T_n expansion and banded Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions, and you need a sparse, banded pencil matrix assembled stage-by-stage (tau rows, recombination, mode interleaving) rather than a dense Chebyshev collocation matrix.

name: chemical-equilibrium-simulation-parameterisation
description: Use when condensation temperatures (Tc) or molecule/element abundance-vs-temperature curves must be derived from a Gibbs free energy minimisation under a defined temperature grid, total pressure (e.g. 1e-4 bar), and stellar elemental abundance pattern.

name: chirp-mass-and-mass-ratio-computation
description: Use when a binary-coalescence dataset has component masses (m1, m2) but lacks the LIGO-comparable derived quantities chirp mass and mass ratio needed for event-selection filtering.

name: chord-diagram-correlation-layout
description: Use when a tabular dataset (CSV/TXT with named columns, NA for missing) has been correlated (Pearson, Spearman, or MIC) and pairwise variable relationships need a circular visual diagnostic.

name: chromatic-psf-fitting-minimization
description: Use when extracting a transient point source from an integral-field spectrograph (e.g. SEDm) data cube whose host galaxy morphology and background models must have their spatial/chromatic shapes fixed prior to a linear 3D amplitude reconstruction.

name: chromatographic-retention-time-correction
description: Use when isothermal capillary-GC retention times (e.g. 40-120°C in 20°C increments on SE-30) must be dead-time corrected, replicate-averaged, and regressed against 1/T to derive enthalpies/entropies of vaporization.

name: chromatographic-retention-time-replicate-averaging
description: Use when capillary GC retention times for reference/relative vapour pressure determination (e.g. tetraorganostannanes on an SE-30 column, 40–120°C) are collected as multiple replicate runs and must be averaged and hold-up corrected.

name: chronological-collision-list-maintenance
description: Use when simulating a Keplerian N-body system (e.g. a Solar-System-like configuration with bodies on Keplerian orbits about a central mass) where collisions are rare, and collision times per pair can be computed analytically via the continued-fraction grid-point solution.

name: chunked-storage-io-profiling
description: Use when profiling storage I/O of chunked HDF5 visibility datasets under a rounding-only (precision-reduction, no lossless compression) condition, or when validating single-core compression/decompression throughput against the paper's Table 2 numbers.

name: cigale-sed-grid-fitting
description: Use when you need to turn pre-transient broadband host-galaxy images (e.g. PS1 grizy cutouts) into a spectrally resolved galaxy cube, or when fitting per-pixel SEDs on a fixed parameter grid with an external redshift prior.

name: circumsecondary-disc-transit-modelling
description: Use when a transit light curve (e.g. J1407 SuperWASP photometry or PDS 110 eclipse photometry) is attributed to a circumsecondary disc and you need to reduce the parameter space of possible disc geometries before detailed fitting.

name: clausius-clapeyron-vapour-pressure-regression
description: Use when you have a compound's vapour pressure measured at multiple isothermal temperatures (e.g. 40-120°C in 20°C increments) and need the derived enthalpy of vaporization from the log P vs 1/T slope.

name: clean-bias-mitigation-iterative-thresholding
description: Use when producing cleaned images from pre-calibrated multi-epoch radio-synthesis measurement sets and you need a defensible, data-driven Clean stopping threshold instead of a fixed flux cutoff, to avoid Clean-bias.

name: client-server-task-dispatching
description: Reference for implementing or debugging websocket-based task dispatch in the Toyz web application: routing send_task messages to per-session subprocesses, persisting variables across sequential tasks, and isolating session state from the web layer.

name: client-side-web-image-rendering
description: Use when a client must render hill-shaded relief from a 32-bit DEM height channel (stored as a 1-channel TIFF in an IIPImage multi-resolution pyramid) and the light-source incidence angle must be user-adjustable in real time.

name: closed-form-analytic-solution-verification
description: Use when implementing a new equilibrium solver (e.g. Solve_CE) and a closed-form expression exists (Eqs. 19-20) that lets you validate outputs at sample (T, nH, nHe) points before trusting the iterative code.

name: closed-loop-gnc-simulation-timing
description: Use when estimating whether SISPO's non-photorealistic OpenGL rendering path can support closed-loop GNC or visual-navigation studies within a practical wall-clock budget, as opposed to the Cycles path-tracer.

name: cloud-condensation-thermodynamic-equilibrium-simulation
description: Use when you need to predict the compositional and vertical structure of condensation clouds in a 1D planetary atmosphere for a given bulk elemental composition, especially for hot-Jupiter, sub-Neptune, or self-luminous planet retrieval contexts.

name: cloud-particle-optical-property-modeling
description: Use when a transmission/emission spectrum must be generated from a converged cloud-atmosphere profile and checked for the 8–10 μm MgSiO3/Mg2SiO4 absorption feature, or when cloud particle composition is to be constrained from a mid-infrared spectral feature.

name: cloudy-reference-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when an analytic radiative-transfer code's ionization or temperature profiles must be validated against a published Cloudy benchmark case (e.g. a 1e5 K blackbody, case A recombination, evolving-temperature sphere) with quantitative agreement thresholds.

name: cloudy-reference-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when validating a hydrogen emission-line model against Cloudy: compute Balmer (nupper=2), Paschen (nupper=3), and Brackett (nupper=4) emissivities and check each series stays within 1 per cent of reference values.

name: cluster-baryon-fraction-cosmic-value-comparison
description: Use when a cluster sample has joint X-ray (surface brightness, spectroscopic temperature) and SZ pressure profiles plus a hydrostatic mass reconstruction, and the goal is to evaluate the baryon fraction profile against the cosmic value at R200.

name: cluster-gravitational-acceleration-decomposition
description: Use when testing whether the spiral-galaxy radial acceleration relation extends to galaxy-cluster scale: you have X-ray/SZ cluster data, hydrostatic mass profile reconstructions, and need log(g_obs) vs log(g_bar) comparison against the RAR.

name: cluster-profile-shape-diversity-analysis
description: Use when you have recovered (nonparametric) mass profiles for multiple clusters and need to test whether a parametric NFW model exhausts their shape variation, e.g. residual analysis over the X-COP 12-cluster sample.

name: cluster-validity-diagnostic-reproduction
description: Use when a hierarchical clustering of catalog variables (correlation distance d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)|) must be cut and an objective, data-driven number of clusters is needed.

name: cmb-baryon-density-constraint-comparison
description: Use when predicted BBN light-element abundances are available across a grid of eta_B values and you need to check consistency with the CMB-inferred baryon density and quasar absorption deuterium observations.

name: cmb-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when comparing theoretical predictions (spectral observables) of single-field inflationary models against publicly available Planck CMB likelihood data to compute per-model likelihoods and Bayesian evidences.

name: cmb-likelihood-module-integration
description: Reference for plugging cosmological core/likelihood modules (e.g. CambCoreModule, WmapLikelihoodModule) into CosmoHammer's chain when building MCMC parameter-estimation configurations over CMB data.

name: cmb-map-fits-data-handling
description: Use when the input is a HEALPix FITS sky map from a CMB polarimeter (I, Q, U at Nside 512) and the goal is to extract, inspect, or cut out regions (e.g. 5-degree patches around Tau A) for photometry or comparison.

name: cmb-mapmaking-destriping
description: Use when a CMB polarimeter timestream (e.g. HDF5 with TIME/PHI/THETA/PSI/FLAG/TEMP/Q/U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise with knee frequency below the scan rate and you need a destriped I/Q sky map with minimal signal impact.

name: cmb-polarimeter-baseline-solving
description: Use when polarimeter timestream data (e.g. HDF5 files with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, Q, U columns) contains correlated 1/f noise to be removed via Maximum Likelihood destriping and the baseline amplitudes must be solved for.

name: cmb-power-spectrum-band-binning
description: Use when designing or re-binning a CMB power spectrum likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G TT/TE/EE or a mock data set in .yaml form) and you need to choose the band power bin width that minimises parameter sigma errors via Fisher forecasts.

name: cmb-power-spectrum-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when a CMB TT/TE/EE, BB, lensing (phiphi, kappakappa) likelihood must be evaluated (or differentiated) at a set of cosmological and nuisance parameters, e.g. Planck/SPT/ACT band-power data with .yaml likelihood files.

name: cmb-spectrum-computation
description: Use when you need linear CMB angular power spectra (TT/EE/TE D_l) from a cosmological model, especially when the spectra must be differentiable (ForwardDiff) or compared against CLASS/established Boltzmann codes.

name: cmb-timestream-destriping
description: Use when a polarimeter timestream (HDF5 with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise below the scan rate that must be removed before map-making, e.g. for B-Machine 37.5 GHz or LATTE-like data.

name: cmb-timestream-simulation
description: Use when validating a destriping pipeline with simulated polarimeter timelines: a signal-only timestream from a known input map, and a signal-plus-noise timestream with white variance and 1/f knee/slope from measured detector noise properties.

name: cmb-white-noise-variance-prediction
description: Use when validating a destriped single-dish polarimeter map (e.g. B-Machine 37.5 GHz Q/U HEALPix maps): the measured spectrum must match the predicted white-noise variance so that excess power reveals residual correlated noise.

name: cme-coronal-deflection-rotation-simulation
description: Use when a study needs the coronal trajectory of one or more CMEs — final latitude, longitude, and tilt plus profiles vs. distance — from a magnetogram-derived PFSS background, with optional ensemble uncertainty quantification.

name: cme-deflection-validation-against-observations
description: Use when validating that ForeCAT reproduces known coronal deflection/rotation behavior for specific CMEs — e.g., a near-radial CME should stay within ~0.5° of its seed latitude/longitude/tilt, while a deflecting CME shows multi-degree latitudinal and longitudinal displacement.

name: cme-ensemble-impact-projection
description: Use when an OSPREI ensemble run (nRuns > 1 with a .ens file) needs to be turned into latitude–longitude contour maps of impact probability and CME properties at a satellite, and when interpreting why the nonzero-impact region deviates from a rounded rectangle.

name: cme-footprint-geometry-interpretation
description: Use when a latitude–longitude contour map of ensemble CME impact percentage shows a distorted (non–rounded-rectangle) nonzero-impact region and you need to attribute the distortion to ensemble spread in CME position, orientation, size, or shape at impact.

name: cme-insitu-profile-simulation
description: Use when you need predicted in situ profiles (B, Bz, velocity, Kp) at a spacecraft for a CME ensemble, not just an arrival time — e.g., reproducing geomagnetic-storm-relevant properties like max B and peak Kp within the sheath.

name: cme-interplanetary-propagation-simulation
description: Use when you have a ForeCAT far-corona terminal CME state (latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) and need to propagate it through interplanetary space to predict arrival time, speed, size, and internal magnetic/thermal properties at a satellite.

name: cme-parameter-source-attribution
description: Use when configuring OSPREI (or similar CME forecast-model) input files for specific CME events and you must document where every parameter value comes from — e.g., building a labeled parameter table from DONKI CMEAnalysis entries, GCS reconstructions, OMNI solar wind, and EUV imagery.
tools: OSPREI (Open Solar Physics Rapid Ensemble Information)

name: cme-profile-histogram-visualization
description: Use when OSPREI (ForeCAT/ANTEATR-PARADE/FIDO) runs have completed and standardized output files exist, and you need histograms of ensemble profile quantities or distance profiles, e.g., arrival-time/duration/density/B distributions.

name: cme-trajectory-profile-visualization
description: Use when OSPREI (or a ForeCAT/ANTEATR/FIDO ensemble or single run) has produced standardized output data files and you need automated, forecast-ready figures of CME trajectories, parameter profiles, histograms, and ensemble statistics.

name: cme-trajectory-sensitivity-interpretation
description: Use when OSPREI ensemble output files (from '.ens'-configured runs, e.g., the 22 April and 09 May 2021 CMEs) need input-output correlation analysis to reveal which parameter uncertainties drive forecast outputs like arrival time, speed, and in situ properties.

name: co-depletion-correction-analysis
description: Use when comparing modelled 12CO line fluxes with ALMA disc-survey flux/size samples and you must test whether CO depletion from initial conditions reconciles models with observations.

name: co-depletion-modelling
description: Use when comparing semi-analytical 12CO flux model predictions to ALMA survey observations (e.g. Upper Sco or Lupus fluxes and CO-disc radii) and model–data mismatch suggests volatiles are depleted; also when quantifying how CO depletion shifts model tracks in the flux–size plane.

name: co-flux-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a fast semi-analytical CO flux model must be validated against thermochemical reference fluxes, and you have paired model outputs on matching disc structural parameters plus a paper-stated tolerance (factor of three).

name: co-flux-semi-analytical-modelling
description: Use when comparing disc evolution models (viscous vs MHD-wind) against ALMA 12CO flux observations of disc populations (e.g. Lupus, Upper Sco) and synthesising population-level CO fluxes cheaply.

name: co-ratio-abundance-analysis
description: Use when you have SimAb run outputs (run_sum(n).txt files with [(x/H) of the planet]/[(X/H) of the sun]) and need to classify subsolar vs supersolar metallicity and compute C/O ratios to trace the source of heavy elements.

name: collisional-excitation-rate-inclusion
description: Use when reconstructing HyLight Case B hydrogen level-population solvers or line emissivities for photoionised nebular gas where collisional excitation from the ground state must enter the rate-equation system (ne up to ~1e2 cm**(-3), T ~1e4 K).

name: collisionless-shock-initialization
description: Use when you need to reproduce a 1D collisionless-shock discretisation study with Vlasiator, e.g. to check whether a hybrid-Vlasov model departs from fluid (MHD) theory at coarse resolutions like ~1000 km.

name: column-density-ratio-verification
description: Use when replicating or validating the five-model Slab2Bgnd study with Slab2Bgnd, or when any rabacus slab calculation must be checked against published column-density ratio benchmarks (e.g. grey/polychromatic N_HI ≈ 1.8, evoT/fixT ≈ 11).

name: common-envelope-efficiency-parameter-variation
description: Use when assessing sensitivity of COMPAS-predicted BBH merger rates (total and per-event analogs like GW150914, GW151226, LVT151012) to the common-envelope parameter alpha_lambda at Z=0.002 and Z=0.001.

name: common-envelope-parameter-configuration
description: Use when running COMPAS (or similar BSE-derived) binary population synthesis at fixed metallicity (e.g. Z=0.002 and Z=0.001) and you must set or vary the common-envelope prescription (alpha_lambda) to test its impact on double-compact-object yields and BBH merger rates.

name: common-envelope-survival-model-comparison
description: Use when comparing COMPAS population-synthesis runs that differ only in CE survival treatment (pessimistic vs optimistic, HG donors surviving) to quantify the effect on merging-BBH counts per 1e9 solar masses of star formation at specific metallicities.

name: compact-object-merger-time-evaluation
description: Use when a COMPAS (or BSE-style) population synthesis run has produced double compact objects with component masses and separations, and you must compute GW merger times and select merging BBHs within a Hubble time.

name: compas-output-data-handling
description: Use when the task requires extracting progenitor binary properties (e.g. ZAMS total mass m1+m2) from COMPAS population-synthesis output files by filtering systems that merge within a Hubble time and match the 90% credible intervals of a specific GW event.

name: compas-population-synthesis-configuration
description: Use when running population synthesis with COMPAS to evolve massive stellar binaries into double compact objects, or when testing whether an alternative physics prescription (e.g. supernova engine) changes evolutionary pathways for heavy BBH mergers.

name: complex-valued-output-parsing
description: Use when a solver's step output (e.g. oscode's 'output.txt') stores numerical solution steps as complex-valued pairs on a time grid and downstream plotting or comparison needs real arrays of times and solution values.

name: compound-mapping-construction
description: Use when stacked coordinate transformations must be reduced or merged — e.g. a Mapping compounded with its own inverse, embedded UnitMaps, series/parallel MatrixMaps, or adjacent ShiftMaps — and the resulting simplified Mapping class must be verified.

name: compressible-euler-equation-discretization
description: Use when a stationary 2-D gas flow in a galactic potential with a rotating weak bar must be computed by discretizing the compressible isothermal Euler equations, or when reproducing the galax2d solver behavior.

name: compressible-flow-steady-state-validation
description: Use when a task requires confirming that the galax2d time-dependent solver relaxes to a stationary gas-dynamic solution, or when reproducing runs under a modified parameter set from g2myparms.m instead of the default.

name: compression-ratio-comparison-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a new error-bounded lossy compressor on solar EUV imaging data (FITS from Solar Orbiter EUI FSI/HRI_EUV) and you need compression-ratio comparisons versus baseline compressors under identical error bounds.

name: compression-ratio-measurement-from-storage-size
description: Use when a chunked HDF5 dataset has been written through an HDF5 filter (e.g. Bitshuffle filter 32008 with LZ4) and you need to report how much on-disk space the filtered data occupies relative to the raw typed array.

name: compression-ratio-throughput-measurement
description: Decision support for choosing a lossless compression filter when storing large typed binary arrays (e.g. FITS images or HDF5 datasets), where both compression ratio and compression throughput matter.

name: compression-ratio-timing-analysis
description: Use when you need to decide which lossless codec (Rice, LZF, bitshuffle) to store large binary-table or array data in, and require reproducible compression-ratio and timing numbers per file-codec combination.

name: computational-stage-separation
description: Use when a cosmological model is specified as one symbolic equation system (metric, gravity, recombination, baryons, photons, CDM, neutrinos, dark energy) and must be decomposed into computational stages with analytical sparse Jacobians for implicit stiff ODE integration.

name: concentration-scatter-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have per-cluster posterior samples of parametric mass-model parameters (c200, M200) and need population-level statistics (mean concentration, scatter) and deviation thresholds to validate a mass model.

name: concurrent-request-latency-measurement
description: Use when estimating server capacity for tile-based image streaming: you need to measure requests-per-second and latency as concurrent 256×256 tile requests scale up on a multi-core server.

name: condensation-curve-smoothing
description: Use when raw ECCOplanets equilibrium condensation output (element/molecule abundances vs temperature, 2000-300 K) shows numerical glitches or jagged curves that must be cleaned before extracting 50% condensation temperatures or ∆Tc trends.
