name: condensation-sequence-simulation
description: Use when you need equilibrium condensation sequences or 50% condensation temperatures (Tc) of rock-forming elements (Al, Ti, Ca, Mg, Fe, Si) for a given stellar abundance pattern and disk pressure, e.g. reproducing Table 2 benchmarks at p = 1e-4 bar.

name: condensation-temperature-derivation
description: Use when a T-p-dependent condensation simulation (Gibbs minimisation over gas + pure-condensate species) has been run for a stellar abundance pattern at a fixed pressure (e.g. 1e-4 bar) and you need to extract and validate per-element condensation temperatures against literature benchmarks.

name: condensation-temperature-extraction
description: Use when you have run (or need to run) an ECCOplanets equilibrium condensation simulation and must convert element/molecule abundance-vs-temperature curves into per-element 50% condensation temperatures for validation or composition analysis.

name: condensation-temperature-pressure-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you need to determine how equilibrium condensation temperatures of rock-forming elements depend on disk pressure (e.g. testing whether element volatility defined at Solar System pressure applies to other disks), or to reproduce a ∆Tc vs. pressure sensitivity table.

name: condensation-temperature-simulation
description: Use when you need condensation temperatures (Tc) of planet-building elements for a stellar abundance pattern, or when quantifying how ∆Tc responds to varying disk pressure, metallicity, or element ratios like C/O from 0.1 to 0.7.

name: confidence-level-exclusion-region-derivation
description: Use when Fermi-LAT spectral data of a blazar sightline (e.g. NGC 1275, PKS 2155-304) must be scanned over (ma, gaγ) to build a confidence-level exclusion region for axion-like particle couplings.

name: confidence-limit-curve-reproduction
description: Use when null-result direct detection data (e.g. argon/xenon ionization searches) must be converted into per-operator, per-mass exclusion limit curves on DM-electron coupling strength, given pre-computed atomic response tables.

name: conservative-variable-flux-formulation
description: Use when solving hyperbolic conservative systems (e.g. 1D SRHD) with shock-capturing schemes, where the spatial flux term must remain in conservative form while variables are evolved in primitive form.

name: contaminant-source-transit-attribution
description: Use when a TESS target shows a transit and/or activity signal and you must decide, from TESS photometry alone, which nearby Gaia contaminant stars inside the aperture can or cannot be the origin of the signal.

name: continued-fraction-period-ratio-analysis
description: Use when two or more bodies follow Keplerian orbits around a central mass with intersecting orbits, and you need analytic soonest-collision times or a fast collision-detection schedule rather than brute-force time stepping.

name: continuous-time-gru-vector-field-implementation
description: Use when you need to show a discrete recurrent network (GRU) is the Euler discretisation of a continuous-time ODE system, or to inspect the -h(t) exponential-decay term governing hidden-state dynamics.

name: convergence-criterion-tuning-for-iterative-imaging
description: Use when automating radio-synthesis imaging (e.g. chimenea/CASA Clean) and you must decide when iterative re-Cleaning has converged, since estimating an RMS threshold requires an image to sample.

name: convergence-curve-figure-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking MCMC statistical error epsilon as a function of walker count L, sequential steps n, burn-in b, and autocorrelation time tau from Table 2 of a sampling study.

name: coordinate-frame-attribute-restoration-testing
description: Use when validating that a FrameSet-as-Mapping still generates correct coordinate values after mutating the current Frame's attributes, and when checking whether integrity restoration is triggered versus bypassed.

name: coordinate-frame-identity-verification
description: Use when a FITS header buffer contains WCS cards (CTYPE/CRVAL/CRPIX-type) that must be read into an AST FrameSet, and the pixel-vs-world coordinate frame identity of the base and current Frames must be confirmed.

name: core-mantle-thickness-constraint-analysis
description: Use when you have an ExoMDN-trained interior inference setup (mass, radius, equilibrium temperature) plus a candidate additional observable like fluid Love number k2 with a known measurement uncertainty, and you want to quantify the resulting constraint on layer thicknesses.

name: core-mass-parameter-sweep
description: Use when a SimAb-based study needs to isolate the effect of one initial condition (e.g., initial core mass) on final atmospheric C/O ratio and metallicity, keeping all other initial conditions fixed at paper values.

name: corner-plot-posterior-comparison
description: Use when you have two or more completed jaxspec Bayesian fits (MCMCFitter results with posterior samples) and need a visual, side-by-side comparison of their posterior parameter distributions, such as comparing background-handling models on the same observation.

name: correlated-noise-simulation-1f
description: Use when you need a signal-plus-correlated-noise simulated polarimeter timestream (e.g. LATTE-scale, ~half billion samples) to test a destriping/map-making pipeline before real instrument data exist.

name: correlation-cutoff-panel-selection
description: Use when analyzing OSPREI ensemble runs (e.g., the 22 April and 09 May 2021 CMEs) to identify which varied input parameters correlate with which quantifiable outputs above a 0.5 cutoff.

name: correlation-distance-matrix-analysis
description: Use when a tabular astronomical catalog (CSV/TXT with named columns) must be explored by clustering its variables, and similarity should be the AMADA correlation distance d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)| feeding an agglomerative hierarchy with a Calinski-Harabasz-guided cluster count.

name: correlation-function-tabulation
description: Use when you have an input galaxy dataset (positions on the sky) and need to produce the 2-pt angular correlation function w(theta) as a tabulated table of angular separations vs. correlation values.

name: correlation-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you need a pairwise association overview (variable-by-variable correlation structure) of a high-dimensional dataset of named numeric columns, with clustering-based ordering and optional dendrograms.

name: correlation-matrix-computation
description: Use when exploring pairwise relationships among numeric columns of a tabular astronomical catalog (CSV/TXT with named, space-separated columns) before clustering variables or running PCA, especially with possible NA entries.

name: correlation-matrix-eigendecomposition
description: Use when a named-column CSV/TXT table of high-dimensional astronomical data (e.g. galaxy catalog properties) needs dimensionality reduction into uncorrelated PCs, with PC scores and variable loadings extracted.

name: correlation-network-graph-layout
description: Use when you have a parameter-by-parameter correlation matrix (Pearson, Spearman, or MIC) for a multidimensional dataset and want to inspect variable association structure as a weighted network graph.

name: cosmic-ray-detection-and-replacement
description: Use when input is an AAOmega-format (or Marz-format) FITS spectrum with flux and variance extensions that needs cleaning — NaN/negative/over-threshold flux pixels, negative-variance pixels, or >30 sigma cosmic-ray spikes — prior to redshift cross-correlation.

name: cosmological-boltzmann-solver-benchmarking
description: Use when measuring wall-clock performance or thread scaling of a cosmological Boltzmann solver run (e.g. SymBoltz integrating many k-modes), or when validating that an approximation-free implementation achieves performance comparable to approximation-based codes.

name: cosmological-catalogue-pair-counting
description: Use when measuring two-point or three-point correlation functions from real or simulated extragalactic catalogues, where naive O(N^2) pair/triplet enumeration over all objects is prohibitively slow.

name: cosmological-growth-rate-evaluation
description: Use when the goal is a numerical value of the linear growth rate fσ8 at a specific redshift under a specified cosmology, and an external Boltzmann solver (CAMB) may be used as the computation backend.

name: cosmological-n-body-simulation-execution
description: Reference for running particle-based large-scale-structure simulations (e.g. N=1024^3 particles in 2048/1024/512/256 Mpc/h boxes) when output must be validated against GADGET-2 to sub-per-mille/1% accuracy.

name: cosmological-parameter-configuration
description: Use when a CBL modelling task requires a non-default cosmology: the example constructors apply Planck-like defaults, but mass function, bias, growth-rate (fσ8) or 2PCF computations need explicitly set parameters.

name: cosmological-parameter-configuration
description: Use when a cosmological analysis requires setting up a Boltzmann-solver model with explicit cosmological parameters (H0, Ωm, Ωb, w0, wa, c_s^2, lmax, reionization) that must be reproduced identically across two codes.

name: cosmological-parameter-configuration-for-hmf
description: Use when setting up or varying the cosmology (Omega_c, Omega_Lambda, sigma_8, spectral index, transfer function source, growth factor) underlying an hmf/HMFcalc halo mass function calculation.

name: cosmological-parameter-error-propagation
description: Use when a Fisher-forecast-style error budget is needed for CMB or lensing power-spectrum data (e.g. SPT-3G TT/TE/EE, ACT phi-phi) at a fixed fiducial cosmology, and exact derivatives are preferred over finite differences.

name: cosmological-parameter-grid-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking speed or accuracy of cosmological emulators (e.g. symbolic_pofk plin_emulated() vs CAMB vs BACCO) — identical cosmology/k grids are required for fair per-point ratio computation.

name: cosmological-parameter-interpretation
description: Use when a learned symbolic expression for the linear matter power spectrum (or similar emulator formula) needs each subterm annotated with its physical role and cosmological-parameter dependence, e.g. to show interpretability beyond black-box fitting.

name: cosmological-parameter-log-derivative-analysis
description: Use when exact derivatives of power spectra or CMB spectra with respect to cosmological parameters are needed for Fisher forecasting, gradient-based MCMC, emulator training, or sensitivity analyses, and when AD Jacobians must be validated against an established Boltzmann solver.

name: cosmological-parameter-mcmc-sampling
description: Use when a task requires setting up or benchmarking MCMC posterior sampling of cosmological parameters (H0, Omega_b, Omega_cdm, tau, n_s, logA, sigma8) from CMB likelihoods, or when reproducing autocorrelation times, burn-in lengths, or epsilon-convergence comparisons between ensemble and.

name: cosmological-parameter-sampler-setup
description: Use when you need to sample a posterior over cosmological parameters (e.g. 6 WMAP-constrained CMB parameters) with emcee/CosmoHammer, requiring explicit parameter bounds, walker counts, burn-in/sample iterations, and chain module wiring.

name: cosmological-parameter-sensitivity-benchmarking
description: Use when you need exact derivatives of cosmological observables (power spectra P(k), CMB D_l) with respect to parameters like h, Ωc0, Ωb0, YHe for Fisher forecasting, gradient-based MCMC, or AD runtime benchmarking.

name: cosmological-simulation-merger-tree-analysis
description: Use when you have halo merger tree catalogs (e.g., from TNG or gravity-only simulations) and need to model, fit, or evaluate individual halo mass accretion histories log(Mhalo) vs. cosmic time.

name: cosmological-simulation-parameter-reproduction
description: Reference for reproducing a published cosmological simulation (e.g. the 512 Mpc/h, N=1024^3 CONCEPT 1.0 vs GADGET-4 comparison) when the goal is to recreate runs from released parameter files and validate code outputs against reported agreement levels.

name: cosmological-snapshot-particle-classification
description: Use when a simulation snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) needs per-particle bound/unbound labels from a topology-based binding criterion that relies only on instantaneous information and no ad hoc thresholds.

name: cosmological-software-api-usage
description: Use when a task requires chaining cosmological calculation stages (e.g. parameter modules that read/write a shared state object) in a fixed order using the CosmoSIS Python API and its DataBlock data flow.

name: cosmological-table-export
description: Use when you need to reproduce and save a tabulated dark matter halo mass function (M vs dn/dlnM) from hmf, e.g. to share HMF values for a given cosmology, fitting function and mass range as a portable CSV file.

name: cosmological-time-step-limiter-analysis
description: Use when analysing or reproducing how the allowed global time step Δln a in a cosmological N-body code (specifically CONCEPT 1.0) evolves across cosmic history and which limiter governs at each scale factor and resolution.

name: cosmological-wavenumber-grid-handling
description: Reference for ingesting a CAMB-format transfer function T(k), interpolating it in log-space with linear splines, and re-gridding it onto hmf's k-bounds before power-spectrum or HMF computation.

name: cosmology-example-visualization
description: Use when you need to reproduce or validate the scalar primordial power spectrum from Mukhanov-Sasaki mode functions, or benchmark pyoscode on oscillatory cosmological perturbation equations with Bunch-Davies initial conditions.

name: cosmology-prior-sampling
description: Use when an MCMC, grid, or validation study needs LambdaCDM parameter vectors sampled across the paper's prior range to evaluate the syren linear P(k) emulator or the invertible sigma8 <-> As conversion at z=0.

name: cosmomc-metropolis-hastings-baseline-execution
description: Reference for establishing a Metropolis–Hastings baseline: when comparing a new MCMC sampler's efficiency (autocorrelation time per parameter) against CosmoMC on identical cosmological parameter spaces and likelihoods.

name: coupled-channel-bound-state-calculation
description: Use when the goal is to locate bound-state eigenvalues of an atom–molecule or molecule–molecule system (or field-dependent threshold crossings) from namelist-defined &INPUT/&BASIS/&POTL coupled-channel inputs.

name: coupled-channel-scattering-calculation-with-alkali-hyperfine-basis
description: Use when you need field-dependent s-wave scattering lengths or resonance locations for two alkali-metal atoms at ultracold collision energies, from coupled-channel calculations with hyperfine structure in a magnetic field.

name: coupled-cme-model-rerun-configuration
description: Use when a new estimate exists for an OSPREI input parameter (e.g., a PEA-reconnected-flux-derived β_M) and you need to quantify its effect on CME arrival time and in situ B relative to assumed baseline values.

name: cplusplus-class-implementation-for-clustering
description: Use when counting object pairs or triplets in large catalogues for 2PCF/3PCF estimation and brute-force O(N^2) searches are too slow; spatial neighbour queries must be restricted to relevant cells.

name: cpp-numerical-library-usage
description: Use when the analysis requires CBL's optimised C++ routines (e.g. parallel chain-mesh pair/triplet counting for 2PCF/3PCF) and the task involves handling real or simulated astronomical catalogues.

name: cpu-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a trained model's claimed inference speed must be validated on commodity CPU hardware, e.g. verifying that one ExoMDN forward pass on (mass, radius, equilibrium temperature) yields a full four-layer interior posterior in under a second.

name: credible-interval-coverage-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate a Bayesian mass-modeling fit (e.g. GravSphere2 + dynesty) by measuring credible-interval coverage of known truth profiles from mock galaxy data across tracer counts.

name: credible-interval-width-quantification
description: Use when posterior samples or published credible intervals must be reduced to a single scalar (interval width) to decide whether one analysis genuinely shrinks uncertainty relative to a baseline, e.g. R_1.4 = 11.98 (+0.35/−0.40) km vs prior literature rows.

name: cross-backend-consistency-comparison
description: Use when a GAMBIT observable can be computed by multiple interchangeable backends and you need to verify that different external codes agree on the same pinned model point, rather than relying on a single backend's output.

name: cross-code-field-comparison
description: Use when a benchmark problem has run through two independent solvers (e.g., Dedalus 2048^2 spectral modes vs. Athena finite-volume) and you must quantify how resolution governs accuracy against unphysical secondary instabilities.

name: cross-code-n-body-power-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when two or more N-body codes must be validated against each other via relative power spectra P_codeA/P_codeB, especially when diagnosing force-solver differences (multipole order, randomised displacements) at early vs late redshifts.

name: cross-code-neighbor-list-verification
description: Use when a custom octree traversal must reproduce FleCSPH's neighbor lists: reference data from a sodtube/hydro generator is available, particles are inserted into the FleCSI octree, and per-particle neighbor lists must be cross-checked entry-by-entry.

name: cross-code-profile-interpolation-and-difference-analysis
description: Use when two codes have produced radial profiles (x_HII, x_HeII, x_HeIII, T) for the same well-posed problem and you must quantify agreement, e.g. validating rabacus against Cloudy 13.03 reference profiles.

name: cross-code-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a new forward-modelling tool against an established code: you need a single-realization runtime ratio plus fractional-agreement of model outputs (e.g. rotation/dispersion curves) on matched synthetic observations.

name: cross-code-simulation-comparison
description: Use when two simulation codes' power spectra are available as |code_A/code_B − 1| versus k curves and you need to locate the wavenumber where they diverge beyond a threshold (e.g. 1‰) and determine whether that scale is resolution-dependent.

name: cross-code-spectra-interpolation-and-residual-analysis
description: Use when a new linear perturbation solver's P(k) or CMB spectra must be validated against a benchmark code like CLASS, requiring grid alignment via interpolation and relative/absolute residual quantification.

name: cross-code-yield-comparison
description: Use when a newly computed dN/dE photon yield table for dark matter annihilation final states must be validated against established codes, or when quantitatively comparing dark matter codes' indirect-detection outputs.

name: cross-correlation-peak-quality-assignment
description: Use when you have ranked cross-correlation peak heights (v1, v2) from an autoz-style matcher and need to convert them into discrete match-quality classes (QOP1–QOP6) or flag matches needing manual merging.

name: cross-format-storage-comparison
description: Use when comparing storage codecs (e.g. FITS Rice vs HDF5 LZF_SS vs bitshuffle) on large binary-table or image data files, and you need per-codec compression ratio, compression time, and read time with lossless round-trip verification.

name: cross-module-data-passing-testing
description: Use when building or testing an in-memory store that passes calculation results between sequential pipeline modules, especially when values must be keyed by (section, name) pairs and retrieved via typed getters.

name: cross-observation-background-variability-analysis
description: Use when analyzing multiple public IXPE level-2 event files and you need per-observation characterization of the instrumental background's off-axis radial distribution (slope alpha) for background modeling or subtraction.

name: cross-sampler-convergence-comparison
description: Use when parallelised MCMC chains from different samplers (e.g. emcee ensemble walkers vs. Metropolis–Hastings chains) must be compared for initialisation bias and a burn-in length must be justified numerically.

name: cross-sampler-convergence-comparison-against-bugs-reference
description: Use when a newly implemented MCMC sampler (e.g. DE-MC with N=2d chains, gamma=2.38/sqrt(2d)) must be validated by reproducing posterior percentiles of a high-dimensional Bayesian model against an independent long-run reference sampler like WinBUGS.

name: cross-software-fit-comparison
description: Use when a composite X-ray spectral model has been fitted in one framework and you need to confirm the posterior parameter estimates are reliable by benchmarking them against a blind reference fit (e.g. XSPEC with C-stat) or another software approach.

name: cross-survey-transit-parameter-comparison
description: Use when a previously published exoplanet transit light curve (e.g. MAST Kepler long-cadence photometry or ground-based transits) needs an independent MCMC reanalysis whose system parameters are compared against the published values.

name: crossover-proposal-generation
description: Use when sampling a high-dimensional posterior (e.g. the 43-parameter Theophylline nonlinear mixed-effects model) via block updating, where full-vector DE-MC jumps mix poorly and per-block jumps with binomial crossover are needed.

name: cuda-kernel-profiling-data-extraction
description: Use when reproducing or verifying GPU kernel profiling tables (occupancy, register usage, block size, instruction vs memory time, bandwidths) reported for specific CUDA kernels on an NVIDIA K40, per floating-point precision.

name: cycles-path-traced-rendering
description: Use when you need synthetic imagery of a small solar system body (e.g. 25143 Itokawa) or planet surface for instrument characterisation, mission planning or computer-vision algorithm development, and you have a 3-D shape model plus trajectory, illumination and camera parameters.

name: cython-numeric-kernel-implementation
description: Use when a pure-Python/NumPy loop over N-body particle pairs (e.g. within a short-range cut-off x_r) is the bottleneck and per-pair work must be compiled to C while retaining Python-level orchestration.

name: dark-matter-annihilation-spectrum-computation
description: Use when a dark matter model predicts annihilation into multiple final states and per-final-state gamma-ray yields dN/dE on a log-spaced photon energy grid are needed for indirect-detection likelihoods.

name: dark-matter-effective-operator-running
description: Use when you need low-energy DM-nucleon couplings or direct detection bounds for a vector-mediator simplified model defined at high energy, or when translating LHC mediator mass limits into direct detection cross-section bounds.

name: dark-matter-electron-response-computation
description: Use when parameterizing DM-electron ionization rates of argon or xenon detector targets in terms of atomic responses, or when reproducing the radial-integral and response-function tables of arXiv:1912.08204.

name: dark-matter-electron-scattering-effective-theory
description: Use when modeling sub-GeV dark matter-electron ionization of atomic targets (argon, xenon) under general effective-theory interaction operators, and you need the tabulated atomic responses — not just the ionization form factor — or must assess the relative weight of the three newly identified.

name: dark-matter-free-streaming-scale-parameterization
description: Use when computing halo mass functions under a WDM model: a CDM linear transfer function is available and the small-scale power must be suppressed via a free-streaming scale set by m_X, Omega_X, h and g_X.

name: dark-matter-halo-abundance-calculation
description: Use when you need to compute dark matter halo abundances (dndlnm) over ~10^10-10^16 h^-1 M_sun at a fixed redshift, or quantify how HMF fitting functions (PS, ST, Jenkins, Tinker, Warren, Watson, etc.) diverge from Sheth-Tormen.

name: dark-matter-halo-parameter-sampling
description: Use when you have per-halo diffmah parameter fits (early-time, peak-time, late-time power-law parameters) and need synthetic Monte Carlo realizations of halo mass histories whose ensemble reproduces population-average growth and assembly diversity.

name: dark-matter-halo-residual-quantification
description: Use when you have per-halo fit residuals from a halo assembly-history model (e.g. diffmah fit errors) plus halo positions and a large-scale density field from a simulation like TNG, and need to test whether approximation errors remain uncorrelated with environment — i.

name: dark-matter-observable-computation
description: Use when the analysis goal is to compute dark matter observables or likelihoods (relic abundance, gamma-ray yields, spin-independent/spin-dependent direct-detection limits) for a BSM model via a GAMBIT module-mode scan.

name: dark-matter-particle-binding-energy-assessment
description: Use when you have a cosmological simulation particle snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) and need a threshold-free per-particle bound/unbound classification for halo structure assignment.

name: dark-matter-photon-signal-yield-calculation
description: Use when a global-fit scan must score a dark matter model point against a current gamma-ray experiment's likelihood, and photon yields need to be generated from the model's annihilation/decay channels.

name: dark-matter-relic-density-calculation
description: Use when a task requires the dark matter relic density for a pinned benchmark model point (e.g. MSSM7), or a side-by-side DarkSUSY vs micrOMEGAs comparison on shared inputs.

name: data-release-product-retrieval
description: Use when the task requires enumerating spectra, targets, or derived RV/activity products from a public survey data release (e.g. CARMENES DR1 GTO 2016-2020) and validating counts against published values such as 19,633 spectra / 362 targets.

name: datablock-typed-put-get-usage
description: Use when building or testing a CosmoSIS pipeline: you need to seed a DataBlock with chosen parameters, or a module must read/write typed values (e.g. get_int, get_double_array_1d) in section/name keys before handing the block to the next module.

name: daubechies-dwt-signal-processing
description: Use when fitting transit light curves (e.g., Kepler photometry) whose residuals show correlated (red) noise, and you need MCMC parameter uncertainties that marginalize over free σw and σr instead of fixed χ² error bars.

name: ddcalc-experiment-configuration
description: Use when a dark matter benchmark point specifies both spin-independent and spin-dependent couplings and a direct detection likelihood (e.g. XENON1T) must be computed with DDCalc inside a GAMBIT scan.

name: de-mc-adaptive-jump-scale-tuning
description: Use when evaluating or tuning the jump scale gamma of Differential Evolution Markov Chain (DE-MC) on a multimodal target such as a two-component Normal mixture, where random walk Metropolis fails and RMSE of the posterior mean and acceptance fraction are the quality metrics.

name: dealiased-fourier-nonlinear-evaluation
description: Use when solving PDEs with Dedalus on a periodic 2D Fourier domain where quadratic nonlinear products of fields (e.g. convective and Lorentz-force terms in compressible MHD) must be evaluated on a mode grid such as 4096x4096.

name: debris-disc-geometry-parameterization
description: Use when fitting an inclined debris disc in u,v space with vis-r and you need to fix or initialize disc geometry (inclination, PA, sky-plane offsets) from e.g. scattered-light or moment maps before sampling radial-profile parameters.

name: debris-disc-radial-profile-modelling
description: Use when high-resolution ALMA observations of a (debris) disc need fast parametric radial-profile fitting directly in the visibility plane, e.g. from an exported ms to .npy/.txt visibilities with disc geometry (-g) and radial profile (-p) parameters.

name: debris-disc-surface-brightness-profile-specification
description: Use when you have u,v visibilities exported to a numpy/text file from an ALMA ms (e.g. hr4796.selfcal.npy) and want to model the disc as a parametric radial profile evaluated directly in visibility space.

name: density-field-variance-evaluation
description: Use when estimating halo number density dn/dM or effective halo bias b(z) from dark matter halo mass function models (Press-Schechter, Sheth-Tormen, Tinker, etc.) and you need sigma(M) at a fixed cosmology.

name: density-profile-computation
description: Use when a particle snapshot has been split into bound/unbound populations (e.g. by Strawberry's boosted-potential criterion) and you need radial density profiles to test which component is finite-extent and virialised.

name: density-volume-import-into-blender
description: Use when a simulated gas/dust coma number-density volume (e.g., ComaCreator EXR output on a 64x64x64 sample grid) must be visualised as a rendered image of a comet nucleus embedded in a diffuse coma within a fly-by scene.

name: dependency-graph-cascading-update-implementation
description: Use when a parameterized scientific calculation must be re-run after changing one or more inputs and only the dependent quantities should be recomputed rather than the entire pipeline.

name: destriper-baseline-null-validation
description: Use when a signal-only (noise-free) simulated polarimeter timestream is available and you need to verify the destriper adds no spurious offsets — i.e., baselines should solve to ~1e-16 K.

name: detection-fraction-sample-statistics
description: Use when comparing survey detection counts for two observables of the same disc sample (e.g. 12CO flux vs disc size) to decide which observable maximizes the usable population for model–data comparison.

name: deuterium-abundance-anomaly-comparison-across-rate-prescriptions
description: Use when primordial deuterium (or lithium) abundance predictions from a BBN code must be compared under different nuclear-rate compilations (PRIMAT vs NACRE II), propagating rate uncertainties via Monte Carlo posterior sampling.

name: devolatilisation-trend-analysis
description: Use when you have stellar elemental abundance patterns for F/G/K stars and need to compute per-element condensation temperatures and planet bulk compositions/devolatilisation trends, validating synthetic abundance-pattern effects against real solar-neighbourhood data.

name: dewiggled-power-spectrum-bao-damping
description: Reference for modelling redshift-space 2PCF xi(s) from a de-wiggled BAO power spectrum in CosmoBolognaLib, when redshift errors, RSD (growth rate f), and BAO damping must be propagated into the monopole model.

name: dex-accuracy-quantification
description: Use when you have fitted model MAHs and simulated halo mass-assembly histories (from merger trees of gravity-only or TNG simulations) and need to validate approximation accuracy in dex units over a time range.

name: differentiable-model-evaluation-with-jax
description: Use when you hold per-halo fitted diffmah parameters (early-time, peak-time, late-time) and need to evaluate the differentiable model to generate mass assembly histories, e.g. Monte Carlo-sampled synthetic halo populations reproducing mean growth and assembly diversity.

name: differentiable-model-gradient-optimization
description: Use when you need to approximate individual halo mass growth curves (log halo mass vs. cosmic time) from merger-tree catalogs, e.g. TNG host halos or subhalos above 10^11 Msun, with a compact analytic parameterization.

name: differential-evolution-markov-chain-sampling
description: Use when sampling a Bayesian posterior over real-valued parameters (d ≈ 5–100+) where choosing jump scale/orientation for single-chain RWM is hard, or when benchmarking MCMC efficiency against WinBUGS or optimal-normal-jump random walk Metropolis.

name: differential-evolution-proposal-tuning
description: Use when fitting Bayesian models on real parameter spaces where an appropriate scale and orientation for the jumping distribution is hard to choose, e.g. nonlinear mixed-effects models, and multi-chain MCMC should adapt jumps automatically via gamma = 2.38/sqrt(2d).

name: diffmah-model-residual-analysis
description: Use when validating that a fitted halo mass accretion history model (e.g., diffmah 3-parameter fits) reproduces assembly bias: i.e., residuals must show negligible correlation with large-scale density in simulations like TNG.

name: dimension-6-operator-mixing-analysis
description: Use when you have a vector-mediator simplified model defined by the mediator mass and high-energy couplings to SM fields, and you need low-energy couplings to u, d, s quarks and protons/neutrons for direct detection.

name: dirbe-cio-reference-comparison
description: Use when you have a simulated zodiacal emission timestream for a survey observer (e.g. DIRBE) and need a binned HEALPix map that can be validated pixel-by-pixel against calibrated time-ordered observations such as the DIRBE CIO dataset.

name: direct-detection-coefficient-extraction
description: Use when you have runDM-evolved low-energy couplings for a vector mediator and need the dimension-6 operator coefficients for direct detection: couplings to u, d, s quarks and to protons and neutrons.

name: dirichlet-basis-recombination
description: Use when assembling sparse tau-method matrices for a 1D spectral PDE (e.g. Poisson with Dirichlet/Neumann BCs on x∈[-1,1]) and you need boundary conditions folded into the basis via recombination rather than ad-hoc constraint rows.

name: disc-evolution-model-data-comparison
description: Use when ALMA survey catalogs of 12CO line fluxes and 887-micron disc sizes need to be overlaid with disc-evolution model tracks to test viscous vs MHD-wind scenarios, or when deciding whether to select samples by flux or size criteria.

name: disc-geometry-gradient-mapping
description: Use when fitting a disc transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc and you need to reduce the parameter space of disc size/orientation configurations by gradient-based rejection.

name: disc-geometry-parameterisation
description: Use when modelling transits of circumsecondary disc (CSD) systems with azimuthally symmetric, non-uniform optical-depth profiles, and you need theoretical light-curve gradients for every possible disc geometry before rejecting configurations.

name: disc-orientation-parameter-space-rejection
description: Use when modelling a transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc and you need to constrain disc size and orientation by rejecting azimuthally symmetric disc geometries that cannot reproduce the observed light-curve gradient.

name: disc-parameter-grid-sampling
description: Use when model–data agreement for 12CO fluxes (e.g. against Lupus or Upper Sco ALMA samples) is inconclusive and you need to quantify how uncertainties in initial disc mass and radius propagate into predicted flux spread.

name: discrete-hankel-transform-implementation
description: Use when fitting ALMA visibility data with parametric radial profiles (e.g. the '-p 0.013 1.07 0.06 0.01' style vis-r parameters) and a fast model-visibility prediction is needed without image generation.

name: disk-boundary-condition-configuration
description: Use when reproducing or parameterizing a Thompson et al. (2005) style AGN disk in pagn and you must choose Rout, Mdot_out (in MSun/yr), and Rin before calling solve_disk, or when validating inner-boundary accretion rates against reference values.

name: disk-bulge-halo-mass-decomposition
description: Use when a 1D rotation curve from a rotationally supported (V/sigma_0 >~ 2) disk galaxy must be attributed to disk, bulge, and dark-matter-halo mass components with fitted parameter posteriors.

name: disk-structure-diagnostic-visualization
description: Use when a pagn SirkoAGN or ThompsonAGN disk has just been solved and you need to verify the solution ran correctly before using the profiles (temperature, density) downstream.

name: dispersion-delay-alignment
description: Use when input is a dispersed frequency-channel filterbank (e.g. SIGPROC format) in which a pulse arrives later at lower frequencies due to interstellar free electrons, and a DM-search dedispersed time series is needed.

name: display-scaling-parameter-derivation
description: Use when a FITS science image must be transcoded to a browser-friendly format (e.g., TIFF tiles for IIPImage) and global display cut-offs Smin/Smax must be written to TIFF sample-value tags.

name: distributed-octree-particle-insertion
description: Use when reimplementing or validating parallel SPH neighbor search: particles must be inserted into a shared octree, refined until smoothing neighborhoods are isolated, and data on remote ranks fetched via non-blocking MPI instead of blocking waits.

name: dm-electron-operator-mapping
description: Use when null-result ionization data from argon or xenon DM search experiments must be converted into 90% C.L. exclusion limits on effective DM-electron operator couplings as a function of DM mass.

name: dominant-mode-selection-and-rheology-reduction
description: Use when a layered viscoelastic body's full Voigt representation has more relaxation elements than needed and the tidal response only matters over a specified frequency interval (e.g. the orbital-evolution range), requiring a reduced model.

name: donki-cme-catalog-retrieval
description: Use when configuring a CME simulation (e.g., OSPREI) from observational, real-time-analogous sources: you have a CME date and need catalog-derived latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal velocity, and angular width plus solar wind values.

name: drag-based-cme-arrival-time-modeling
description: Use when a coronagraph- or ForeCAT-derived far-corona CME state (lat, lon, tilt, coronal speed) must be propagated to 1 AU to predict transit/arrival time, duration, density, and central B at a spacecraft.

name: drift-kick-scheduling-across-time-rungs
description: Use when implementing or reproducing an individual/adaptive particle time-stepping scheme from CONCEPT 1.0, e.g. scheduling drifts and kicks over multiple rungs and assigning particles to rungs via the eq. 42 acceleration criterion.

name: dust-impact-dynamics
description: Use when propagating a spacecraft attitude profile around a small body (e.g., comet/asteroid fly-by) and you must quantify how dust particle impacts, atmospheric drag, or gravity-gradient torques perturb an attitude solution that would otherwise be treated as perfectly controlled.

name: dwarf-galaxy-density-slope-recovery
description: Use when you have discrete stellar tracer positions and LOS velocities (optionally proper motions) for a spherical, equilibrium stellar system and need the inner dark matter density slope at R1/2 with a statistical error, e.g. to distinguish cuspy from cored profiles.

name: dwarf-galaxy-mass-modeling
description: Use when you have discrete stellar tracer positions and velocities (LOS-only or LOS+PM) for a dwarf galaxy or star cluster assumed to be in equilibrium, and you need an unbinned posterior for the log density slope at R1/2 (e.g. cuspy vs cored discrimination).

name: dye-tracer-reversibility-visualization
description: Use when a low-Reynolds-number (Stokes) flow demonstration needs reversible tracer advection — e.g., verifying a spectral PDE solver reproduces the classic dye unmixing after n_rot inner-wall rotations.

name: e-merlin-antenna-data-quality-screening
description: Use when reducing e-MERLIN visibility datasets where, beyond RFI flagged by SumThreshold, antenna zero-amplitude dropouts or Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans must be identified and flagged before calibration.

name: e-merlin-instrumental-artifact-mitigation
description: Use when reducing e-MERLIN visibility data in AIPS/ParselTongue and Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans (an inherent e-MERLIN instrumental artifact) must be flagged alongside RFI and zero-amplitude dropouts.

name: eddington-accretion-rate-normalization
description: Use when a solved pAGN Thompson or Sirko disk yields Mdot(R) in physical units (MSun/yr) and you need a dimensionless, source-independent accretion-rate profile or inner-boundary value comparable across black-hole masses.

name: eddy-field-visualization
description: Use when HDF5 snapshot output from a spectrally-discretized geophysical-flow simulation (e.g. Dedalus quasigeostrophic run with 256x128x32 modes) must be inspected qualitatively for coherent eddy structures in its saturated state.

name: effective-halo-bias-parameterisation
description: Use when modelling or interpreting halo/galaxy clustering at a given redshift and you need the effective halo bias b(z) from published parameterisations, or when comparing bias prescriptions against halo number densities dn/dM.

name: eigenphase-sum-resonance-analysis
description: Use when a coupled-channel scattering calculation must locate a Feshbach or shape resonance via its signature in the eigenphase sum, e.g. two coupled Lennard-Jones channels with a closed upper channel shifted by ~100 cm-1.

name: eigenspectrum-spacing-and-mode-trapping-visualization
description: Use when a computed wave eigenproblem must be checked against theoretical spectral regularities — constant frequency spacing of acoustic modes, constant period spacing of gravity modes — or when mode trapping regions must be visualized as eigenfrequency vs. horizontal wavenumber.

name: einstein-a-coefficient-summation
description: Use when you have an ExoMol (or similar) molecular line list with states and transitions files containing Einstein A coefficients and need per-level radiative lifetimes rather than spectra.

name: einstein-boltzmann-perturbation-evolution
description: Use when you need perturbation-level cosmological observables — metric potentials Φ/Ψ, density overdensities δ, velocity divergences θ, shear and polarization moments — as functions of conformal time for fixed wavenumbers, or when validating a new EB solver against CLASS.

name: einstein-boltzmann-solver-cross-validation
description: Use when a new or modified cosmological solver must be validated against CLASS: compare background quantities, thermodynamics, spectra, or parameter derivatives by quantifying maximum differences against stated tolerances.

name: eisenstein-hu-fit-ratio-target-construction
description: Use when building an interpretable symbolic emulator for P(k): instead of regressing the full spectrum directly, evaluate an existing low-accuracy fitting function for the same cosmologies and regress the fitting-function-to-CAMB ratio as the learning target.

name: electric-field-spectrum-extraction
description: Use when NuRadioMC simulation outputs for a fixed in-ice neutrino shower must be reduced to per-model frequency-domain electric-field spectra at an antenna, e.g. to compare Askaryan emission parameterizations.

name: electron-density-fixed-point-iteration
description: Use when equilibrium ionization fractions of H/He gas are needed for given (T, nH, nHe) but eliminating n_e from the implicit photo-collisional equilibrium equations yields an intractable high-order polynomial.

name: elemental-ratio-variation-analysis
description: Use when you need to isolate the effect of a single stellar/disk abundance ratio (e.g. C/O) on element condensation temperatures in an equilibrium condensation simulation, keeping temperature range, pressure, molecule selection and all other element ratios fixed.

name: elliptical-aperture-photometry
description: Use when you have a separated host galaxy component (cube or spaxel map) plus co-registered reference imaging, and need an integrated 1D host spectrum for redshift or line-flux measurements.

name: embedding-csv-export
description: Use when you have FITS astronomical images and a pretrained astromorph checkpoint, and need a machine-readable CSV table of image embeddings plus metadata for clustering, similarity exploration, or morphological comparison.

name: empirical-interpolant-node-selection
description: Use when a reduced basis of m greedy parameters has been built for a fiducial waveform family and you must induce m time nodes for empirical interpolation to construct a surrogate's compact offline representation.

name: empirical-interpolant-online-evaluation
description: Use when a fast, accurate waveform prediction is needed at a generic parameter choice after a surrogate (reduced basis + empirical interpolant + fits) has already been built, and solving EOB/NR equations online is too costly.

name: empirical-interpolant-reconstruction
description: Use when a fiducial waveform family (e.g. EOB-LAL nonspinning BBH modes) has already been compressed into greedy-reduced-basis coefficients plus empirical interpolant times, and fast reconstruction at new parameters (mass ratio q, spins chiA/chiB) with pointwise error checks is required.

name: ems-error-stack-forwarding
description: Use when layering a re-implemented API (e.g. HDSv5 over HDF5) onto a backend that maintains its own error stack, so backend failures must be reported through the host error system (EMS).

name: energy-conservation-error-analysis
description: Use when validating a multi-scale integrator (e.g. Nemesis) against a direct N-body reference (Ph4): you need to quantify energy-error behaviour and confirm global- and local-scale indistinguishability over a controlled test window.

name: ensemble-feature-importance-analysis
description: Use when a trained ensemble classifier's outputs must be explained (ranked feature importances) or when per-source class probabilities must be screened to isolate ambiguous astronomical sources for follow-up.

name: ensemble-learning-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when training gradient-boosting ensemble classifiers on tabular photometric (or other tabular) data where F1-score per class is the target metric and hyper-parameters must be re-tuned after any change to the input features.

name: ensemble-output-data-processing
description: Use when OSPREI ensemble runs (nRuns > 1 with a '.ens' configuration file) have completed for one or more CMEs and the standardized output files must be converted into figures, histograms, contour plots, or correlation panels.

name: ensemble-parameter-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have standardized OSPREI ensemble output files (from a '.ens' configuration varying input ranges) and need to identify which varied inputs drive which quantifiable outputs, e.g. final latitude, longitude, tilt, arrival time, speed, or in situ properties.

name: ensemble-parameter-sampling
description: Use when uncertainty in CME initial parameters (latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal velocity, angular width, etc.) must be propagated through ForeCAT/OSPREI to produce probabilistic distributions of deflection, rotation, arrival time, or in situ properties.

name: ensemble-probability-contour-visualization
description: Use when standardized OSPREI output files exist from a single run or ensemble and need to be converted into profile figures, histograms, and ensemble probability contour plots with optional OMNI data overlays.

name: ensemble-sampler-walkers-configuration
description: Use when running MCMC sampling of CMB/WMAP cosmological parameters with CosmoHammer and you must size the emcee walker ensemble and configure the LikelihoodComputationChain before sampling.

name: enthalpy-of-vaporization-calculation
description: Use when you have corrected isothermal GC retention times for a compound series over a temperature range plus one reference compound with known vapour pressure-temperature data, and need ΔHv/ΔHv-Tb values.

name: enthalpy-of-vaporization-data-compilation
description: Use when combining derived or literature ΔHv data for organostannanes and reference hydrocarbons into one dataset and testing descriptor choice (molecular weight vs intrinsic molar volume) via linear regression.

name: entropy-of-vaporization-derivation-from-boiling-points
description: Use when you have per-compound enthalpies of vaporization from GC vapour-pressure data plus literature boiling points (Tb), and need ΔSv = ΔHv/Tb for Table 4-style comparisons across organostannanes and hydrocarbons.

name: eob-waveform-generation
description: Use when you need fiducial EOB waveforms as training data for reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate building, or as a timing and accuracy baseline against a surrogate model.

name: eos-likelihood-implementation
description: Use when you have a set of candidate EOSs each with a mass-radius curve and maximum mass M_TOV, and need to weight them by radio-timing pulsar mass posteriors and NICER M-R constraints as part of a Bayesian EOS-inference run.

name: eos-posterior-comparison-across-analyses
description: Use when you have NMMA posterior samples from a multi-messenger fit (e.g., GW170817 strain + AT2017gfo photometry) and want to test whether adding another messenger (GRB170817A) shifts or tightens posteriors on R_1.4 and ejecta parameters.

name: eos-speed-of-sound-extension-modeling
description: Use when you must extend a nuclear-physics-constrained EOS (chiral-EFT/AFDMC samples, valid to ~1.5 nsat) to supra-nuclear densities to obtain mass-radius-tidal-deformability families for neutron-star inference.

name: equal-arrival-time-flux-integration
description: Use when a joint GW + kilonova + GRB-afterglow analysis (e.g., GW170817/AT2017gfo/GRB170817A) needs a model afterglow lightcurve from a structured jet to fit observed afterglow flux-density data.

name: equation-of-state-constraint-analysis
description: Use when a binary-neutron-star event has gravitational-wave data plus kilonova photometry and/or a GRB afterglow light curve, and the goal is a joint EOS/neutron-star-radius posterior rather than per-messenger analyses combined a posteriori.

name: equilibrium-condensation-simulation
description: Use when you need condensation sequences or 50% condensation temperatures (Tc) of elements/molecules from a stellar abundance pattern, or bulk compositions of rocky planets accreted from a feeding zone, e.g. testing metallicity or C/O sensitivity of Tc.

name: equilibrium-photoionization-solver-execution
description: Use when you need equilibrium ionization/temperature solutions for hydrogen and helium gas in a spherical geometry with a central point source, and when agreement with a Cloudy reference profile (e.g. Cloudy 13.03) must be quantified radius by radius.

name: equilibrium-temperature-slab-solution
description: Use when quantifying how thermal evolution, helium treatment, and recombination-radiation transfer alter H I / He I / He II column densities in Lyman-limit slabs exposed to an isotropic UV background.

name: error-bound-auto-tuning-per-level
description: Use when implementing or extending error-bounded lossy compressors for multi-level interpolation predictors (e.g., SolarZip on Solar Orbiter EUI FITS data) and you must guarantee the user-specified REL/ABS bound is honored despite error accumulation across interpolation levels.

name: error-bounded-lossy-compression-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing compression ratios of an error-bounded lossy compressor against baselines on scientific imaging data (e.g. Solar EUV FITS from FSI or HRI_EUV) under identical error-bound settings.

name: espresso-ccf-rv-comparison
description: Use when comparing template-matching RV precision against DRS CCF uncertainties for ESPRESSO M-type spectra, or when validating an S-BART RV run against the paper's ~15 cm/s median uncertainty claim.

name: espresso-rv-drift-correction
description: Use when processing S-BART output RV .txt files (columns BJD, RVc, RVc_ERR, SA, DRIFT) from ESPRESSO observations and you need drift-corrected RVs in m/s or an instrument NZP estimate.

name: euler-discretisation-equivalence-verification
description: Use when you need to numerically confirm that a discrete recurrent architecture (GRU-style gating with update/reset gates and candidate state) matches a proposed continuous-time ODE under unit-step explicit Euler discretisation.

name: euler-equation-stationary-solver-configuration
description: Use when the goal is to solve the 2-D compressible isothermal Euler equations to a stationary state with galax2d, or to rerun the solver with alternative parameter sets from ./paper/paper.pdf instead of the defaults.

name: event-driven-n-body-collision-scheduling
description: Use when simulating an N-body system of bodies on Keplerian orbits about a central mass where collisions are rare (e.g. Solar-System-like systems) and small-step integration would be wasteful.

name: exact-nbody-reference-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a fast multipole method (FMM) gravity solver: you need a quadratic-complexity exact N-body reference whose wall-clock timings prove the FMM runtime scales linearly or sublinearly with particle count N.

name: exafs-fit-statistics-extraction
description: Use when a feffit refinement of Feff paths to EXAFS chi(k) data has completed and you need to pull refined parameter values, chi-square, and R-factor out of the results object for model comparison or reporting (e.g. to a CSV).

name: exclusion-limit-overlay-visualization-vs-mass
description: Use when a BBN parameter scan over the mass of a thermalized new species (scalar, vector, Majorana, or Dirac X) yields abundance predictions that must be compared against observational exclusion limits on a shared mass axis.

name: exclusion-limit-statistical-inference
description: Use when the goal is to convert null-result ionization-rate data from argon or xenon target DM searches, plus tabulated atomic response functions, into coupling-vs-mass exclusion limit curves for DM-electron interaction operators.

name: exomol-database-file-handling
description: Use when preparing ExoMol line-list files (e.g. 1H2-16O__POKAZATEL.states.bz2 and .trans.bz2) for PyExoCross: identifying the molecule/isotopologue/dataset/SpeciesID and arranging ReadPath/SavePath before running any function.

name: exomol-line-list-processing
description: Use when the input is an ExoMol molecular line list (e.g. 1H2-16O POKAZATEL .states.bz2/.trans.bz2/.pf/.def files) and derived spectroscopic properties such as LTE stick spectra, partition functions, lifetimes, cooling functions, or oscillator strengths must be computed.

name: exoplanet-archive-population-sampling
description: Use when comparing a physical-property distribution (e.g. bulk density) between two exoplanet populations split by a diagram position (period–radius), and when locating the empirical dividing value between the two regimes.

name: exoplanet-cloud-composition-profile-simulation
description: Use when a study asks how cloud composition and extinction in an exoplanet atmosphere change with bulk elemental composition (e.g., metal-rich vs C-rich bulk), and requires a fast 1D cloud model with condensed-species profiles per altitude layer.

name: exoplanet-cloud-condensation-modeling
description: Use when you need vertical compositional structure of clouds (e.g., layered magnesiumsilicate over iron) in a hot-Jupiter, sub-Neptune, or self-luminous planet atmosphere, and require the result in seconds for joint gas+cloud retrieval.

name: exoplanet-cloud-model-execution
description: Use when you need to execute the ExoLyn codebase to compute an exoplanet atmospheric cloud structure (e.g., a hot-Jupiter layered Mg-silicate/Fe cloud) or benchmark its runtime, starting from its parameter and chemistry text files.

name: exoplanet-discovery-category-classification
description: Use when a radial-velocity survey data release (e.g. CARMENES DR1) provides planet and sample tables and the goal is to reproduce the published yield tally broken down by planet provenance/status category.

name: exoplanet-interior-posterior-inference
description: Use when a low-mass (<25 Earth mass) exoplanet needs full-posterior interior characterization from only mass, radius, and equilibrium temperature observables, including uncertainty propagation via repeated predictions within observational error ranges.

name: exoplanet-interior-structure-data-preparation
description: Use when preparing compositional interior-structure labels (layer mass fractions constrained to sum to one) as training targets for an MDN that predicts planetary layer fractions and thicknesses from mass, radius, and equilibrium temperature.

name: exoplanet-model-comparison-bic-evidence
description: Use when an RV time-series analysis must decide how many Keplerian (planet) signals to retain, i.e. successive EMPEROR autorun models (k = 1, 2, ...) need ranking by Bayesian evidence (log Z) or BIC under a stopping tolerance.

name: exoplanet-occurrence-rate-estimation
description: Use when estimating planet occurrence rates as a function of stellar metallicity, age, or galactic population for a resolved stellar population, or when comparing planet demographics between metal-rich and metal-poor galactic regions.

name: exoplanet-orbital-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you have multi-instrument RV timeseries for a star (e.g. GJ 699, 51 Peg) and need to detect and characterise planetary signals with posteriors, evidence-based model selection, and stellar-mass-derived physical parameters.

name: exoplanet-parameter-uncertainty-propagation
description: Use when a derived planetary quantity (e.g. atmospheric mass-loss rate) must be computed from fitted planet/star parameters and reported with a propagated uncertainty, especially when comparing alternative physical models on identical inputs.

name: exoplanet-signal-detection-model-selection
description: Use when you have one or more RV timeseries (optionally with Hipparcos/Gaia astrometry) and need to automatically decide how many Keplerian signals plus noise models (Jitter, magnetic cycle, acceleration) describe the data without manual model comparison.

name: exoplanet-transit-parameter-estimation
description: Use when unbinned, un-phase-folded transit photometry (ground-based or Kepler) must yield inclination, a/Rs, Rp/Rs, and per-transit mid-transit times with uncertainties that correctly account for red noise.

name: exoplanet-transit-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you have a (synthetic or real) transit light curve as time/flux arrays and need posterior credible intervals on transit parameters such as depth, duration, and ephemeris, or a transmission spectrum, without pre-specifying a GP covariance kernel.

name: exoplanet-transit-photometry-modelling
description: Use when multi-instrument transit photometry (e.g. CHEOPS visits plus two TESS sectors) is available for a multi-planet system and per-planet radii and orbital periods must be derived jointly with uncertainties.

name: exoplanet-transmission-spectrum-generation
description: Use when an atmospheric column with layered Mg-silicate clouds atop an iron cloud must be converted into a synthetic spectrum, and the 8–10 μm Mg-silicate absorption feature must be reproduced or checked against observed mid-infrared data.

name: exponential-decay-peak-recovery-analysis
description: Use when preprocessing noisy (e.g. Poisson-noised) quasar or AAOmega spectra prior to autoz cross-correlation matching, and a smoother must preserve broad emission-feature peak locations rather than depress them as a moving average would.

name: external-boltzmann-code-dispatch-camb
description: Use when the analysis goal is to compute fσ8 (or other growth quantities) at a chosen redshift using CosmoBolognaLib's cosmobl::Cosmology with an external Boltzmann code (CAMB) rather than internal approximations.

name: external-torque-computation-flyby
description: Use when you have a propagated spacecraft-state time series from SISPO's Orekit trajectory simulation that presumes perfect attitude control, and you must quantify attitude offsets from dust-impact, drag, or gravity-gradient torques.

name: f1-score-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to verify or benchmark a machine-learning classification pipeline against published per-class F1-scores on SDSS+WISE photometry, or to establish a reproducible galaxy/QSO/star classification baseline before modifying the method.

name: factorial-model-formula-specification
description: Use when fitting a gamma-family, log-link GLM to predict photometric redshifts from PCA-decomposed magnitudes and you must decide which covariates and interaction terms enter the model formula.

name: false-positive-rate-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a supernova spectral classifier's contamination of the SN Ia sample, e.g. counting core-collapse SNe (II, Ibc) typed as Ia across contrast bins for an extraction method like HyperGal.

name: fast-multipole-gravity-solver-configuration
description: Use when a 3D self-gravitating particle simulation must be evolved with FMM gravity (linear/sublinear complexity instead of exact O(N^2) N-body) and momentum conservation must be validated.

name: fastcgi-server-performance-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking how a web tile/image server's throughput and latency scale with concurrent requests beyond the number of CPU cores, to substantiate per-server user-capacity claims.

name: fermi-lat-photon-data-reduction
description: Use when the analysis goal is to constrain axion-like particle (ALP) parameters from gamma-ray spectra of a blazar and requires binned spectral extraction from multi-year (e.g., 12-year) Fermi-LAT photon event data.

name: fermi-lat-spectral-data-handling
description: Use when re-analyzing a Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observation (e.g. NGC 1275) to search for axion-like particle effects, and binned spectral data must be prepared for spectral-irregularity computation or ALP-photon conversion runs.

name: field-height-dependent-aberration-psf-simulation
description: Use when synthetic space-scene images (e.g. Blender Cycles renders of the 25143 Itokawa model) must be degraded with realistic lens aberrations and sensor noise to test imaging instruments or computer-vision algorithms.

name: figure-and-text-fact-tabulation
description: Use when an article reports quantitative performance or benchmark results in a figure plus supporting section text (e.g. strong-scaling curves), and the goal is to turn those stated facts into a structured, per-condition table.

name: figure-caption-information-extraction
description: Use when a research question asks to reproduce or verify results reported in a specific figure (e.g., GPU speedups in Figure 5) and the values must be read from the figure or caption and converted to structured rows.

name: figure-data-digitization
description: Use when a paper reports a quantitative relation only as a scatter plot (e.g. brightest masked-source flux-density vs proportional RMS drop in Figs. 4-5) with no machine-readable table, and the points must be extracted for refitting or sub-sample comparison.

name: figure-reproduction-comparison-plotting
description: Use when a paper's figure demonstrates a quantitative or qualitative algorithm property (e.g. peak recovery under smoothing) that can be validated by regenerating the synthetic inputs and overlaying original, method, and baseline curves in one plot.

name: figure-section-citation-mapping
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a paper's figure or results summary and each claim must be paired with its citation location (figure/section number) in a structured, machine-checkable output.

name: file-format-fallback-open
description: Use when a legacy file-format library and its re-implementation (e.g. HDSv4 and HDS-on-HDF5) must coexist behind one API, and existing files of either flavor must open transparently without user-visible backend choice.

name: file-size-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when a paper or migration plan compares file sizes of an old vs new data format (e.g. HDSv4 vs HDSv5/HDF5) for a fixed set of benchmark datasets and you need to reproduce or extend the byte-size comparison table.

name: finite-difference-jacobian-evaluation
description: Use when validating automatic-differentiation derivatives of cosmological observables against an independent solver: you need a reference finite-difference Jacobian of D_l(TT/EE/TE) or P(k) w.r.t. (h, Ω_c0, Ω_b0) computed with CLASS.

name: finite-temperature-fermion-statistics
description: Use when computing ab-initio n<->p weak-conversion rates for BBN freeze-out where finite-temperature (as opposed to zero-temperature) effects on the lepton phase space must be included alongside QED and weak-magnetism corrections.

name: fisher-matrix-forecasting
description: Use when you need 1-sigma parameter error forecasts (e.g. sigma(H0), sigma(ombh2)) from a CMB power-spectrum likelihood without running MCMC, or when scanning an experimental design choice (e.g. bin width) against forecast precision.

name: fisher-matrix-parameter-normalisation
description: Use when you need a parameter covariance estimate for a differentiable likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE via candl) without finite differences, or when preparing a normalised parameter space for a gradient-based sampler such as BlackJAX NUTS.

name: fit-residual-scatter-analysis
description: Use when you have binned Fermi-LAT count/flux spectra of a point source and want to test for ALP-induced spectral oscillation via spectrum irregularity instead of direct ALP-model fitting of the observed spectrum.

name: fits-binary-table-compression-benchmarking
description: Use when large (>500 MB) binary-table FITS files must be compressed or converted to HDF5 and you need to compare codec ratios/timings before choosing a storage format.

name: fits-event-file-construction
description: Use when simulating X-ray polarimetric observations that must be written as FITS event lists compatible with the IXPE data products (e.g. from ixpeobssim source models and IRFs).

name: fits-file-sequential-read-timing
description: Use when comparing I/O performance of serialised scientific file formats (FITS vs HDF5/HDFITS) for large 3D datasets, especially when random slice access speed, not just full-file throughput, is the deciding factor.

name: fits-hdf5-roundtrip-conversion
description: Use when a FITS file must be moved into HDF5 (HDFITS) and back, and you need to establish whether the conversion is lossless at the data-unit level versus the byte level.

name: fits-header-card-diffing
description: Use when a FITS file has been converted to another format (e.g. HDFITS via fits2hdf) and back, and you must verify whether HDU data values and header cards survived the round trip, or when deciding if a converted file is safe for archiving.

name: fits-header-keyword-handling
description: Use when building an IXPE instrumental background template from pha1 dark-field spectra and the per-file rates must be rescaled by livetime and BACKSCAL read from the FITS headers.

name: fits-histogram-percentile-clipping
description: Use when transcoding FITS science data to a browser-friendly TIFF format and the output must carry display clipping metadata (SMinSampleValue/SMaxSampleValue) computed from the image histogram rather than hard-coded min/max pixel values.

name: fits-image-compression-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing lossless compression performance (ratio and throughput) of FITS Rice/FPACK vs HDF5 filters (LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP) on integer or astronomical image data.

name: fits-image-embedding-inference
description: Use when you have a trained astromorph checkpoint and a set of FITS images (e.g. Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark clouds) and need label-free morphological embeddings for each image.

name: fits-image-export
description: Use when a per-epoch radio-synthesis image produced by CASA Clean must be made telescope-portable and consumable by external tools, i.e. after deconvolution, requiring primary-beam correction and FITS export.

name: fits-image-tiled-rendering
description: Use when a user needs to inspect or navigate a >2 Gb DECam or other large-FOV FITS image stored remotely, without local storage, local software installation, or loading the whole image into memory.

name: fits-spectra-ingestion
description: Use when input data are FITS-format spectra (e.g. from the AAOmega spectrograph or any instrument matching Marz's well-defined input format) that need to be loaded for automatic redshift matching or simple FITS inspection.

name: fits-spectrum-assembly
description: Use when observational spectra (e.g. Spitzer spectroscopy) must be rebinned/convolved onto the coarser wavelength grid of pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries and packaged as multi-extension FITS for SED fitting input.

name: fits-spectrum-loading
description: Use when the input is a generic FITS file containing 1D spectra with flux, variance and wavelength extensions (e.g. AAOmega/OzDES data) that must be ingested for redshifting or visual inspection.

name: fits-to-hdf5-data-model-mapping
description: Use when converting FITS files (or MeasurementSets) into HDF5 while preserving the FITS data model of HDUs, header cards, image datasets, and binary-table columns.

name: fits-wcs-header-card-parsing
description: Use when a FITS file's header cards (CTYPE/CRVAL/CRPIX-type WCS cards) must be converted into an AST FrameSet, and the consumed cards must be verified as removed from the residual header buffer.

name: fitschan-destructive-read-verification
description: Use when a buffer of FITS header cards encoding WCS information must be converted into an AST FrameSet (e.g. from a FITS file's WCS representation), and the destructive-read semantics of the FitsChan need to be exercised and verified.

name: flexible-chain-methylene-count-grouping
description: Use when comparing derived entropies of vaporization (ΔSvap = ΔHvap/Tb) across homologous tetraorganostannanes and you need to test whether flexible-link count (≥5 methylene-like links) shifts ΔSvap away from Trouton's ~90 J/K/mol reference.

name: floating-point-subtractive-dithering-quantization
description: Use when compressing floating-point astronomical image or binary-table data into HDF5 and you need a dithered quantization filter comparable to FPACK's scaled-Rice mode, or when benchmarking HDF5 filters (lzf, gzip, bitshuffle) against FITS Rice baselines.

name: floating-point-to-8bit-encoding
description: Use when serving floating-point or 16-bit FITS-derived tiled TIFF science images to HTML5/JavaScript web clients, whose engines can only display gamma-encoded 8-bit-per-channel images and cannot process full bit-depth pixels.

name: flux-rope-internal-property-evolution
description: Use when a ForeCAT terminal CME state (final latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) must be propagated interplanetary space and the analysis needs internal flux rope properties (B, temperature) and expansion/deformation profiles, not just arrival time.

name: flux-rope-magnetic-field-scaling-parameterization
description: Use when a CME simulation input requires an initial flux-rope magnetic field strength (FRB/β_M) and only a hand-assumed value exists, but SDO/AIA 193 and 304 Å post-eruption arcade observations are available to derive it.

name: flux-rope-spacecraft-flythrough-modeling
description: Use when forecasting CME arrival and in situ magnetic field, velocity, or Kp profiles at Earth (or any satellite location) from a magnetogram- and coronagraph-constrained CME ensemble, and when verifying those predictions against OMNI observations.

name: flux-size-plane-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or extending the Upper Sco 12CO flux-size comparison: you have an ALMA survey catalog of 12CO integrated fluxes and CO-disc radii and want to overlay semi-analytical COpops model tracks with CO depletion switched on and off.

name: fmm-gravity-force-computation
description: Use when benchmarking long-range self-gravity for large particle systems, or when verifying that an FMM implementation scales linearly with particle count and quantifying its sensitivity to the MAC angle against a quadratic exact N-body baseline.

name: force-solver-configuration-treepm-fmm
description: Use when validating two cosmological N-body codes (e.g. CONCEPT 1.0 vs gadget-4) against each other on the same initial conditions, or when diagnosing a scale- or time-dependent power discrepancy attributable to the gravitational force solver configuration.

name: fortran-dimension-order-transposition
description: Use when porting an array-based scientific data model with Fortran-order dimensions (e.g. HDS primitives) onto HDF5, so multi-dimensional datasets have correctly transposed dataspace sizes.

name: fortran-executable-build-and-execution
description: Use when a task requires compiling a variant of MOLSCAT/BOUND/FIELD from the molscat/molscat source tree and executing it on an example .input file to generate or verify quantitative outputs such as bound-state energies in cm-1 or Feshbach resonance fields in Gauss.

name: fortran-potential-routine-development
description: Use when a molscat/BOUND/FIELD &POTL potential cannot be expressed as input-data power terms (NPOWER, A) and must instead come from a user-coded routine, or when reproducing a documented model potential (e.g. molscat-basic1) via the plug-in route.

name: fortran-python-wrapped-package-installation
description: Use when a task requires installing a Python scientific package with compiled Fortran 90 core routines (rabacus-style f2py wrapping), where the build needs a Fortran compiler and OpenMP flags before any Python-level import will succeed.

name: fourier-antitransform-power-spectrum-to-2pcf
description: Use when you need to model the angle-averaged redshift-space 2PCF xi(s) of cosmic tracers from a P(k,mu) model, including Gaussian redshift-error damping and de-wiggled BAO treatment.

name: fourier-domain-signal-processing
description: Use when automatically redshifting one-dimensional FITS spectra (e.g. from the AAOmega spectrograph) by cross-correlating continuum-subtracted, RMS-normalised spectra against stellar/galaxy templates in Fourier space.

name: fpack-rice-table-compression
description: Use when comparing lossless compression ratios and I/O throughput of FITS Rice (FPACK -table) versus HDF5 (LZF_SS, bitshuffle) codecs on large astronomical binary-table datasets, or when deciding whether to migrate FITS tables to HDFITS.

name: fractional-error-rms-quantification
description: Use when a fast analytic approximation or emulator must be validated against a high-fidelity reference solver, and accuracy is reported as pointwise fractional difference aggregated to an RMS value.

name: fractional-error-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when validating a fast analytic approximation or emulator against a slower trusted solver by summarizing its accuracy as a single RMS fractional error across sampled inputs.

name: frame-quality-selection-filtering
description: Use when preparing reduced S2D Echelle observations (HARPS, ESPRESSO) for SBART template creation or RV extraction, and you must decide which frames and pixels are trustworthy before co-adding spectra into a stellar template.

name: frame-rejection-quality-control
description: Use when loading S2D spectrograph frames into the SBART DataClass before building stellar templates, and you need to discard low-SNR orders, frames with warning keywords, or flux outliers.

name: frameset-fits-serialization
description: Use when a coordinate conversion Mapping between Frames (e.g. ICRS to Galactic SkyFrames) must be persisted to disk and later re-loaded and validated through AST's FrameSet FITS channels.

name: frameset-mapping-interface-testing
description: Use when testing or documenting coordinate-system library semantics where a container object (FrameSet) exposes both a Mapping interface and mutator access to its contained Frames, and you must confirm that Mapping integrity is preserved after attribute changes.

name: frb-survey-configuration-extraction
description: Use when a paper states a production FRB survey deployment in prose (nodes, GPUs, beams per node, DM count, integration steps) and the goal is to reproduce that allocation as a structured table or CSV.

name: freeze-out-annihilation-cross-section-interpretation
description: Use when a single fixed benchmark dark matter model point needs its thermal freeze-out annihilation cross section evaluated and its relic density (Omega*h^2) computed via DarkBit's Boltzmann-equation integration, rather than a full GAMBIT global scan.

name: frequency-array-problem-specification
description: Use when setting up an oscillatory ODE x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 whose frequency and friction can be sampled or given as arrays/functions before calling pyoscode.solve.

name: frequency-domain-visualisation-of-detector-noise
description: Use when the goal is to characterise detector noise from public GW event strain data (e.g. GW150914 from GWOSC) by transforming time-domain strain into a frequency-domain ASD and rendering it as a figure.

name: full-precision-scientific-image-handling
description: Use when scientific imagery stored as 32-bit floating point or 16-bit data must be visualized in a web browser, because browser engines only display gamma-encoded 8-bit-per-channel images and quantization must be avoided server-side.

name: fully-convolutional-network-inference
description: Use when a headerless two-column stellar spectrum (wavelengths in angstroms, flux in the second column) needs a pseudo-continuum prediction from the SUPP Network before spline-based normalisation or manual correction.

name: fwhm-peak-width-extraction
description: Use when you have stored numerical vs. exact solution profiles (e.g., density in relativistic blast-wave Test 3) at several grid resolutions and need to show that the fluctuation width shrinks toward zero as Δx decreases.

name: gaia-challenge-mock-benchmarking
description: Use when validating or calibrating a stellar-dynamics mass-modeling method on known ground truth, especially to test whether cusped versus cored dark-matter density profiles in dwarf galaxies can be statistically distinguished from discrete tracer kinematics.

name: gaia-dr3-radial-velocity-map-plotting
description: Use when you need to generate or reproduce the local velocity-space distribution and disk-wide median radial velocity maps from a backward-integrated Milky Way model and compare them against Gaia DR3 stellar kinematics.

name: gaia-nearby-source-crossmatching
description: Use when analyzing TESS TPF/FFI photometry of a target whose SPOC aperture may include flux from neighboring Gaia sources, and you need to rank contaminants or test whether any could produce the observed transit depth.

name: gaia-source-identification
description: Use when quantifying which nearby Gaia DR2/DR3 stars contaminate a TESS target's aperture — e.g. a TOI/TIC where flux dilution or false-positive checks require per-source Gaia IDs and inside/outside-aperture flags.

name: galactic-component-stellar-classification
description: Use when the input is a HESTIA (or comparable) hydrodynamical MW-analogue snapshot with per-star metallicity, age, and mass, and the analysis goal requires grouping stars by Galactic component before computing planet occurrence rates.
