name: galactic-disc-component-classification-thick-thin-halo
description: Use when you have a simulated stellar population with per-star metallicity, age, stellar mass, and Galactocentric position, and need to decompose it into bulge, thin disc, thick disc, and halo components before aggregating demographics per region.

name: galactic-dynamics-backward-orbit-integration
description: Use when you need to model Milky Way disk kinematics with a bar and spiral arms constrained by Gaia DR3 radial-velocity features (e.g., the ridges of the local velocity distribution or median Galactocentric radial velocity maps), via backward orbit integration.

name: galactic-kinematics-curve-reconstruction
description: Use when a parametric mass model of a rotationally supported (V/sigma_0 >= 2) axisymmetric disk galaxy must be forward-modelled into an observed 1D rotation curve with beam-smearing corrections for PSF-convolved IFU data.

name: galactic-kinematics-data-parsing
description: Use when you need to quantify the composition of the galkin Milky Way rotation-curve compilation by counting tracer measurements per category (gas, stars, masers) from the raw data file.

name: galactic-model-parameter-extraction
description: Use when the task requires reproducing the reported fiducial parameter table (bar pattern speed 37 km/s/kpc; two-armed spiral at 13.1 km/s/kpc with ~25% local contrast; three-armed spiral at 16.4 km/s/kpc with ~9% local contrast) from published article text.

name: galactic-nonaxisymmetric-potential-fitting
description: Use when reconstructing a non-axisymmetric Galactic potential from Gaia DR3 disk-star kinematics — e.g. matching moving groups, phase-space ridges, or median Galactocentric radial-velocity maps with bar and spiral-arm parameters.

name: galactic-potential-source-term-implementation
description: Use when a solver for the 2-D compressible isothermal Euler equations in a barred galaxy potential must be set up or run, e.g. reproducing g2test or porting the galactic-potential and rotating-bar source terms to another code.

name: galactic-rotation-curve-data-compilation
description: Use when a Milky Way rotation curve normalized to a chosen Galactocentric parameter set is needed, or when reproducing/validating the 2780-measurement galkin compilation between ~3 and 20 kpc.

name: galactic-tracer-data-normalization
description: Use when you need rotation-curve position and velocity data re-parameterised to a chosen Galactocentric parameter set (e.g. R0), starting from galkin's original data_*.dat files, and want output checkable against deposited baseline references.

name: galactic-tracer-spatial-distribution-plotting
description: Use when you have output/vcdata.dat and output/posdata.dat produced by galkin_data.py and need to visualise the tracer spatial distribution and the inferred rotation curve of the Galaxy.

name: galaxy-catalog-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a named-column CSV/TXT catalog of galaxy or supernova-host properties must be explored for pairwise variable relationships before clustering or PCA, and linear, rank-based, and information-theoretic measures are all wanted.

name: galaxy-catalog-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when a high-dimensional galaxy/astronomical catalog in CSV/TXT format with named columns needs dimensionality reduction, and you want PC scores and loadings from either standard correlation-matrix PCA or robust Projection-Pursuit PCA.

name: galaxy-catalogue-handling
description: Use when you need to load a galaxy or simulated halo catalogue (e.g. cat.dat) into CosmoBolognaLib Catalogue objects, build a random catalogue, apply mass/Mmin cuts, or count pairs/triplets for 2PCF/3PCF.

name: galaxy-catalogue-pair-counting
description: Use when the analysis goal is to measure the angular clustering of a galaxy dataset, i.e. produce tabulated w(theta) values over angular separation bins from data and random catalogues.

name: galaxy-catalogue-train-test-splitting
description: Use when a galaxy photometric catalogue (e.g., PHAT0 magnitudes with spectroscopic redshifts) must be partitioned into training/test sets before fitting a photo-z model, so outlier rates are evaluated on unseen galaxies.

name: galaxy-cluster-stellar-mass-fraction-estimation
description: Use when disentangling the gravitational field of X-ray/SZ galaxy clusters into gas, stellar (BCG + satellite), and dark-matter contributions, and you need the radial stellar mass fraction or the radius where stars dominate the field (e.g. inside ~0.02 R500).

name: galaxy-mass-model-construction
description: Use when you need to define a rotationally supported (V/sigma_0 >= 2) axisymmetric disk galaxy's mass components and analytical density profiles as input to forward-model rotation curves or synthetic observations.

name: galaxy-photometric-data-import
description: Use when a tabular catalog of galaxy or supernova host-galaxy photometric properties must be loaded into AMADA for clustering/PCA exploration, and the table needs formatting as named, space-separated CSV/TXT with NA for missing data.

name: galaxy-psf-convolution-image-drawing
description: Use when the task is to generate a synthetic galaxy image with a known surface brightness profile (e.g. Gaussian sigma 2 arcsec, flux 1.e5) convolved with a PSF (sigma 1 arcsec), on a 0.2 arcsec/pixel grid, with specified pixel noise.

name: galaxy-quasar-star-multi-class-classification
description: Use when the task is classifying tabular photometric catalogues (e.g. SDSS DR15+WISE magnitudes of millions of sources) into galaxy/QSO/star classes and per-class F1-scores around 0.96–0.99 are the target benchmark.

name: galaxy-sed-model-space-assembly
description: Use when building a multi-component galaxy SED model from radiative transfer templates (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust) for ultraviolet-to-millimetre fitting, e.g. with SMART or a reimplementation of its component-combination step.

name: galsim-executable-invocation
description: Use when a simulation task must run purely from a config file without Python scripting — e.g. reproducing demo*.yaml images of a Gaussian galaxy convolved with a Gaussian PSF with Gaussian noise.

name: galsim-python-api-scripting
description: Use when you need to generate a synthetic image of a galaxy convolved with a PSF plus Gaussian pixel noise using the GalSim Python API, e.g. to replicate the demo1.py tutorial or build a simple forward-model simulation.

name: gamma-family-glm-fitting
description: Use when photometric redshifts (or any positive, continuous response) must be regressed on magnitude-derived principal components — e.g. PHAT0 or SDSS DR10 catalogues — using a gamma GLM with interaction terms fitted by IRLS.

name: gamma-glm-photoz-regression
description: Use when predicting galaxy photo-z from broadband magnitudes (e.g. PHAT0/PHAT1/SDSS DR10 catalogues) with a fast, statistically principled regression whose predictions must remain non-negative and redshift-dependent in scatter.

name: gamma-glm-regression-with-interaction-terms
description: Use when predicting a positive, continuous target (e.g., galaxy photometric redshift z_phot) from dimensionality-reduced photometric features (principal components of u'g'r'i'z' magnitudes) and a fast, statistically grounded regression is needed.

name: gamma-ray-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when a global-fit or single-point analysis needs a gamma-ray experiment log-likelihood for a dark matter model, and photon yields from annihilation or decay cascades must be produced and compared to experiment data.

name: gamma-ray-spectral-fitting
description: Use when re-analyzing binned Fermi-LAT gamma-ray spectra of a blazar or AGN (e.g. NGC 1275) to search for ALP-induced spectral oscillations via an irregularity statistic rather than ALP model fitting.

name: gamma-ray-spectral-null-baseline-comparison
description: Use when re-analyzing Fermi-LAT (or similar) blazar spectra for ALP-photon conversion effects with an irregularity method, where a no-oscillation reference spectrum must be built instead of fitting ALP models to the observed spectrum.

name: gas-density-profile-reconstruction
description: Use when you have radial/annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (e.g. extracted with pyproffit) and need to deproject them into electron-density and thermodynamic profiles as input to hydrostatic mass reconstruction from X-ray and/or SZ data.

name: gas-giant-atmospheric-composition-analysis
description: Use when you need to map a giant planet's formation history (core mass, initial orbital distance, planetesimal ratio, dust grain fraction) to its final atmospheric C/O ratio and [(X/H)_planet]/[(X/H)_sun] metallicity.

name: gauss-legendre-angular-quadrature-transfer
description: Use when a central point source ionizes a spherical hydrogen cloud and the analysis requires the effect of diffuse recombination photons rather than the on-the-spot approximation, e.g. reproducing the Raičević et al. (2014) Test 1 sphere.

name: gaussian-covariance-sampling
description: Use when you need a synthetic TT/TE/EE (or lensing) band-power data vector consistent with a candl likelihood's covariance — e.g. for forecasting, Fisher/bin-width optimisation studies, or validating a likelihood via chi-squared at the fiducial cosmology.

name: gaussian-noise-addition-to-fits-images
description: Use when simulating an astronomical image that needs realistic pixel-level noise after drawing a galaxy convolved with a PSF, e.g. reproducing demo1-style GalSim outputs with a fixed random seed.

name: gaussian-prior-chi-squared-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when a posterior must be defined numerically before MCMC sampling in CBL: a chi-squared likelihood from model-data comparison plus Gaussian priors on cosmological parameters, to be explored by Metropolis-Hastings or stretch-move samplers.

name: gaussian-prior-specification-cosmological-parameters
description: Use when running an MCMC posterior analysis of Big Bang Nucleosynthesis abundances where neutron lifetime and baryon density must be Gaussian-constrained and nuclear-rate uncertainties propagated log-normally.

name: gaussian-process-kernel-structure-learning
description: Use when a time series (e.g., astronomical light curves of stellar variability or exoplanet transits) must be modelled with a Gaussian Process but no covariance function can be justified a priori, and accurate uncertainty estimation is required.

name: gaussian-process-noise-modelling
description: Use when fitting RV timeseries (e.g. Barnard's star/GJ 699, HARPS-type instruments) where stellar activity or correlated noise may mimic planetary signals and competing noise models (jitter, moving-average, GP) must be compared by Evidence (ln Z).

name: gaussian-process-stellar-activity-modelling
description: Use when 38-point-class HARPS RV time series show correlated stellar activity noise that a plain Keplerian fit cannot absorb, and joint modelling with TESS sectors plus ground-based transits (PEST, TRAPPIST-South) is needed to separate planetary signal from activity jitter.

name: gc-derived-vapour-pressure-data-analysis
description: Use when isothermal GC retention-time data (corrected against a reference such as natural gas) must be converted to vapour pressures, extrapolated below the measured temperature range (e.g. to 20°C from 40–120°C data), or related to molecular descriptors such as MW or intrinsic molar volume.

name: generalized-voigt-parameter-fitting
description: Use when a layered planetary interior model (radii, densities, shear moduli, viscosities) must be replaced by an effective homogeneous Voigt rheology for long-term orbital/spin evolution, or when a reduced model over a prescribed frequency range is needed.

name: genetic-programming-symbolic-regression
description: Use when a fast, interpretable analytic replacement for an expensive numerical solver (e.g. Boltzmann-code power spectra) is needed, and an existing low-accuracy fitting function exists whose ratio to the ground truth can be regressed.

name: gibbs-free-energy-minimisation
description: Use when condensation sequences, 50% condensation temperatures of elements/species, or equilibrium abundances as a function of temperature are needed for a given elemental abundance pattern (e.g. solar, [M/H]-scaled, or star-specific Brewer+2016) at a fixed total pressure.

name: gibbs-free-energy-minimisation-condensation-simulation
description: Use when you need 50% condensation temperatures (Tc) or ∆Tc of major rock-forming elements (e.g. Mg, Si, Fe, Al, Ca, Na, Ni) under a given stellar abundance pattern, or when quantifying how Tc shifts with disk pressure (e.g. 10^-6–0.1 bar) or metallicity.

name: gmres-iterative-linear-solver-configuration
description: Use when running the dst destriper on polarimeter timelines (HDF5 with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U columns) and the baseline-offset linear system must be solved iteratively rather than by direct inversion.

name: gmres-iterative-solver-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when the left-side matrix of the destriping equation is too large to invert directly (e.g. 12-month datasets of ~half a billion samples) and baselines must be solved iteratively with GMRES while monitoring convergence.

name: goodman-weare-ensemble-stretch-move-sampling
description: Use when you need to sample a Bayesian posterior over cosmological model parameters with an ensemble of walkers, e.g. a chi-squared likelihood with Gaussian priors inside the cosmobl::MCMC framework in C++.

name: gp-interpolation-extrapolation-evaluation
description: Use when a time series (e.g. stellar variability) must be modelled with a GP whose covariance structure is learned rather than fixed, and you must verify predictive accuracy and uncertainty coverage for both held-out interpolation points and times beyond the observed window.

name: gp-kernel-computational-cost-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a GP structure-learning pipeline (gallifrey, JAX backend) can handle larger time series, or when benchmarking runtime/memory scaling of SMC-based posterior approximation.

name: gp-kernel-structure-learning
description: Use when a time series (e.g. stellar variability, exoplanet transit light curve, transmission spectroscopy) requires GP regression but no suitable fixed covariance kernel is known, and accurate predictive accuracy plus uncertainty estimation are needed.

name: gps-time-interval-querying
description: Use when the analysis target is public GWOSC strain data (e.g. GW150914) for a known GPS time interval and no channel name or authentication path is available.

name: gps-time-window-selection
description: Use when an analysis needs a time-bounded slice of strain data around a catalogued GW event, expressed in GPS seconds, before downloading via GWpy's remote-data access into a TimeSeries.

name: gpu-chemistry-emulator-speedup-quantification
description: Use when a trained neural-ODE chemistry surrogate (e.g. from the neuralpdr repo) must be shown to beat the original 3D-PDR solver in wall-clock time, and per-case speedup factors need to be tabulated.

name: gpu-cosmological-computation
description: Use when you need GPU-accelerated cosmological quantities — an aperture mass map from a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog, or the 2-pt angular correlation function w(theta) of a galaxy catalog — via the ccogs packages.

name: gpu-cpu-reference-numerical-verification
description: Use when a new or modified GPU kernel in Montblanc (e.g. an EK-kernel source loop) must be proven numerically correct against an independent CPU reference before its per-antenna terms and chi-squared can be trusted for BIRO use.

name: gpu-kernel-occupancy-metric-interpretation
description: Use when you have NVIDIA Profiler output for CUDA kernels and need to transcribe and interpret per-kernel register usage, block size, and achieved occupancy, or to reconcile theoretical memory-boundness with profiled compute/memory behavior.

name: gpu-speedup-data-tabulation
description: Use when a source card asks you to reproduce quantitative GPU speedup results from a paper figure (e.g., Figure 5) for multiple reaction networks and grid sizes, and the deliverable is a structured table with a limitations column.

name: gpu-vs-cpu-speedup-tabulation
description: Use when a paper reports per-problem-size wall-clock timings for two or more implementations (e.g. Montblanc on an NVIDIA K40 vs OSKAR's GPU RIME on the same K40 vs MeqTrees on a dual hexacore Intel E5-2620v2 CPU) and the ratios must be tabulated and validated.

name: gradient-based-nuts-mcmc-sampling
description: Use when you need posterior samples from a differentiable CMB power-spectrum likelihood (e.g. candl SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) and want NUTS sampling driven by exact JAX gradients of the log-likelihood.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-regression
description: Use when tabular photometric survey data (e.g. SDSS+WISE magnitudes/fluxes) lacks a redshift value that is needed as a regression target or downstream feature, and a per-source photo-z estimate must be produced by an ensemble of gradient-boosted regressors.

name: gradient-boosting-ensemble-training
description: Use when classifying large tabular photometric catalogues (e.g. ~3.5M SDSS+WISE sources) into galaxies, quasars, and stars and a single gradient-boosting model is insufficient — an ensemble of XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost outputs is needed.

name: gravitational-potential-topology-saddle-point-analysis
description: Use when particles in a cosmological N-body snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) must be labelled bound vs unbound using only instantaneous information, without overdensity thresholds or iterative unbinding.

name: gravitational-wave-bayesian-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you have gravitational-wave strain data plus electromagnetic counterpart observations (kilonova photometry, GRB afterglow light curves) and need joint posterior samples over EOS/ejecta parameters, or when comparing posteriors from nested analyses (e.g. GW+KN-only vs GW+KN+GRB).

name: gravitational-wave-event-mass-selection
description: Use when you have a COMPAS DoubleCompactObjects table of merging BBHs and need to identify which simulated systems match the 90% credible intervals of specific observed gravitational-wave events.

name: gravitational-wave-event-progenitor-matching
description: Use when you must match specific observed BBH events (90% credible intervals on chirp/component masses and mass ratio) to progenitor binaries in COMPAS double-compact-object populations at particular metallicities (solar, Z=0.002, Z=0.001).

name: gravitational-wave-likelihood-generation
description: Use when a joint multi-messenger analysis (GW + kilonova + GRB afterglow) needs the gravitational-wave likelihood precomputed via NMMA before running nmma-analysis; triggered by GW strain data for events like GW170817.

name: gravitational-wave-open-data-access
description: Use when an analysis needs public LIGO/Virgo strain or event data (e.g. GW150914 from GWOSC) and it must be retrieved remotely into a TimeSeries object before frequency-domain or visualisation steps.

name: gravitational-wave-strain-data-handling
description: Use when you need to download public GWOSC strain data for a LIGO/Virgo event — given only an interferometer prefix and a GPS start/stop interval — into a time-domain TimeSeries object in Python.

name: gravitational-waveform-surrogate-evaluation
description: Use when waveform generation cost dominates an analysis (e.g., parameter estimation or parameter-space exploration) and fast, accurate evaluation of effective-one-body or NR-trained surrogate models is needed.

name: gravitational-waveform-time-series-validation
description: Use when a surrogate or reduced-basis model predicts gravitational waveform time series at arbitrary parameter values and you must verify accuracy against the fiducial solver and quantify online evaluation cost/speedup before trusting predictions.

name: grb-afterglow-jet-model-fitting
description: Use when a GRB afterglow light-curve data set (e.g., multi-band GRB170817A afterglow measurements) must be modeled with a structured-jet afterglow model and incorporated into joint multi-messenger Bayesian inference.

name: greedy-reduced-basis-construction
description: Use when you have a dense training set of expensive fiducial waveforms (e.g., 501 EOBNRv2 (2,2)-mode waveforms with q in [1,2] generated by the EOB-LAL code) and need a surrogate whose greedy error decays exponentially so m << L basis elements suffice.

name: grid-resolution-convergence-tabulation
description: Use when a numerical-vs-exact solution pair is available at multiple grid resolutions and you need a tabulated, visual convergence indicator (FWHM of the fluctuation tending toward zero).

name: gw-event-analog-rate-tabulation
description: Use when a single binary-evolution parameter (e.g. common-envelope efficiency alphalambda) is varied against a Fiducial COMPAS model and you need per-metallicity drop factors for total and event-analog BBH merger rates plus max-BBH-mass shifts.

name: gwosc-strain-data-loading
description: Use when a workflow must ingest a public GWOSC strain file (e.g. HDF5 covering the GW150914 window GPS 1126259446-1126259478) into GWpy's TimeSeries and surface the attached I/O metadata.

name: h5part-particle-snapshot-extraction
description: Use when FleCSPH hydro_{1-2-3}d or newtonian_3d drivers have written H5part particle snapshot files and you need to extract per-particle position, density, and velocity to compute radial, azimuthal, or shock profiles for validation.

name: halo-assembly-bias-quantification
description: Use when you have per-halo mass accretion histories (or diffmah fits) plus halo positions and a large-scale density field from a simulation (e.g. TNG), and need to measure assembly bias or validate an assembly-history model's residuals.

name: halo-mass-accretion-history-fitting
description: Use when you have halo merger tree catalogs (e.g., TNG, gravity-only simulations) and need compact per-halo parametric fits of log halo mass vs. cosmic time for host halos or subhalos above 10^11 Msun.

name: halo-mass-function-computation
description: Use when a task requires calculating the differential (dndlnm) or cumulative (ngtm) halo mass function for a CDM or WDM cosmology, comparing fitting functions f(sigma), or quantifying WDM suppression of low-mass haloes relative to a CDM baseline.

name: halo-mass-function-model-computation
description: Use when estimating halo number density dn/dM on a mass grid or comparing halo mass function and halo bias models at a fixed cosmology, e.g. for halo occupation or cluster-count modelling.

name: halo-particle-boundness-classification
description: Use when an N-body/hydro snapshot (e.g. HDF5 particle data) contains halo candidates whose membership needs a physically motivated bound/unbound split, or when testing whether bound and unbound halo populations are distinct components.

name: halo-particle-phase-space-labeling
description: Use when you need per-particle bound/unbound labels for dark matter haloes in a cosmological N-body snapshot (positions, velocities, masses, e.g. HDF5 particle data) using only instantaneous information.

name: hamiltonian-monte-carlo-bayesian-inference
description: Use when reconstructing hydrostatic mass profiles or fitting parametric mass models (NFW, Einasto) to X-ray surface brightness, spectroscopic temperature, and SZ pressure profiles under a global Bayesian framework with posterior uncertainties.

name: hardware-configuration-metadata-extraction
description: Use when a paper reports benchmark or performance runs on a named many-core/GPU platform (e.g., NERSC Cori Xeon Phi) and you must turn prose like 'all runs used 4 hardware threads per core' into a validated machine-readable record.

name: harps-spectral-data-ingestion
description: Use when starting a template-matching RV analysis on ESO HARPS archival S2D FITS observations (e.g. of Barnard's star) and a quality-controlled frame set must be loaded into SBART before template building.

name: hdf5-backend-integration
description: Use when an existing HDS API client must read both legacy HDSv4 files and new HDF5-backed HDSv5 files transparently, without modifying application code.

name: hdf5-chunked-io-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify I/O read performance differences between FITS and HDF5 (chunked, optionally bitshuffle-compressed) for full-file vs. random slice access on large 3D scientific arrays.

name: hdf5-chunked-lossless-compression
description: Use when large (>500 MB) binary-table FITS files must be compressed losslessly and you need to choose between FITS Rice, HDF5 LZF_SS, and HDF5 bitshuffle by measuring compression ratio and speed.

name: hdf5-core-driver-in-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure the single-core compute throughput of a chunked HDF5-based transform (e.g. rounding precision reduction) without confounding disk I/O, or to validate throughput claims against published MiB/s figures.

name: hdf5-dataset-access
description: Use when opening Starlink HDS/NDF-format data through the HDF5-backed HDSv5 API (e.g. loading a large multi-GB dataset into GAIA) or when benchmarking load time and resident memory with datMap memory mapping enabled vs disabled.

name: hdf5-dataset-loading
description: Use when a downstream task needs the processed 3D-PDR chemistry data (chemical abundances, temperatures, densities, cosmic ray ionisation rates, Av, radiation field) as HDF5 input for LANODE surrogate training, inference, or benchmarking.

name: hdf5-file-identifier-tracking
description: Use when reimplementing an API layer over HDF5 whose locators must preserve HDS-style primary/secondary semantics, deciding when a file can actually be closed.

name: hdf5-filter-compression-evaluation
description: Use when a user needs to benchmark lossless compression filters — FITS Rice, HDF5 LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP — on synthetic random-integer image grids and reproduce a ratio-vs-time comparison table.

name: hdf5-snapshot-analysis
description: Use when a Dedalus simulation run has produced HDF5 snapshot files through its analysis/simulation output handlers and the goal is to extract named task fields (density, vorticity, buoyancy w, potential vorticity p) and compare or render them at specific simulation times.

name: hdf5-solution-output-handling
description: Use when a multi-stage Dedalus workflow must pass intermediate solver state (e.g., a solved static atmosphere background) from one stage (NLBVP Newton solve) to another (eigenvalue solves) via files.

name: hdf5-timeline-io
description: Use when raw or simulated polarimeter timelines (e.g. B-Machine channel 6 at 33.4 Hz) must be stored or loaded for the dst destriper, or when adapting a new dataset to dst's HDF5 input format.

name: hdf5-timestream-format-assembly
description: Use when timelines (TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U) from a CMB polarimeter such as B-Machine or a LATTE-scale simulation must be serialized into the single HDF5 file format dst expects.

name: hdfits-file-io
description: Use when FITS files (e.g. SDSS images, radio-interferometric data) need to be converted to HDF5 for faster reads or compression, or when an HDFITS file must be emitted back as FITS for legacy software.

name: hdfits-roundtrip-validation
description: Use when converting FITS or MeasurementSet data into HDF5/HDFITS (or back) and you must verify the converted file is scientifically identical — e.g. before adopting HDF5 storage or benchmarking compression filters against the FITS baseline.

name: hds-api-dispatch-wrapping
description: Use when you must support both legacy HDS v4 files and new HDF5-backed HDS v5 files behind one drop-in HDS API, and need a dispatch mechanism that routes each API call based on the locator's file version.

name: hds-group-flush-implementation
description: Use when reimplementing HDS file-close semantics over HDF5: you must decide when an HDF5 file can be closed given multiple locators, named groups, and datPrmry promotions.

name: hds-hdf5-file-format-conversion
description: Use when legacy HDS/HDSv4 astronomy data files (NDF images, ADAM parameter files, SCUBA-2 acquisition files) must be written or re-expressed as HDF5 via the HDSv5 drop-in library, or when comparing HDSv4 vs HDSv5 file sizes.

name: hds-hdf5-library-benchmark-execution
description: Use when comparing wall-clock performance of two drop-in file-format library builds — native HDSv4 versus the HDF5-backed hds-v5 — using the Starlink starbench, ccdpack, ccdbig and SCUBA-2 orac-dr benchmarks.

name: hds-locator-lifecycle-management
description: Use when reimplementing or porting the HDS API onto HDF5 and you must decide when a file can be closed given multiple outstanding locators, or implement locator-group behavior (hdsLink/hdsFlush) and datPrmry promotion.

name: hds-to-hdf5-data-model-mapping
description: Use when reconstructing how an HDS structure (structures, primitives, _CHAR*24 strings, _INTEGER, _LOGICAL, arrays of structures) is represented in an HDF5 file, or when building/validating an HDS-equivalent .h5 hierarchy with h5dump.

name: hdu-group-attribute-serialization
description: Use when converting FITS files (or MeasurementSets) into the HDFITS HDF5 format and the FITS hierarchy of HDUs, headers, images, and binary-table columns must be preserved as groups, datasets, and attributes.

name: healpix-fits-map-loading
description: Use when the input is a HEALPix FITS map of polarized CMB data (Q/U) that must be loaded into healpy for partial-sky analysis, e.g. B-Machine destriped Nside 512 maps from figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.644507.

name: healpix-gnomonic-projection
description: Use when a HEALPix full-sky map (e.g. B-Machine destriped I/Q/U FITS maps) must be converted to small projected patches centered on a known point source for flux measurement or visual inspection.

name: healpix-map-binning
description: Use when a scanned timestream with per-sample sky coordinates (e.g. TIME/PHI/THETA/PSI columns in an HDF5 file) must be projected onto a HEALPix Nside 256/512 map, either as a plain-binned baseline or as the binning operator for destriping.

name: healpix-partial-sky-anafast-analysis
description: Use when you have partial-sky Q/U (or T) maps in HEALPix FITS format plus a hitcount map, and you need to validate map noise properties by comparing measured EE/BB spectra to a white-noise prediction.

name: healpix-pointing-generation
description: Use when simulating a polarimeter timestream that requires a realistic scanning strategy (fixed elevation, sky rotation) converted into HEALPix PHI/THETA/PSI pointing columns for map-making or destriping.

name: heavy-element-accretion-mode-parameterization
description: Decision support for interpreting a formed giant planet's atmospheric C/O ratio in terms of the dominant source of accreted heavy elements (dust grains vs. planetesimals).

name: hermite-cubic-spline-interpolation
description: Use when irregularly sampled time series must be turned into a continuous control path for a neural CDE, especially the 2D spiral classification setup, and a smooth interpolation with good measurability is needed.

name: hidden-state-decay-dynamics-interpretation
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a discrete recurrent architecture (GRU) is the Euler discretisation of a continuous-time system, or to interpret hidden-state dynamics such as the exponential decay implied by the -h(t) term.

name: hierarchical-clustering-correlation-distance
description: Use when you need to reveal hidden multi-level structure among variables (or objects) in a high-dimensional galaxy-catalog or photometric table without pre-specifying the number of clusters.

name: hierarchical-clustering-cut-selection
description: Use when a dendrogram from AMADA's hierarchical clustering must be cut into a partition, and no prior number of clusters is specified — the Calinski-Harabasz index guides the cut height choice.

name: hierarchical-clustering-dendrogram-plotting
description: Use when you need a tree representation of hidden structure among variables of a high-dimensional astronomical dataset (e.g. SDSS supernova hosts, Millennium mock catalogs, ZENS groups) and an optimal cluster count without pre-specifying it.

name: hierarchical-leapfrog-timestepping-implementation
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing adaptive, individual-particle time integration in an N-body cosmology code, specifically the multi-rung leapfrog schedule and rung-assignment criterion of CONCEPT 1.0.

name: hierarchical-n-body-simulation-configuration
description: Use when simulating hierarchical astrophysical systems (e.g. star clusters hosting planetary systems or binary stars) with extreme scale separations, where direct N-body integration is too costly and subsystem isolation with Ph4/Huayno is appropriate.

name: highcharts-point-selection-linking
description: Use when a custom Toyz tile must display cutout images and surface plots for point sources selected (clicked or drag-boxed) in a Highcharts plot sharing the same data source.

name: highcharts-series-data-source-binding
description: Use when you need browser-based interactive scatter/line plots from a shared tabular dataset on a remote server, and want selecting points in one chart to highlight the same points in every chart derived from that source.

name: hillshade-relief-rendering
description: Use when the input is a digital elevation model (DEM) height channel stored as full 32-bit TIFF tiles in an IIPImage multi-resolution pyramid and the goal is a hill-shaded relief rendering with a user-adjustable light-source incidence angle.

name: hitomi-perseus-results-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking Bayesian X-ray spectral fitting on high-resolution calorimeter data (e.g. the Hitomi Perseus cluster observation) and the goal is a GPU variational-inference fit that completes in under 10 minutes while matching published Hitomi parameters.

name: hitran-fixed-width-record-handling
description: Use when an ExoMol (or ExoMolHR/ExoAtom) line list must be emitted in HITRAN/HITEMP format over a defined wavenumber range, e.g. ConversionFormat=HITRAN with ConversionFrequncyRange 0–30000 cm-1.

name: hll-riemann-solver-flux-computation
description: Use when a hyperbolic conservative system (e.g. 1D SRHD with charges q=(D,Sx,τ)) needs cell-interface numerical fluxes without solving an algebraic primitive-recovery polynomial per cell and time step.

name: hll-riemann-solver-implementation
description: Use when a finite-volume HRSC solver for hyperbolic conservation laws (e.g. 1D special relativistic hydrodynamics shock-tube problems) needs a numerical flux at cell interfaces given qL, qR and characteristic speeds λL, λR.

name: hm12-uv-background-initialization
description: Use when a radiative-transfer run needs a homogeneous isotropic UV background (e.g. grey_fixT_B, hm12_fixT_B, hm12_evoT_B/A/rt models) and you must build and verify the HM12 photorates table before feeding the solvers.

name: hmc-posterior-sampling-for-cluster-profiles
description: Use when reconstructing hydrostatic mass profiles and deprojecting gas thermodynamic profiles from X-ray (surface brightness, spectroscopic temperature) and/or Sunyaev-Zeldovich pressure data for galaxy clusters.

name: hmi-magnetogram-availability-checking
description: Use when configuring an OSPREI/ForeCAT simulation and you must confirm a usable HMI synchronic magnetogram exists in the JSOC catalog for the eruption date, applying the day-before fallback rule when the eruption occurs before the magnetogram time.

name: host-and-subhalo-sample-selection
description: Use when building the per-halo fitting sample for diffmah MAH fits: selecting both host halos and subhalos with present-day mass greater than 10^11 Msun from merger tree catalogs such as TNG.

name: host-galaxy-candidate-filtering
description: Use when preparing galaxy-only catalog samples around transient sky localisations (e.g. from a Transient_sources.ecsv file) prior to computing chance-alignment probabilities, and stars must be removed from Pan-STARRS or HSC catalog data.

name: host-galaxy-contamination-subtraction
description: Use when a transient spectrum from an IFS cube is contaminated by host-galaxy light — e.g. the transient lies near the host core (~30% of SEDm observations show severe contamination) and an isolated point-source extractor would yield biased or unclassifiable spectra.

name: host-model-cube-astrometric-registration
description: Use when a square-pixel photometric host model (e.g. PS1, 0.50 arcsec pixels after 2x2 rebinning) must be remapped onto mismatched integral-field-spectrograph spaxels (SEDm hexagonal 0.558 arcsec spaxels) per monochromatic slice.

name: hot-jupiter-atmospheric-configuration
description: Use when you need to reproduce the ExoLyn baseline hot-Jupiter cloud-structure solve, or measure wall-clock runtime of a single relaxation run to validate the few-seconds performance claim.

name: hpc-core-count-sweep-execution
description: Use when you need to measure or predict how the wall time of a parallelised sampling or simulation workflow scales with the number of cores/nodes, e.g. planning cloud (EC2) or grid budgets for MCMC runs.

name: hpc-performance-benchmarking
description: Decision support for quantifying HPC solver performance of a parallel destriping pipeline — e.g. when asking whether the destriping matrix is too heavy to invert directly and how baselines can instead be estimated iteratively for large parallel runs.

name: hpc-strong-scaling-interpretation
description: Use when a benchmark figure or table reports GPU/node scaling for an AMReX astrophysics code (e.g., Figure 4 of the Castro/Maestro paper: Star Lord on Summitdev) and the goal is to characterize speedup behavior and GPU-vs-CPU performance ratios.

name: hsc-extended-flag-galaxy-classification
description: Use when preparing an HSC galaxy catalog for transient host-galaxy association (e.g. galclaim / Association_pval.py) and you need to keep only extended (galaxy) sources, since HSC requires no extra star/galaxy separation beyond its provided extended flag.

name: html5-canvas-pixel-level-color-compositing
description: Use when an interactive web client must composite multi-band planetary/astronomy tile images on demand, and per-tile processing time (target: 1–3 ms per 256×256 tile) must be measured in-browser.

name: http-load-benchmarking-of-tile-servers
description: Use when sizing or validating a web tile server for scientific imagery: you need requests-per-second and per-request latency scaling with concurrency, or a user-capacity figure (e.g. ~100 users on a 12-core server).

name: hybrid-vlasov-simulation-configuration
description: Use when the task requires setting up and executing Vlasiator simulations (e.g., 1D collisionless shock runs at 1000 km or 200 km grid resolution, low-β wave tests, or multi-population proton/O+ configurations) and analysing .vlsv outputs.

name: hybrid-vlasov-solver-implementation
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing a (hybrid-)Vlasov solver that must propagate an ion velocity distribution function noiselessly and couple it to electromagnetic fields, following Vlasiator's documented numerical design.

name: hydrocarbon-analogue-substitution-for-tin-centre
description: Use when estimating vapour pressures (or other hydrocarbon-derived physicochemical properties) of organostannanes at environmentally relevant temperatures (e.g. 20°C) where no direct hydrocarbon-based QSPR exists for the Sn-centred compound.

name: hydrocarbon-reference-data-compilation
description: Use when fitting a structure-property regression (lnP or ΔHv vs intrinsic molar volume) that must merge experimentally measured organostannane data with published hydrocarbon values, and when validating against a reported single-relationship equation.

name: hydrogen-ionization-equilibrium-slab-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or validating plane-parallel (slab) hydrogen ionization equilibrium solutions against a closed-form analytic solution, or when benchmarking the Slab_Pln solver near the ionization front.

name: hydrogen-ionization-equilibrium-solving
description: Use when you need equilibrium ionization/temperature profiles or column densities for H/He gas under a central point source, an isotropic UV background (e.g. HM12), or single-zone conditions, and must choose between case A, case B (on-the-spot), or full recombination radiation transfer.

name: hydrogen-recombination-line-emissivity-calculation
description: Use when you need to compute hydrogen recombination line emissivities (Balmer, Paschen, Brackett) or excited-state (n, l) population densities from nebular gas conditions (electron/proton/neutral H densities and temperature).

name: hydrostatic-mass-profile-reconstruction
description: Use when you have joint X-ray (surface brightness + spectroscopic temperature) and SZ pressure profiles for galaxy clusters and need hydrostatic mass profiles with posterior uncertainties, via nonparametric or parametric reconstruction.

name: hypercube-dimension-array-registration
description: Use when constructing a Montblanc solver problem (e.g. adding new source types or testing the EK/B Sum pipeline) and you must define named dimensions, extents, and the arrays tiled by SourceProvider data sources.

name: hypercube-memory-budgeted-problem-subdivision
description: Use when a RIME (or similarly dimension-parallel) GPU computation exceeds a supplied memory budget and must still yield one χ2 value; triggered by large ntime/nchan/npsrc hypercube dimensions that force time-dimension tiling with asynchronous transfers.

name: hyperspectral-host-cube-generation
description: Use when you need a spectrally-resolved host galaxy cube from archival broadband photometry (e.g. PS1 grizy cutouts) to serve as a fixed background template for IFS scene modeling or transient subtraction.

name: iae-decoder-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to justify replacing a physical (look-up-table) spectral model with a learned surrogate by measuring wall-clock inference cost per call for both models in a common environment.

name: iae-reconstruction-residual-analysis
description: Use when trained IAE spectral models are available and you need to verify their generative reconstruction quality on held-out spectra before using them as surrogates in SUSHI unmixing.

name: iae-spectral-surrogate-modeling
description: Use when a physical spectral model (e.g. APEC via XSpec look-up tables) is too slow or non-differentiable for per-pixel hyperspectral fitting, and you need a learned, differentiable spectral decoder for components like thermal and synchrotron emission.

name: ice-line-crossing-abundance-analysis
description: Use when studying how initial formation location (inside the H2O ice line, between H2O and CO ice lines, or beyond the CO ice line) determines the final C/O ratio of a gas giant's atmosphere in SimAb-style models.

name: icrs-to-galactic-mapping-verification
description: Use when an analysis needs a validated celestial coordinate transformation between ICRS (RA,Dec) and Galactic (l,b) frames and requires proof that the AST-generated Mapping round-trips through FITS and yields finite, in-range outputs.

name: ifeffit-compatible-xafs-procedure-reproduction
description: Use when processing raw XAS/XAFS spectra (e.g. ASCII energy/mu files like fe.060) to produce normalized mu(E) and background-subtracted chi(k), and when IFEFFIT-equivalent procedure semantics matter.

name: ifu-beam-convolution-of-kinematics
description: Use when a 1D rotation curve from IFU observations must be compared to a disk+bulge+halo mass model, and instrumental beam smearing (PSF convolution) must be applied to the model before fitting.

name: ifu-hexagonal-spaxel-grid-geometry
description: Use when resampling a square-pixel photometric model cube (e.g. PS1 0.50 arcsec pixels after 2x2 rebinning) onto a hexagonal IFS spaxel grid (e.g. SEDm 0.558 arcsec spaxels) per monochromatic slice, with mismatched pixel geometries and a transient position as spatial anchor.

name: iip-protocol-command-implementation
description: Use when serving floating-point tiled TIFF astronomy imagery to a web client and dynamic channel mixing, gamma, min/max cuts or pixel profiles must be computed from full bit-depth data rather than the browser's 8-bit display pipeline.

name: iipsrv-tile-server-deployment
description: Use when serving gigapixel-scale 32-bit floating point scientific TIFFs to browser clients via on-the-fly 256x256 JPEG tile generation, or benchmarking server-side tile-processing stages under different storage and cache configurations.

name: image-rebinning-resampling
description: Use when FITS science rasters must be transcoded into a tiled multi-resolution TIFF pyramid (e.g. for serving with the IIPImage server in the VisiOmatic web visualization stack) via successive 2×2 rebinning.

name: incremental-sfm-3d-reconstruction
description: Use when a synthetic fly-by image sequence (e.g., 25 pinhole-camera images rendered with SISPO/Blender Cycles from a known shape model such as 25143 Itokawa) must be turned into camera poses and a 3-D model whose deviation from the ground-truth model is reported as Gaussian error statistics.

name: independent-sample-efficiency-quantification
description: Use when comparing MCMC/HMC sampler efficiency between two implementations run on the same fitting problem, to decide which sampler (e.g. stan vs emcee) delivers more independent posterior draws per step.

name: indirect-detection-experiment-configuration
description: Use when you need an indirect-detection (gamma-ray) likelihood for a dark matter model point under a specific current experiment, e.g. reproducing gamLike likelihoods inside a GAMBIT scan.

name: inflationary-background-root-finding
description: Use when integrating an inflationary background with pyoscode and you must locate the moment epsilon = 1 (end of inflation) before setting Bunch-Davies initial conditions and evaluating Mukhanov-Sasaki modes at horizon exit.

name: inflationary-potential-parameter-to-observable-mapping
description: Use when you need reheating-consistent n_s and r predictions from a specified single-field inflationary potential and its parameter values, e.g. for comparison with cosmological data or Bayesian model comparison.

name: inflationary-slow-roll-observable-computation
description: Use when you need reheating-consistent slow-roll predictions (n_s, r, number of e-folds) for one or more of the 74 single-field inflationary models supported by ASPIC, or when building libaspic from source.

name: infrared-dark-cloud-image-analysis
description: Use when you have a sample of FITS images (e.g. Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark clouds) and need label-free morphological embeddings for clustering, anomaly detection, or similarity-based exploration.

name: infrared-spectral-rebinning
description: Use when mid/far-infrared spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer IRS) must be included in an SED fit whose model library components (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust) are pre-computed on a coarser spectral resolution grid.

name: inice-medium-propagation-setup
description: Use when a NuRadioMC simulation must specify the in-ice propagation medium and ray tracer (e.g., a firn index-of-refraction profile) so Askaryan signals travel from the interaction vertex to the detector.

name: initial-condition-parameter-specification
description: Use when running SimAb in single-simulation mode and you must map a target mature planet (mass, final orbital distance) onto a full set of initial formation parameters before invoking Srun.py.

name: initial-condition-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when model–data agreement for CO fluxes of a disc sample is inconclusive and you need to test whether uncertainties in the model's initial conditions (disc initial mass and radius) limit the interpretation of the observations.

name: insitu-probability-contour-plotting
description: Use when a completed OSPREI ensemble run (nRuns > 1) has produced standardized output files and you need probability visualizations of FIDO in situ properties or ensemble correlations rather than raw data files.

name: instrument-response-convolution
description: Use when generating simulated IXPE event lists from a source model (e.g. a power-law spectrum with constant polarization degree/angle) plus IRF definitions identified by IRFNAME/CALDB keywords, and the count spectrum must be produced by convolution with the instrument response.

name: integer-visibility-precision-reduction
description: Use when handling large integer visibility datasets (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder correlator output) where information entropy must be reduced before lossless compression without measurably increasing thermal noise.

name: integral-field-spectroscopy-scene-modeling
description: Use when a transient spectrum must be extracted from an IFS data cube (e.g. SEDm) and the transient lies near its host galaxy core, so standard isolated point-source extraction suffers host-galaxy contamination.

name: interaction-term-model-formulation
description: Use when building a photometric redshift regression from PCA-reduced galaxy magnitudes where a simple additive formula fails to capture the data's complexity and interaction terms among PCs are required.

name: interactive-plot-selection-propagation-verification
description: Use when multiple interactive Highcharts tiles in a Toyz workspace share one registered tabular data source and you must confirm that selecting a point in one chart selects the same points in all other charts from that source.

name: interferometer-prefix-channel-identification
description: Use when the analysis goal is to download public GWOSC strain data for a known event (e.g. GW150914) and you must decide whether to supply an interferometer prefix plus GPS interval rather than an instrument channel name.

name: interferometric-uv-data-handling
description: Use when you have a parametric radial brightness profile (e.g. '-p 0.013 1.07 0.06 0.01' style parameters) for a circumstellar disc and need model visibilities at sampled u,v points without rendering images.

name: interpolated-solution-grid-alignment
description: Use when comparing outputs of two cosmological solvers (or any two ODE solutions) that were sampled on different grids and you need per-quantity maximum-error validation against a documented tolerance.

name: interpolatory-autoencoder-decoding
description: Use when a hyperspectral (IFU) unmixing problem needs a differentiable spectral model per physical component — e.g. APEC thermal plasma or synchrotron power-law spectra convolved with Chandra ARF/RMF responses — and the physical model itself is too slow or non-differentiable for optimization.

name: intrinsic-molar-volume-fragment-additivity
description: Use when you have vapour pressure (lnP, kPa) data for chemically heterogeneous compound classes (e.g. hydrocarbons plus organometallics like tetraorganostannanes) and need a single unified QSPR descriptor or a structural predictor of P.

name: intrinsic-molar-volume-qspr-verification
description: Use when testing whether a property of organometallic compounds (e.g. ΔHv or lnP of tetraorganostannanes) is better predicted by intrinsic molar volume than by molecular weight, or when validating that hydrocarbon-derived QSPRs transfer to organostannanes.

name: involutive-mcmc-transition-kernel-construction
description: Use when the GP covariance function cannot be fixed a priori for a time series (e.g. stellar variability or exoplanet transit flux data) and the kernel structure itself must be inferred as a latent discrete variable via SMC with involutive MCMC transitions.

name: ionization-front-relative-difference-quantification
description: Use when validating a plane-parallel radiative-transfer solver against a known closed-form solution, i.e. when you have both a numerical and an analytic ionization-fraction profile as a function of column depth and need to quantify their agreement near the ionization front.

name: irls-factorial-model-fitting
description: Use when predicting galaxy photo-zs from magnitude-derived principal components and you need a fast regression that respects the positive, right-skewed redshift distribution via gamma regression with a log link.

name: irregular-time-series-interpolation
description: Use when observations arrive at irregular timestamps (e.g. decaying-oscillator series sampled non-uniformly over [0,3]) and a continuous path must be constructed before solving a neural differential equation.

name: iterated-reweighted-least-squares-fitting
description: Use when predicting positive, continuous responses such as galaxy photo-z from PCA-reduced u'g'r'i'z' magnitudes via a gamma GLM whose covariates must be estimated by likelihood maximisation with IRLS.

name: iterative-polynomial-continuum-subtraction
description: Use when preparing AAOmega-format FITS spectra (flux + variance + wavelength extensions) for redshift cross-correlation, and the continuum must be removed so matching operates on emission/absorption features rather than the continuum shape.

name: ixpe-level2-fits-event-list-handling
description: Use when the analysis starts from public IXPE level-2 filtered event lists downloaded from HEASARC and needs event positions (DETX/DETY) or per-event attributes extracted in Python/ixpeobssim for spatial, spectral, or temporal (polarization-aware) analysis.

name: ixpeobssim-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when you need to generate simulated IXPE observations or an ensemble of realizations of a fixed-duration exposure (e.g. 1000 realizations of 50 ks) with FITS event lists and binned polarization products as outputs.

name: jackknife-covariance-estimation
description: Use when you have a galaxy catalogue (real or simulated) and need covariance/error estimates for 2PCF measurements via jackknife, bootstrap, or lognormal mock resampling of survey sub-regions.

name: jax-accelerated-probabilistic-programming
description: Use when a Bayesian model (e.g. GP structure learning over discrete kernel structures plus continuous hyperparameters) requires sampling-intensive inference and Python/JAX is available to JIT-compile the SMC and MCMC kernels.

name: jax-automatic-differentiation-derivatives
description: Use when you need parameter-derivative quantities from a CMB power-spectrum likelihood — Fisher matrices, parameter covariance, or gradient-based optimisation/sampling — and want exact derivatives rather than finite-difference estimates.

name: jax-diffrax-ode-solve-configuration
description: Use when a numerical differential-equation model must be solved in JAX — e.g. verifying that a discrete recurrence (GRU) matches an Euler-discretised continuous-time system, or training a neural CDE on interpolated control paths with adaptive step sizes.

name: jax-hessian-fisher-matrix-computation
description: Use when you need parameter forecasts or uncertainty estimates from a CMB power spectrum likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) and want robust derivatives without finite-difference step-size tuning.

name: jeans-equation-bin-free-fitting
description: Use when you have discrete stellar tracer positions and velocities (LOS-only or LOS+PM) for an equilibrium spherical system and need an unbiased recovery of the density profile, its logarithmic slope at R1/2, anisotropy, dispersion, or kurtosis without binning.

name: jeans-equation-mass-modeling
description: Use when you have discrete (unbinned) stellar tracer positions and line-of-sight and/or proper-motion velocities for a system assumed to be in equilibrium and approximately spherical, and you need posterior mass density, anisotropy, or log-slope profiles with credible intervals.

name: joint-photometric-rv-bayesian-inference
description: Use when combining radial velocities and transit light curves (space + ground) to derive planet mass, radius, and orbital parameters with Bayesian evidence-based model comparison and posterior credible intervals.

name: jupyter-notebook-reproducible-execution
description: Use when a paper ships a Jupyter notebook (e.g. SPIBACK) and the goal is to regenerate its fiducial-model outputs — the 2D local velocity-space distribution and median Galactocentric radial velocity map — on your own machine.

name: kepler-photometry-normalization
description: Use when you have long-cadence Kepler transit photometry (multiple transits of one planet) that must be normalized per segment without phase folding or rebinning and fitted simultaneously with shared system parameters.

name: keplerian-collision-time-computation
description: Use when two bodies follow Keplerian orbits about a central mass with intersecting orbital paths and you need a finite, strictly positive time to their next collision without stepwise numerical integration.

name: kernel-bandwidth-selection
description: Use when performing FINKER-style frequency identification on astronomical time series with measurement uncertainties and you must choose kernel_type and bandwidth_method before running parallel_nonparametric_kernel_regression over a frequency grid.

name: kernel-regression-frequency-estimation
description: Use when a time series (e.g. a synthetic or observed light curve with magnitudes, times, and uncertainties) must have its primary periodic frequency recovered, especially with few observations (down to ~10) or across varying SNR levels.

name: kilonova-lightcurve-inference
description: Use when multi-band kilonova photometry (e.g., AT2017gfo) must be fitted with an NMMA kilonova model to obtain ejecta-parameter posteriors, or when a GW+kilonova joint analysis needs the kilonova likelihood component.

name: kinematic-tracer-data-retrieval
description: Use when you need a unified, parameter-normalized compilation of Galactic rotation-curve tracer measurements (gas, stars, masers) for Galactocentric radii ~3–20 kpc, either from files or in-memory for parameter scans.

name: kp-index-prediction-comparison
description: Use when validating Sun-to-Earth CME ensemble forecasts that need a predicted geomagnetic response: run FIDO over a synthetic spacecraft, extract the maximum Kp from the ensemble in situ profiles, and check it against observed OMNI Kp for the event.

name: kroupa-imf-binary-sampling
description: Use when setting up a binary population synthesis run (e.g. COMPAS) that needs initial conditions for massive-star binaries to predict double compact object or BBH merger yields.

name: krylov-gmres-matrix-free-linear-solver
description: Use when the destriping equation has a dense [n_b, n_b] left-side matrix too heavy to invert even for modest datasets, and baselines (e.g. 2000-sample/60 s offsets for B-Machine data) must be recovered iteratively.

name: l1-norm-convergence-order-analysis
description: Use when you have numerical solutions of a hyperbolic PDE at multiple resolutions plus an exact analytic reference, and need to measure whether L1 error decreases and what convergence order the scheme attains.

name: l2-linf-waveform-accuracy-validation
description: Use when a rebuilt or extended surrogate (e.g., larger mass ratios, longer durations, higher harmonic modes) must be certified accurate and fast before release or reuse.

name: lal-object-memory-ownership-tracking
description: Use when wrapping C libraries that assume a single-owner memory paradigm (e.g., LALSuite classes) into garbage-collected languages, to test that parent/child object destruction and reference counting behave as expected.

name: lalsuite-api-surface-extraction
description: Use when you need a machine-readable enumeration of the public API surface (constants, functions, classes) of a LALSuite C library, e.g. as input to automated interface annotation or wrapper generation.

name: lalsuite-public-api-introspection
description: Use when you need an exhaustive, machine-readable inventory of the public constants, functions, and classes exported by a LALSuite C library's header files, e.g. to automate SWIG interface annotation.

name: lambda-cdm-parameter-inference
description: Use when a task requires MCMC-based posterior estimation of the seven Lambda-CDM parameters from WMAP likelihood data, or benchmarking an emcee-based sampler against CosmoMC.

name: landy-szalay-estimator-application
description: Use when the task requires measuring the angle-averaged two-point correlation function from a galaxy catalogue and an associated random catalogue in configuration space, e.g. over linearly spaced separation bins spanning r = 1–50 h⁻¹Mpc.

name: laplace-approximation-posterior-inference
description: Use when deriving RVs and their uncertainties from echelle spectra (e.g. HARPS S2D, ESPRESSO) by template matching and you need a statistically principled posterior for a common RV shift per spectrum, marginalizing over the continuum.

name: large-image-scaling-with-scipy-numpy
description: Use when a user needs to view or navigate a very large (>2 Gb) FITS image stored on a remote server in a browser, without downloading the full file or installing local visualization software.

name: large-scale-density-field-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have fitted halo accretion histories (e.g. diffmah parameters), halo positions, and a large-scale density field, and you need to quantify the correlation between halo assembly class or model residuals and environment.

name: large-scale-density-field-halo-mapping
description: Use when you have per-halo diffmah growth-history fit residuals and need to test whether those residual errors correlate with the large-scale density field, i.e. to validate that halo assembly bias is captured by the model.

name: latent-ode-variational-inference
description: Use when you have irregularly-sampled continuous-time series, need generative modelling of latent dynamics, and must extrapolate far beyond the training window (e.g. train on [0, 3], test on [0, 12]).

name: latent-space-interpolation-forward-pass
description: Use when you have a trained IAE spectral model (one per physical component) and need to reconstruct held-out spectra via encoder/interpolator/decoder, e.g. to reproduce Table B.1 reconstruction residuals.

name: lateral-chromatic-aberration-channel-rescaling
description: Use when generating synthetic space-mission imagery that must include realistic chromatic aberration — e.g. after Cycles path-traced rendering and Brown–Conrady distortion, before sensor-noise injection — to stress-test visual-navigation or 3-D reconstruction algorithms.

name: latitude-longitude-contour-panel-visualization
description: Use when processing standardized OSPREI ensemble output (nRuns > 1 with a .ens file) into per-CME latitude–longitude contour panels showing spatial maps of impact probability and mean CME/space-weather properties at a satellite.

name: lattice-grid-point-closest-to-origin-geometry
description: Use when two bodies are on intersecting Kepler orbits and you need an analytic collision time from their orbital elements and period ratio, e.g. to jump directly between collision events instead of time-stepping.

name: legendre-spectral-basis-eigenvalue-problem-setup
description: Use when a linearized PDE (e.g., wave perturbations on a static atmosphere) must be posed as an eigenvalue problem over multiple horizontal wavenumbers and solved with targeted sparse eigenvalue extraction in Dedalus.

name: lgbm-gradient-boosting-classifier-training
description: Use when a labeled multi-wavelength photometric catalog (fluxes in μJy plus redshift) with AGN/SFG classes exists and a fast, reproducible binary classifier for radio continuum survey sources is needed.

name: light-curve-gradient-measurement
description: Use when fitting a transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc (e.g. the J1407 SuperWASP photometry or the PDS 110 eclipse photometry) and you need to reject disc size/orientation configurations whose theoretical ring gradient cannot exceed the measured light-curve gradient.

name: lightcurve-dataset-generation
description: Use when you need simulated, noise-inclusive light curves of transients (e.g. SNe Ia) as they would be observed by a survey such as ZTF or LSST, starting from a target population and pointing/obsim observing history.

name: lightcurve-folding-residual-minimization
description: Use when an unevenly sampled astronomical time series (e.g. ~100 points over 10 time units) needs its primary frequency recovered, and a residual-minimising nonparametric kernel regression over a frequency grid is preferred over conditional entropy period-finding.

name: lightgbm-classifier-inference
description: Use when a catalog of extragalactic radio-survey sources with multi-band photometry (u-y, JHK, IRAC ch1-ch4, MIPS24, PACS, SPIRE, 150 MHz radio) and redshifts must be classified as AGN vs SFG and benchmarked.

name: lightgbm-feature-importance-extraction
description: Use when a trained MBASC/LightGBM classifier exists on multi-wavelength flux data and you need to rank which photometric bands (e.g. FIR and radio) most influence AGN vs SFG predictions.

name: lightgbm-supervised-classifier-training
description: Use when you have a CSV of multi-wavelength flux densities in μJy with redshift and need a supervised SFG-vs-AGN classification, or must retrain the classifier on degraded/modified band subsets to probe feature importance.

name: likelihood-chain-architecture-implementation
description: Use when assembling self-contained core modules (e.g., CAMB) and likelihood modules (e.g., WMAP) into a chain that shares a chain context (ctx) and enforces min/max parameter bounds for MCMC or PSO sampling.

name: likelihood-chisq-evaluation
description: Use when a mock or real band power vector (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) must be scored against a forward model at fixed cosmological parameters (H0=67.37, ombh2=0.02233, omch2=0.1198, logA=3.043, ns=0.9652, tau=0.054, yp=1.0) to obtain a chi-squared/log-likelihood value.

name: limb-darkening-per-filter-configuration
description: Use when fitting multiple transit light curves observed under different filters, instruments, or weather/limb-darkening conditions simultaneously, and you must let limb darkening vary per curve while sharing system parameters across curves.

name: line-list-format-conversion
description: Use when an ExoMol-format line list (e.g. .states.bz2/.trans.bz2 files like 24Mg-1H__XAB) must be emitted as fixed-width HITRAN2004 160-character records, or vice versa, for cross-database interoperability.

name: linear-growth-factor-application
description: Use when computing the halo mass function at redshift z != 0 (or normalising the power spectrum at z=0 via sigma8): the z-independent transfer function output must be grown to redshift z before evaluating f(sigma) and the HMF.

name: linear-growth-factor-redshift-scaling
description: Use when computing a halo mass function (HMF) or mass variance at nonzero redshift from a z=0 transfer function, or when updating an existing hmf calculation for a changed redshift without recomputing the transfer function.

name: linear-hot-plasma-dispersion-relation-comparison
description: Use when validating a plasma-wave simulation code: 1D low-β wave-test runs are available and numerical dispersion curves must be checked against linearised hot-plasma theory (WHAMP) per propagation angle.

name: linear-momentum-conservation-verification
description: Use when validating an FMM-based gravitational solver for conservation properties — e.g., after evolving a 3D self-gravitating SPH problem (Noh, Sod tube, single/binary star) with FleCSPH's newtonian_3d driver and you have initial and final H5part snapshots to compare.

name: linear-regression-fit-evaluation
description: Use when combining measured/literature property data for two compound classes (e.g. organostannanes + hydrocarbons) and you need to decide whether a molecular descriptor (MW vs intrinsic molar volume) collapses the data onto one linear relationship.

name: linear-regression-goodness-of-fit-verification
description: Use when tabulated paired measurements (e.g. vapour pressure vs temperature at 40-120°C in 20°C increments) must be reduced to a linear model whose slope yields a derived physical constant, and the fit must be validated against reported parameters.

name: linear-regression-of-vant-hoff-plots
description: Use when you have corrected GC retention times for a homologous series measured isothermally at multiple temperatures, a reference compound with known vaporization enthalpy, and need ΔHv/ΔSv per compound.

name: log-derivative-airy-propagation
description: Use when solving coupled-channel scattering or bound-state equations for ultracold atom–molecule systems, or when locating external field values where a bound level crosses a specified energy (e.g. Feshbach resonance positions).

name: log-mass-residual-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-halo diffmah -fit parameters and the original merger-tree mass histories and need to quantify fit quality via log-mass residuals against the 0.1 dex accuracy benchmark.

name: log-normal-nuclear-rate-uncertainty-propagation
description: Use when running BBN Monte Carlo analyses with PRyMordial and you need to propagate nuclear thermonuclear-rate uncertainties into light-element abundance posteriors, or compare PRIMAT vs NACRE II rate compilations.

name: log-radius-spline-differentiation
description: Use when migration-torque or thermodynamic gradient calculations need continuous dSigmadR, dTdR, dPdR functions evaluated at arbitrary migrator radii from discrete AGN-disk profiles (e.g. pAGN Sirko & Goodman or Thompson solved disks).

name: log-ratio-output-backtransformation
description: Use when an ExoMDN mixture density network has produced log-ratio-transformed outputs and they must be converted back to physical layer mass fractions and thicknesses of a low-mass exoplanet interior.

name: log-space-linear-spline-interpolation
description: Use when computing the mass variance sigma(M), power spectrum P(k), or cumulative HMF integrals from a CAMB-format transfer function and you must match hmf's numerics (log-space linear splines, 4097-point re-grid, Romberg integration).

name: loglog-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when you need to compare multiple implicit ODE solvers/tolerances by runtime-versus-accuracy, e.g. sweeping abstol=reltol from 1/10^7 to 1/10^11 against a fixed low-tolerance reference solution.

name: lognormal-mixture-temperature-deprojection
description: Use when deep X-ray surface brightness, spectroscopic temperature, and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich pressure profiles are available for galaxy clusters and a nonparametric hydrostatic mass profile is needed to test parametric forms such as NFW or Einasto.

name: lognormal-mock-catalogue-generation
description: Use when you need synthetic mock catalogues with realistic clustering (driven by an input power spectrum) to validate error estimates, e.g. jackknife/bootstrap covariance matrices for 2PCF measurements.

name: logsignature-timeseries-preprocessing
description: Use when an irregularly sampled, long time series must drive a neural CDE/RDE whose integration step size is far larger than the data sampling rate, and naive interpolation would discard sub-step dynamics (the log-ODE method of Appendix B).

name: long-cadence-transit-model-rebinning
description: Use when fitting transit light curves with long integration times (e.g. Kepler 29.4-minute long-cadence data), where unbinned model evaluation would distort fitted parameters such as Rp/Rs and a/Rs.

name: low-metallicity-progenitor-analysis
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or perturb the paper's COMPAS BBH progenitor analysis at Z=0.001 (5% solar metallicity) — e.g. changing the LBV mass-loss rate — to compare total merger rates and LVT151012-like (progenitor total mass ≳90 Msun) yields against the Fiducial model.

name: lte-spectral-simulation
description: Use when a task requires LTE absorption cross-sections from an ExoMol/HITRAN line list with a Voigt profile in sampling mode, e.g. reproducing H2O 1H2-16O POKAZATEL cross-sections for comparison against exomol.com reference data.

name: lte-spectroscopic-post-processing
description: Use when you have an ExoMol, ExoMolHR, ExoAtom, HITRAN, or HITEMP molecular/atomic line list and need LTE or non-LTE stick spectra, cross-sections, or derived properties such as partition functions or cooling functions.

name: lunar-layered-interior-modeling
description: Use when a multilayered lunar (or other planetary) interior model with radii, densities, shear moduli, and viscosities must be reduced to an equivalent homogeneous generalized Voigt body for long-term tidal/orbital evolution calculations.

name: lupus-disc-sample-comparison
description: Use when testing disc evolution models against a Lupus-style ALMA survey catalog of 12CO fluxes and continuum sizes, or when deciding whether flux- or size-based selection yields a larger detectable disc sample.

name: lvt151012-like-merger-classification
description: Use when counting COMPAS BBH mergers resembling LVT151012 (progenitor total mass ~90 M⊙ regime at Z=0.001) to test how a single parameter change alters the yield of one event class.

name: lyman-limit-slab-radiative-transfer
description: Use when quantifying how spectral shape, equilibrium temperature evolution, helium treatment, and on-the-spot approximation change H I / He I / He II column densities in a slab exposed to an isotropic ionizing background at Lyman-limit densities.

name: m-dwarf-planet-population-statistics
description: Use when you have RV time series (e.g. CARMENES DR1, 238-target subsample) and need a per-star planet occurrence rate over a mass–period grid, with completeness correction for minimum masses M pl sin i.

name: mac-angle-parameter-sweep
description: Use when benchmarking a fast multipole method's runtime scaling against an exact N-body reference, or when quantifying how the MAC opening angle controls the FMM accuracy/performance trade-off in tree-based particle codes.

name: mad-flux-outlier-flagging
description: Use when building S-BART stellar templates from reduced S2D HARPS/ESPRESSO observations and individual spectral frames contain anomalous pixel fluxes (cosmic rays, detector artifacts) that must be excluded before co-adding orders into the template.

name: magnetic-cycle-period-recovery
description: Use when an RV timeseries shows long-period (multi-year) activity-related variability plus a stellar rotation signal, and you need posterior credible intervals for P_mag and P_rot with automatic model selection over ln Z.

name: magnetic-field-configuration-modeling
description: Use when ALP-photon conversion limits derived under a turbulent ICM field baseline must be checked for robustness against a regular magnetic field configuration, e.g. varying the assumed ICMF/GMF model in an alpconv-based analysis.

name: magnetohydrodynamic-simulation-setup
description: Use when a task requires solving high-Mach-number MHD flows that develop shocks with a spectral solver, specifically reproducing tests like the Orszag-Tang vortex (Figs. 11-12) up to a target simulation time such as t=0.5.

name: mangle-survey-mask-handling
description: Use when a galaxy survey footprint must be split into N sub-regions for jackknife or bootstrap covariance estimation and the geometry follows the survey mask (MANGLE) rather than a periodic-box cubic decomposition.

name: many-core-platform-performance-extraction
description: Use when an article reports benchmark runs of a code (e.g., Castro's wdmerger self-gravity problem) on a many-core architecture such as Intel Xeon Phi on NERSC Cori, and the threading configuration and optimization status must be captured as structured fields.

name: map-residual-statistics
description: Use when you have a predicted-emission timestream sampled at an instrument's pointings (e.g. ZodiPy output for the DIRBE observer) and need a binned HEALPix map comparable to reference observations such as DIRBE CIO, plus per-pixel residual statistics.

name: markov-chain-monte-carlo-posterior-sampling
description: Use when a cosmological model defined by a chi-squared likelihood with Gaussian priors needs parameter-space posterior sampling, chain output, and marginalised (one-dimensional) posteriors.

name: markov-chain-monte-carlo-sampler-implementation
description: Use when sampling from a Bayesian posterior or other target density on a real parameter space of dimension d where choosing the scale and orientation of a jumping distribution is hard, and block/multi-chain updating is desired.

name: markov-chain-monte-carlo-target-density-specification
description: Use when you need to draw samples from a real-parameter-space target density (e.g. a high-dimensional posterior) and want an MCMC that avoids hand-tuning the jump distribution's scale and orientation.

name: mass-profile-residual-quantification
description: Use when you have nonparametric hydrostatic mass profiles (e.g. from hydromass log-normal mixture reconstruction of X-ray/SZ cluster data) and need to test whether an NFW parametric fit captures each cluster's radial mass shape.

name: matlab-configuration-module-authoring
description: Use when rebuilding or extending a Matlab model codebase where model parameters must be centralized in a single editable function, with each field matching values reported in a reference document.

name: matter-lambda-equality-diagnostics
description: Use when reproducing or validating CONCEPT 1.0 Figure 2 time-step curves: you must identify which limiter (fixed-Δa, Hubble, dynamical, or non-linear P3M) governs Δln a at each scale factor and check the equality-transition feature.

name: mcmc-autocorrelation-time-analysis
description: Use when comparing sampler efficiency (e.g. emcee/CosmoHammer vs Metropolis-Hastings CosmoMC) by estimating autocorrelation times per parameter, or when determining the sampling effort needed to reach a target statistical error epsilon <= 0.1.

name: mcmc-chain-convergence-and-marginal-posterior-analysis
description: Use when a C++/CBL analysis needs posterior sampling of cosmological model parameters via MCMC, with a chi-squared likelihood plus Gaussian priors, and chain/posterior outputs must be validated.

name: mcmc-context-data-exchange-design
description: Use when building an extensible MCMC framework that must combine independent theory-prediction (core) and likelihood modules via a shared context, or when refactoring a monolithic likelihood computation into plug-in modules.

name: mcmc-convergence-and-posterior-constraining
description: Use when a radial-velocity time series contains an unknown number of planetary signals and you need the sampler itself to decide how many Keplerian components to keep, with posteriors from each run seeding the next and a tolerance-based stopping rule.

name: mcmc-convergence-diagnostic-analysis
description: Use when comparing two sampler backends (e.g. emcee ensemble MCMC vs stan HMC/NUTS) on the same visibility likelihood, or when deciding whether a posterior run has converged before trusting parameter estimates.

name: mcmc-convergence-diagnostic-tabulation
