description: Use when you have posterior chains from ensemble (Goodman-Weare/emcee) or Metropolis-Hastings MCMC samplers and need per-parameter autocorrelation times to compare sampler convergence and efficiency side by side.

name: mcmc-convergence-verification-against-reference
description: Use when an MCMC posterior sample of cosmological parameters (e.g. from CosmoHammer/emcee on WMAP 7 data) must be cross-checked against a reference sampler like CosmoMC to confirm convergence and statistical agreement within ~3.4%-of-sigma tolerance.

name: mcmc-ensemble-mean-tracking
description: Use when you need to quantify how many MCMC iterations are required before chains lose their initialisation bias, especially when comparing ensemble samplers with large walker counts L against Metropolis–Hastings chains.

name: mcmc-ensemble-sampling-cosmological-parameters
description: Use when you need to estimate cosmological parameters (e.g. the seven Lambda-CDM parameters) from CMB data via MCMC, or benchmark a new sampler's posteriors against a CosmoMC reference chain.

name: mcmc-gibbs-sampling
description: Use when fitting Kepler or ground-based transit light curves where classic chi-squared underestimates parameter uncertainties because the photometric noise contains a correlated (red) component.

name: mcmc-population-chain-initialization
description: Use when sampling from a high-dimensional Bayesian posterior in real parameter space where choosing jump scale/orientation for standard MCMC is hard, and WinBUGS-style one-dimensional updates are too limited.

name: mcmc-posterior-marginalization
description: Use when you need to marginalize over nuisance parameters (e.g., 63 log-normal nuclear-rate uncertainties) to obtain light-element abundance posteriors from a BBN forward model like PRyMordial, comparing rate prescriptions such as PRIMAT vs NACRE II.

name: mcmc-posterior-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you have multi-instrument radial-velocity data (e.g. 51peg.vels from LICK) and need posterior parameter estimates plus Bayesian model selection (ln Z, BIC) over increasing Keplerian counts.

name: mcmc-posterior-parameter-estimation
description: Use when reanalyzing Kepler long-cadence (29.4 min) transit photometry to derive Period, Inclination, a/Rs, and Rp/Rs posteriors via MCMC, or when comparing independent transit fits with a fractional-difference significance test.

name: mcmc-posterior-percentile-summarization
description: Use when posterior summaries of a Bayesian hierarchical/nonlinear mixed-effects model must be reported as percentiles and checked against a reference sampler's output for agreement within Monte Carlo error.

name: mcmc-posterior-sampling
description: Use when fitting parametric radial profiles (e.g. Gaussian, power) to ALMA visibility sets exported from an ms file and you need posterior parameter estimates via MCMC rather than a single optimisation.

name: mcmc-posterior-sampling
description: Use when fitting a 1D (optionally beam-smeared) galaxy rotation curve to recover physical mass-model parameters, or when validating MCMC parameter recovery on synthetic rotation curves at known S/N levels.

name: mcmc-sampler-implementation-in-r
description: Use when Bayesian computing requires sampling a real-parameter target density (e.g. multivariate Normal or Student t3 posteriors) and scale/orientation of the jumping distribution must adapt automatically, or when benchmarking MCMC efficiency vs RWM.

name: mcmc-sampler-performance-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking an ensemble MCMC sampler against a self-tuning Metropolis–Hastings sampler: you have autocorrelation times tau, burn-in length b, walker count L and sequential steps n, and need to find at what sampling effort epsilon <= 0.1.

name: mcmc-transit-light-curve-fitting
description: Use when you have one or more photometric transit time series (ground-based or Kepler 29.4-min long-cadence from MAST) and need MCMC-derived system parameters with uncertainties that properly treat correlated (red) noise.

name: mcmc-transit-parameter-inference
description: Use when you have raw, non-phase-folded transit photometry (e.g. Kepler long-cadence or ground-based light curves) and need posterior transit parameters (P, a/Rs, Rp/Rs, i, Tmid, limb darkening) with robust uncertainty estimates.

name: median-radial-velocity-map-adjustment
description: Use when fitting non-axisymmetric Milky Way disk potentials: after the bar stage has matched solar-neighborhood velocity-distribution peaks, and median Galactocentric radial velocity maps from Gaia DR3 are the fitting target for spiral-arm parameters.

name: median-rv-precision-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing RV precision of two extraction methods (e.g. template matching vs CCF) on the same spectra: you have per-observation RV uncertainty columns (RVc_ERR, DRIFT_ERR) and need a headline median-uncertainty metric plus a method-to-method ratio.

name: memory-footprint-benchmarking
description: Reference for benchmarking a sparse-grid or adaptive phase-space representation against its dense counterpart: you have a full-grid memory estimate (e.g. ~4 EiB for Vlasiator's 3D–3V magnetospheric configuration) and need a measured reduction factor.

name: memory-hierarchy-bandwidth-tabulation
description: Use when reproducing or cross-checking GPU kernel profiling tables — registers, threads per block, occupancy, instruction-time splits, or per-level memory bandwidths — for CUDA kernels profiled on an NVIDIA K40 or similar device.

name: memory-mapping-configuration-testing
description: Use when porting or profiling HDS datMap/datUnmap semantics onto HDF5, or when benchmark timing ratios (v5/v4) are unexpectedly high for map-heavy routines and you need to isolate the mmap/copy-back overhead.

name: meta-learner-prediction-correction
description: Use when classifying tabular astronomical sources (e.g., SDSS+WISE photometry) into galaxy/QSO/star classes one class at a time, and overlapping one-versus-all binary predictions need correction by a meta-learner.

name: metallicity-dependent-merger-rate-normalization
description: Use when converting a simulated population of double compact objects (e.g. from COMPAS) into per-metallicity merger yields and a rescaled Gpc^-3 per year rate to compare with gravitational-wave observations.

name: metallicity-dependent-population-synthesis-tabulation
description: Use when comparing COMPAS BPS outputs across metallicity or common-envelope prescriptions to quantify how many BBHs merge within a Hubble time per 1e9 solar masses of star formation.

name: metallicity-dependent-rate-comparison
description: Use when you need BBH merger-rate sensitivity to a single varied physics parameter (alpha_lambda, fLBV, CE treatment, Fryer SN model) or metallicity, compared against the COMPAS Fiducial baseline per 1e9 solar masses of star formation.

name: metallicity-planet-formation-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need occurrence rates of planet classes (giants >300 M⊕, Earth-like, low-mass) as a function of stellar metallicity across galactic regions, or thin/thick disc occurrence-rate ratios in a simulated galaxy.

name: metallicity-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you need to test the sensitivity of equilibrium condensation temperatures to metallicity offsets, e.g. to assess how stellar [M/H] propagates into rocky-planet building-block volatility while holding relative element ratios fixed.

name: metropolis-acceptance-criterion-verification
description: Use when implementing or auditing an MCMC sampler with difference-vector proposals (DE-MC scheme DE1) and you must confirm the proposal kernel is symmetric so a plain Metropolis ratio pi(x_p)/pi(x_i) is valid.

name: metropolis-acceptance-rate-monitoring
description: Use when running DE-MC (or another Metropolis-based multi-chain sampler) and you need to verify tuning of the jump scale γ via the per-generation acceptance fraction, e.g. checking it converges to ~0.23 on a high-dimensional target.

name: metropolis-hastings-sampler-implementation
description: Use when you need to sample a multi-parameter posterior defined by a chi-squared likelihood with Gaussian priors in C++/CosmoBolognaLib, producing MCMC chains and marginalised posteriors.

name: mic-nonlinear-correlation-estimation
description: Use when a multivariate table (e.g. galaxy catalog or supernova host properties) may contain non-linear pairwise dependencies and you need a model-free dependence measure to feed clustering or correlation heatmaps.

name: migration-torque-validation-against-reference
description: Use when a re-implemented migration torque-coefficient module must be checked for correctness against published pAGN reference outputs before it is trusted for AGN-disk migration studies.

name: milky-way-bar-spiral-potential-modeling
description: Use when modeling Milky Way bar/spiral non-axisymmetric potentials to reproduce Gaia DR3 moving groups or median Galactocentric radial velocity maps, or when comparing a candidate bar/spiral parameter set against Khalil et al. 2025 fiducial kinematic features.

name: minimum-image-distance-computation
description: Use when implementing or validating short-range gravity pair enumeration in a periodic cosmological N-body box, e.g. reproducing CONCEPT 1.0's tiles-and-subtiles P3M scheme and its early-rejection statistics.

name: mock-data-set-likelihood-initialisation
description: Use when a realistic mock CMB band power data set (TT/TE/EE/BB/phi-phi/kappa-kappa) must be turned into a working differentiable likelihood for Fisher forecasting, e.g. scanning band power bin widths to minimise parameter errors.

name: mock-data-slope-recovery-validation
description: Use when testing a Jeans-based mass-modeling code for graceful degradation with small tracer samples, or verifying that reported density-slope uncertainties at R1/2 grow without introducing bias in mock-data recovery tests.

name: mock-data-vector-generation
description: Use when you need a realistic simulated band power vector (e.g. for Fisher forecasting, robustness tests, or optimising the band power bin width) matching a specific candl data set such as SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE.

name: mock-observation-simulation-of-galaxy-kinematics
description: Use when you have an intrinsic 1D rotation curve (disk+bulge+halo mass model) and need beam-smeared mock-observed rotation/dispersion curves for a given sky-orientation and PSF, e.g. for benchmarking or forward-model fitting.

name: model-data-agreement-quantification
description: Use when comparing population-level model predictions of 12CO fluxes against observed ALMA fluxes (e.g. Lupus or Upper Sco samples) and you need to quantify model-data agreement and its sensitivity to initial-condition uncertainties.

name: model-fit-accuracy-aggregation
description: Use when you have fitted diffmah parameters paired with simulated halo mass assembly histories and need to quantify, per-halo and across the sample, whether the 3-parameter model meets the 0.1 dex accuracy claim for t > 1 Gyr.

name: model-output-validation-against-reference-values
description: Use when a fast surrogate or semi-analytical model (e.g. COpops 12CO fluxes) must be checked against a reference set of expensive physical model outputs (e.g. DALI thermochemical fluxes) before population-scale use.

name: model-parameter-extraction-from-paper
description: Use when a repository's configuration/parameter file (e.g. g2myparms.m) is missing or must be rebuilt, and the authoritative parameter values are listed in the accompanying paper such as ./paper/paper.pdf.

name: module-mode-scan-execution
description: Use when a GAMBIT installation needs to be exercised end-to-end: an example YAML scan (e.g. yaml_files/MSSM7.yaml) must be run in module mode so that a module like DarkBit emits observable and likelihood results through the GAMBIT printer.

name: molecular-cooling-function-calculation
description: Use when you have a molecular line list (e.g., ExoMol POKAZATEL for 1H2-16O) and need temperature-dependent cooling functions W(T) rather than spectra or cross-sections.

name: molecular-line-list-processing
description: Use when a task requires LTE (or non-LTE) absorption/emission cross-sections or stick spectra computed from an ExoMol/HITRAN/HITEMP molecular line list, e.g. reproducing H2O POKAZATEL cross-sections with a Voigt profile in sampling mode.

name: momentum-target-network-update
description: Use when training BYOL directly as a torch.nn.Module (not via ByolTrainer) on astronomical images: after each optimization step you must sync the target network with the online network via an exponential moving average.

name: montblanc-source-provider-implementation
description: Use when extending Montblanc's RIME solver with a new source type: you must add a per-antenna-term kernel loop, a dimension-extent-driven data provider, and prove GPU/CPU numeric agreement for chi2.

name: monte-carlo-input-sampling
description: Use when an exoplanet's observed mass, radius, and equilibrium temperature carry stated measurement uncertainties and the goal is a propagated, uncertainty-aware posterior of interior structure (iron core, silicate mantle, water/ice, H/He) rather than a single-point prediction.

name: monte-carlo-parameter-sampling
description: Use when a surrogate or empirical interpolant has been built (e.g., 19-element reduced basis for q in [1,2] EOB waveforms) and you need a randomized, distribution-aware validation of interpolation error against a theoretical bound such as 1e-8 from Eq. (20).

name: monte-carlo-population-synthesis
description: Use when you have per-halo diffmah parameter fits (early-time, peak-time, late-time power-law parameters) and need a synthetic population of halo histories matching the ensemble's mean growth and scatter across cosmic time.

name: monte-carlo-rejection-filtering
description: Use when simulating X-ray polarimetric observations where an instrumental effect (vignetting vs. off-axis angle, chip fiducial area, readout dead-time) must be realized by stochastic event rejection rather than deterministic reweighting.

name: monte-carlo-standard-error-analysis
description: Use when MCMC chains (e.g. emcee ensemble walkers or CosmoMC Metropolis–Hastings chains) must be shown to lose their initialisation bias before posterior samples are trusted, i.e. to fix a defensible burn-in length.

name: montepython-likelihood-wrapper-implementation
description: Use when a candl CMB power-spectrum likelihood (e.g. candl_data.SPT3G_2018_TTTEEE) must be sampled inside the MontePython framework and wrapper/direct log-likelihood agreement must be verified before sampling.

name: mpi-openmp-hybrid-parallelism-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting or transcribing strong-scaling performance results (core counts, threading mixes, compilers) for hybrid MPI/OpenMP runs of AMReX-based codes like Castro on leadership-class machines such as OLCF Titan.

name: mpi-parallel-destriping-execution
description: Use when CMB polarimeter timestreams (e.g. HDF5 files with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U columns) need correlated-noise removal and the destriping equation's left-side matrix is too large to invert directly for modest-to-large datasets.

name: mpi-parallel-job-execution
description: Use when a FleCSPH executable (hydro_1-2-3d, newtonian_3d, or a *_generator) must be run on multiple MPI ranks to produce H5part particle data or timing measurements for tree-based particle simulations.

name: mpi-parallel-mcmc-scaling-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how wall time of an MCMC likelihood chain (e.g. CAMB + WMAP likelihood) scales with core count on a cluster, cloud (EC2), or grid, and to measure parallelisation overhead.

name: mpi-parallel-simulation-workflow
description: Use when the task requires installing and running an MPI-parallel cosmological N-body code (CONCEPT/GADGET-2) from deposited parameter files and validating it via power-spectrum cross-comparison up to k ~ 13 h/Mpc.

name: mpi-parallel-strong-scaling-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify how an MPI-parallel PDE solver scales to large core counts — i.e., you have per-run timings for fixed-size (strong) or fixed-per-rank (weak) 3D spectral problems and need parallel-efficiency curves.

name: mpi-parallel-time-integration
description: Use when a PDE simulation must be time-integrated to a statistically saturated state (e.g., t=200) over a multi-dimensional spectral domain (e.g., 256x128x32 modes) and serial runtime is infeasible, requiring MPI parallelism.

name: mpi-thread-configuration-interpretation
description: Use when strong-scaling timing data shows an upturn or discontinuity near the maximum processor count, and the run mixes hybrid MPI/OpenMP configurations across NUMA nodes — as in the Maestro 3-d XRB runs on Titan and Edison.

name: mukhanov-sasaki-mode-integration
description: Use when computing the scalar primordial power spectrum from an inflationary background: you need to integrate oscillatory cosmological perturbation modes over a k range after solving the background and locating the end of inflation.

name: multi-band-galaxy-image-visualization
description: Use when hydrodynamical simulation particle data (IllustrisTNG or EAGLE subhalos) must be turned into survey-realistic bandpass images or RGB composites, e.g. to build deep-learning training sets or validate observational pipelines.

name: multi-chain-mcmc-convergence-diagnostics
description: Use when sampling a real-parameter posterior (e.g. a d=5 or d=10 normal mixture with modes at -5 and 5) and you need to verify that chains from dispersed starts mix to the same target distribution and recover a known posterior mean.

name: multi-epoch-deep-image-stacking
description: Use when you hold pre-calibrated multi-epoch radio-synthesis measurement sets and need steady-source detection plus per-epoch cleaned images, e.g. ALARRM-style transient follow-up with AMI-LA or any telescope via CASA.

name: multi-instrument-lightcurve-joint-fitting
description: Use when a planet (or multi-planet system) has transit light curves from more than one instrument (e.g. CHEOPS plus TESS sectors) and you need precise planetary radii and orbital periods before downstream modelling such as internal-structure inference.

name: multi-light-curve-simultaneous-transit-fitting
description: Use when you have N transit light curves of the same planet observed under different conditions (instrument, filter, weather, cadence) and need joint system-parameter estimates with per-transit Tmid values and robust uncertainty comparison versus single-curve fits.

name: multi-messenger-inference-uncertainty-comparison
description: Use when a paper reports a parameter estimate (e.g., R_1.4) with asymmetric credible bounds from a joint analysis and you must verify a claimed precision improvement against Table 1-style literature baselines.

name: multi-sample-photo-z-comparison-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a photo-z method's catastrophic outlier rates (O(a): |zphot-zspec|>0.10; O(b): |zphot-zspec|/(1+zspec)>0.10) against published codes across simulated (PHAT0) and real (SDSS DR10) samples.

name: multi-source-constraint-combination
description: Use when single-source ALP constraints from Fermi-LAT spectra exist for two or more blazars and the goal is a joint 95% CL exclusion region in the (gaγ, ma) plane that strictly enlarges each individual contour.

name: multi-step-flag-preservation-in-uv-data
description: Use when reducing e-MERLIN interferometric visibility data where Lovell phase-calibrator stationary scans must be flagged after RFI and dropout flagging, with prior flags preserved.

name: multi-transit-simultaneous-fitting-with-locked-parameters
description: Use when several transit light curves observed under different conditions (instrument, filter, weather) must be fit at once with shared system parameters but free per-transit mid-transit times.

name: multi-view-stereo-mesh-reconstruction
description: Use when a synthetic (or real) multi-angle image series of a body must be turned into a 3-D model, and the reconstructed model must be validated against a reference shape model via point-deviation statistics.

name: multi-wavelength-sed-feature-preparation
description: Use when building the input CSV for MBASC or a similar LightGBM AGN/SFG classifier: you have multi-band photometry (optical/NIR/MIR/FIR/radio) with redshift that must be assembled into the exact expected feature schema in μJy.

name: multichannel-tiff-encoding
description: Use when derived per-pixel scientific data (vector fields, height maps, normal components) must be packaged for streaming visualization via IIPImage-style tiled servers, or when full 32-bit floating point precision must survive channel mixing and compression.

name: multigrid-solver-scaling-limit-analysis
description: Use when strong-scaling curves from AMReX-based simulations (Maestro/Castro) flatten or show non-monotonic upturns, and the goal is to attribute the behavior to the multigrid nodal solver or to hybrid MPI/OpenMP NUMA placement changes.

name: multimessenger-bayesian-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you must jointly infer compact-binary-merger source parameters from combined gravitational-wave strain data, kilonova photometry (e.g. AT2017gfo), and GRB afterglow light curves (e.g. GRB170817A, Troja et al. data set) rather than combining single-messenger posteriors a posteriori.

name: multivariate-target-density-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a multi-chain MCMC sampler (e.g. DE-MC) against a reference sampler on target distributions of known density, so that percentile-estimate MSE and sampling efficiency can be computed exactly.

name: multiwavelength-photometric-classification
description: Use when a radio-continuum survey catalog has multi-wavelength photometry (optical u–y, NIR JHK, IRAC ch1–ch4, MIPS24, PACS, SPIRE), 150 MHz radio fluxes, and redshifts, and each source must be labelled AGN or SFG.

name: multiwavelength-photometry-assembly
description: Use when building an ultraviolet-to-millimetre photometric data table for galaxies whose SEDs will be fitted with radiative transfer models, and when mid-IR spectra (e.g. Spitzer) must be included at matched spectral resolution.

name: multiwavelength-photometry-band-subset-degradation-analysis
description: Use when planning or interpreting radio galaxy surveys with poorer multi-wavelength coverage than LOFAR Deep Fields, and you need to know which photometric bands (especially far-infrared and radio) the classifier depends on.

name: n-body-cluster-integration
description: Use when simulating star clusters that embed fast-evolving subsystems (planetary systems, binaries, asteroids) where a direct N-body code like Ph4 over the whole system is too costly and extreme scale separation, tidal fields, and stellar evolution must be handled together.

name: na-aware-data-matrix-preparation
description: Use when importing a galaxy/host-galaxy catalog (CSV/TXT, space-separated named columns) that contains missing entries and you intend to compute Pearson, Spearman, or MIC correlation matrices downstream.

name: nacre-rate-compilation-usage
description: Use when predicting primordial light-element abundances from a BBN nuclear network, when comparing abundance predictions to quasar absorption or CMB baryon-density constraints, or when rate choices must be specified for the 63-reaction network.

name: namelist-input-file-configuration
description: Use when preparing an input file for molscat, bound or field variants (e.g. molscat-basic1.input, molscat-basic_Rb2.input, field-Mg_NH.input) that specifies basis, potential expansion, field ranges or energies via &INPUT/&BASIS/&POTL namelists.

name: namelist-input-file-configuration-for-bound
description: Use when you need to set up or reproduce a BOUND bound-state energy calculation (e.g. bound-basic) for an atom–rigid-rotor system and must specify the energy window (EMIN/EMAX), total angular momentum (JTOT), and symmetry/fixing options (IBFIX) in namelist input blocks.

name: namelist-input-file-preparation
description: Use when setting up a new MOLSCAT/BOUND/FIELD run (e.g. atom + linear rigid rotor at 1250 cm-1, a two-channel LJ Feshbach scan, or a FIELD threshold search over magnetic field) and you must author or adapt a namelist input file.

name: nbody-collision-list-propagation
description: Decision support for when an event-driven Kepler collision-list propagator can beat tree-code (octree, k-d tree) collision detection, e.g. Solar-System-like systems with rare collisions and N < 10^8.

name: nbody-simulation-parameter-configuration
description: Use when setting up or reproducing a CONCEPT 1.0 N-body run: you need to specify the ΛCDM background cosmology, particle count/box size, or time-stepping parameters and want the exact parameter files the authors used.

name: nearby-mdwarf-sample-selection
description: Use when auditing the completeness of a spectroscopic survey's target list against a reference catalog of known nearby stars — i.

name: nested-sampling-posterior-extraction
description: Use when a Bayesian multi-messenger analysis (e.g., GW170817 strain + AT2017gfo photometry + GRB170817A afterglow) requires sampling a joint posterior and reporting asymmetric credible intervals on parameters like R_1.4, ejecta masses, or inclination.

name: nested-sampling-posterior-inference
description: Use when you need posterior inference (credible intervals, not point estimates) for GravSphere2 mass modeling of individual stellar LOS/PM velocities — e.g. recovering the log density slope at R1/2 from Gaia Challenge or Fornax-like mocks with quantified uncertainty.

name: nested-sampling-thread-division
description: Use when you have a single nested sampling run (e.g. PolyChord >=1.14 output written with 'write_dead'=True, containing dead points and the iso-likelihood contours at which they were born) and need standard errors on posterior inferences such as logZ and parameter means.

name: neural-cde-ode-reduction
description: Use when a neural CDE dy(t) = f_θ(y(t), dX(t)) must be solved over discrete, irregularly sampled time-series data, and the only available numerical machinery is an ODE solver rather than a native CDE integrator.

name: neural-cde-rnn-correspondence-analysis
description: Use when you need to demonstrate or test that a discrete recurrent architecture (e.g. GRU) corresponds to an ODE discretisation, or to interpret gate dynamics in continuous time.

name: neural-cde-training
description: Use when training a model on irregularly or continuously indexed time-series data (e.g. 2D spiral classification, BIDMC vital-sign regression) where a CDE hidden state driven by an interpolated path is the target architecture.

name: neural-network-continuum-prediction
description: Use when a headerless two-column spectrum (wavelengths in angstroms, flux) of an O–G type star needs an automated pseudo-continuum prediction before dividing out the continuum or applying spline corrections.

name: neural-network-emulator-likelihood-pipelining
description: Use when you need a parameters-to-log-likelihood function for CMB power-spectrum analyses (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) that is end-to-end differentiable with JAX, avoiding slow Boltzmann solvers via a trained emulator.

name: neural-network-emulator-theory-spectra-prediction
description: Use when sampling or differentiating through a CMB likelihood requires fast, JAX-native theory spectra (e.g. gradient-based NUTS with BlackJAX) and a trained CosmoPower emulator for the target data set exists.

name: neural-network-emulator-timing-comparison
description: Use when a study needs to quantify computational cost of power-spectrum evaluation — e.g. justifying an analytic emulator for MCMC or large surveys by timing it against CAMB and BACCO on the same grid.

name: neural-network-surrogate-sampling
description: Use when you have observed stellar and planetary parameters (e.g. CHEOPS/TESS radii plus ESPRESSO/HIRES RVs) for planets of 0.5–15 M⊕ and need internal-structure posteriors without running the full BICEPS interior model directly.

name: neural-ode-conditioning-parameter-encoding
description: Use when building a neural ODE surrogate for PDR chemistry and you must decide which quantities (e.g. Av, G0, cosmic-ray rate, density vs abundances, temperature) are injected as conditioning parameters versus evolved as ODE features.

name: neural-ode-solver-configuration-jax
description: Use when irregularly-sampled time series must be modelled with a latent ODE and the goal is to generate or forecast samples beyond the training time window (e.g. training on [0,3], testing on [0,12]).

name: neural-ode-surrogate-training
description: Use when you have a raw 3D-PDR dataset (HDF5 or simulations.tgz) from one of the v1/v2/v3 Zenodo deposits and need to train an emulator that reproduces chemical abundances, temperatures, and column density maps faster than the chemical solver.

name: neural-rde-model-training
description: Use when irregularly sampled, long time series (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) must be modelled by a differential-equation-based regressor while taking integration steps much larger than the data sampling rate without discarding sub-step information.

name: neural-sde-generative-adversarial-training
description: Use when the goal is to generate synthetic stochastic time series (e.g. Brownian-motion paths) whose distribution — including initial condition — matches a set of observed (t, y) trajectories, via adversarial training of a neural SDE generator.

name: neutrino-decoupling-temperature-tracking
description: Use when a cosmology analysis requires a first-principles SM thermodynamic background (N_eff, neutrino energy density, thermal history) rather than assuming instantaneous neutrino decoupling or hardcoded N_eff values.

name: neutrino-vertex-to-antenna-propagation-solution
description: Use when simulating ultra-high-energy neutrino detection in ice: you have event-generator output (vertex positions, shower parameters) and antenna positions from the detector description, and need per-vertex/per-antenna ray-path solutions before detector simulation.

name: neutron-star-radius-measurement-extraction
description: Use when a paper reports a 1.4M⊙ neutron-star radius with asymmetric credible intervals (e.g., R = 11.98 +0.35/−0.40 km) and you must benchmark it against prior literature values to verify a claimed precision improvement.

name: neutron-to-proton-born-rate-constraint-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to constrain fractional NP modifications of BBN-era weak n↔p conversion rates from percent-level PDG measurements of primordial helium-4 and deuterium, using PRyMordial predictions sampled with emcee.

name: new-physics-energy-injection-modeling
description: Use when scanning a new-physics particle species thermalized with the plasma or neutrino bath over a mass grid and predicting N_eff and light-element abundances for BBN exclusion/allowance regions.

name: newton-iteration-nlbvp-static-atmosphere-solve
description: Use when you need a stratified background atmosphere (e.g. radiative layer with Eddington closure and Kramer-like opacity) as the equilibrium state for a linear perturbation or eigenvalue problem in Dedalus.

name: nfw-density-profile-construction
description: Use when you need a spherically symmetric gas density profile for a halo of known virial mass (e.g. 1e10 Msun at z=0, Δv=200) to feed into a sphere solver with an isotropic background field.

name: nfw-profile-filter-construction
description: Use when computing an aperture mass map from a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog (positions and elliptities) and a radially defined mass filter matching an NFW profile is required.

name: nightly-zero-point-estimation
description: Use when you have per-spectrum radial velocities (with uncertainties, drift and secular-acceleration columns) from a spectrograph's pipeline and need to quantify the instrument's night-to-night zero-point stability as an upper limit on RV precision.

name: nls-network-simulation
description: Use when a nonlinear PDE (e.g. nonlinear Schrodinger equation with a bright soliton) must be evolved on a graph of coupled 1D segments and you need to observe scattering at vertices and spreading across the full network over time.

name: noh-implosion-shock-validation
description: Use when a new SPH build or configuration of FleCSPH (or a similar tree-based SPH code) needs numerical validation against a strong-shock benchmark with a known analytic density plateau and self-similar shock front.

name: noise-function-gas-source-modelling
description: Use when building a cometary dust/gas environment in SISPO Case 2: you have a triangulated nucleus mesh (e.g. .obj) and need surface-resolved gas outflow rates to initialize the gas-density and particle pipelines before Cycles volume rendering.

name: noise-mask-based-texture-blending
description: Use when a plain 3-D asteroid/small-body mesh (e.g., the 25143 Itokawa model) must gain realistic surface elevation and albedo detail in Blender/Cycles while preserving the undistorted input geometry.

name: non-axisymmetric-potential-parameter-tabulation
description: Use when reproducing or validating the reported fiducial parameter table of the Khalil et al. non-axisymmetric Milky Way model (bar and spiral pattern speeds and contrast densities) from the A&A article text.

name: non-instantaneous-decoupling-evolution
description: Use when a precision BBN analysis requires N_eff and neutron-to-proton conversion rates computed from a coupled, non-instantaneous neutrino-decoupling thermal history, optionally with new-physics energy exchange (NP_e_flag/NP_nu_flag) with the plasma or neutrino bath.

name: non-maxwellianity-diagnostics
description: Use when judging whether Vlasiator simulation output (VLSV files) contains kinetic ion physics: compute a non-Maxwellianity metric on downstream shock ion distributions and compare magnetic compression ratios across grid resolutions.

name: nonlinear-mixed-effects-posterior-sampling
description: Use when the target is a high-dimensional Bayesian posterior from a nonlinear mixed-effects (population pharmacokinetic) model whose blocks or correlated parameters defeat one-dimensional Gibbs/WinBUGS-style updates and closed-form conditionals.

name: nonparametric-density-hypothesis-testing-planet-populations
description: Use when comparing a continuous property (e.g. bulk density from published mass/radius) across two independently labeled exoplanet subpopulations and no assumption of normality is justified, as in the savanna-vs-ridge super-Neptune comparison.

name: nonparametric-kernel-regression-fitting
description: Use when a magnitude time series (light curve) with per-point uncertainties must have its periodicity detected/recovered, especially sparse data (down to ~10 observations) or multi-band data, by fitting nonparametric kernel regression on phase-folded datasets.

name: nonparametric-kernel-regression-period-finding
description: Use when you need to recover the dominant frequency/period of a sparsely sampled astronomical light curve (even ~10 observations) from time/magnitude/uncertainty arrays, especially when noise robustness or multi-band handling matters.

name: nonspinning-binary-black-hole-waveform-processing
description: Use when the goal is to quantify reduced-basis compressibility of a fiducial waveform family — e.g. reproducing Fig. 3 greedy-error decay for 501 EOB-LAL nonspinning waveforms with q in [1,2] and checking exponential decay to machine precision.

name: normal-mixture-target-density-evaluation
description: Reference for testing whether a population-based MCMC method converges on a bimodal, distant-mode target where random walk Metropolis fails; triggered when RMSE of the posterior mean estimate and acceptance fraction must be quantified for d=5 and d=10 mixtures.

name: nuclear-equation-of-state-construction
description: Use when building candidate EOS realizations for binary-neutron-star analyses: you have a low-density nuclear EOS uncertainty band (chiral EFT / AFDMC samples) and need high-density extensions, TOV mass-radius sequences, and Lambda values for sampling.

name: nuclear-reaction-network-configuration
description: Use when a task needs PRyMordial's BBN abundance predictions with configurable weak n↔p Born rates (e.g. enabling smallnet_flag and nacreii_flags before a Bayesian NP_delta_nTOp constraint with emcee).

name: nuisance-parameter-block-generation
description: Use when embedding a candl CMB power spectrum likelihood (SPT/ACT/Planck band-power data in .yaml info files) into a MontePython run, and you need the nuisance parameters to declare in the .param file.

name: nuisance-parameter-prior-handling
description: Use when configuring a candl likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE or Planck via clipy) and you need to disable, keep, or selectively override its internal nuisance parameter priors.

name: null-hypothesis-baseline-simulation
description: Use when testing a gamma-ray spectrum (e.g., Fermi-LAT observations of NGC 1275 or PKS 2155-304) for ALP-photon conversion features by comparing an irregularity statistic against a simulated no-ALP null distribution, rather than fitting ALP models to the spectrum.

name: null-oscillation-model-fitting
description: Use when analyzing binned count/flux spectra from a Fermi-LAT source for axion-like particle (ALP) effects, and you need an irregularity statistic (residual scatter) rather than a direct ALP-model spectral fit.

name: numerical-agreement-tolerance-verification
description: Use when two N-body or cosmology codes are run on identical initial conditions and you must quantify their agreement by forming relative power spectra P_A/P_B versus wavenumber and checking per-mille-level tolerances.

name: numerical-artifact-correction-and-curve-smoothing
description: Use when a Gibbs-minimisation condensation simulation produces molecule-abundance curves with numerical glitches or spikes, and you need clean curves before extracting condensation temperatures.

name: numerical-convergence-verification
description: Reference for validating that a FIELD (or BOUND) close-coupling run converged on a bound state at threshold and that reported external-field values are correct before reusing them downstream.

name: numerical-exact-solution-comparison
description: Use when you have numerical solutions of a conservation law (e.g. SRHD shock tubes) at several grid resolutions plus exact solution data, and you need to measure convergence, error norms, or fluctuation widths.

name: numerical-glitch-removal-curve-smoothing
description: Use when a Gibbs free energy minimisation condensation simulation (e.g. ECCOplanets) produces molecule amount-vs-temperature curves containing numerical glitches or unphysical gas-phase artefacts that must be cleaned before extracting 50% condensation temperatures (Tc).

name: numpy-array-tile-provider-implementation
description: Use when a Montblanc RIME problem exceeds the configured mem_budget and must be iterated over time tiles via HyperCube.extent_iter, requiring per-tile data sources backed by NumPy arrays.

name: numpy-binary-array-serialization
description: Use when preparing fixed input arrays for lossless-compression-ratio or read-throughput benchmarking (e.g. FITS vs HDFITS/HDF5), where every candidate format must read byte-identical synthetic integer data.

name: numpyro-prior-dict-specification
description: Use when building the prior dict for a jaxspec MCMC fit — e.g. setting Uniform(0,1) for nh, Uniform(0,5) for alpha and kT, LogUniform(1e-5,1e-2) for powerlaw norm on a 0.3–12 keV XMM-Newton PN spectrum, or background.*-prefixed priors for SpectralModelBackground.

name: observation-configuration-from-pha-file
description: Use when a real X-ray spectrum (PHA file in the OGIP standard, e.g. the XMM-Newton NGC 7793 ULX-4 PN observation) must be ingested into jaxspec with an explicit energy band before fitting or mock-data generation.

name: observational-constraint-overlay-plotting
description: Use when BBN abundance predictions have been computed over a grid of eta_B values and the goal is to compare them graphically against quasar absorption / deuterium observations and the CMB baryon-density band.

name: observer-pointing-coordinate-handling
description: Use when a simulation or binning step requires observer pointings expressed as astropy SkyCoord objects with obstime and Galactic-frame coordinates, e.g. to feed ZodiPy's zodipy.Model or bin a timestream into a HEALPix map.

name: octave-cpp-binding-generation
description: Use when exposing C library constants, functions, and classes for direct scripting from Octave, after the interface has been annotated via a SWIG -xml first pass and generate_swig_iface.py.

name: octave-cpp-dynamic-module-linking
description: Use when SWIG wrapper sources (C for -python mode, C++ for -octave mode over annotated LALSuite C headers) must be compiled and linked into dynamically loadable modules installable alongside LALSuite.

name: ode-solver-performance-visualization
description: Use when you need to quantify or visualize the execution time of ODE solves (e.g. SymBoltz k-mode sweeps, work-precision trade-offs between solvers/tolerances) or measure the speedup from multithreading the integration of independent perturbation k-modes.

name: ogip-standard-spectrum-loading
description: Use when the input is an X-ray observation delivered as a PHA file with ARF/RMF response files in OGIP format (e.g. from Hitomi or XMM-Newton) and you need to prepare it for spectral fitting in jaxspec.

name: omega-k-dispersion-curve-extraction
description: Use when you have time series of simulated electromagnetic field fluctuations from plasma wave runs and need the numerical ω(k) dispersion relation per propagation angle to verify against linear plasma-wave theory.

name: omni-solar-wind-data-extraction
description: Use when configuring Sun-to-Earth CME model inputs (e.g., OSPREI ANTEATR/FIDO runs) that require background solar wind speed, density, or magnetic field strength at the satellite location, and real-time-analogous 1 AU values rather than fine-tuned defaults are needed.

name: on-the-spot-approximation-comparison
description: Use when validating a radiative transfer code's treatment of diffuse recombination photons, or when quantifying how the on-the-spot (case B) approximation biases photo-ionization rates in a central-source Strömgren sphere.

name: one-versus-all-source-classification
description: Use when classifying SDSS/WISE photometric sources into galaxies, quasars, and stars with per-class control, and when a multi-class model is not required — the one-vs-all path in SHEEP gives per-class F1-scores of 0.992/0.967/0.985.

name: opencl-kernel-auto-tuning
description: Use when an OpenCL or other many-core kernel exposes low-level parameters (work-group size, local memory, serial per-thread work) that must be optimized per execution platform against a fixed observational workload scenario.

name: opencv-geometric-image-transforms
description: Use when a physically rendered scene image (e.g. Blender Cycles output of the 25143 Itokawa model) must be distorted with camera intrinsics to emulate a real lens, or when an applied distortion must be inverted for validation.

name: opengl-renderer-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when you need wall-clock timing figures for SISPO image generation (per-image seconds) and closed-loop GNC mission-week runs on CPU-limited hardware, to decide whether the fast OpenGL renderer suffices instead of Cycles.

name: openmp-parallel-neighbour-search
description: Use when counting object pairs or triplets in a large astronomical catalogue within a separation range, or measuring 2PCF/3PCF, and a brute-force O(N^2) neighbour search is too slow.

name: optically-thick-emission-integration
description: Use when you need fast 12CO flux predictions for hundreds of protoplanetary discs (parameter grids of surface density and characteristic radius) and can accept optically thick, factor-of-three accuracy instead of a thermochemical model.

name: optimise-then-discretise-adjoint-implementation
description: Use when gradients must be backpropagated through a neural ODE or neural CDE solve with constant memory cost, or when comparing optimise-then-discretise vs discretise-then-optimise gradient agreement on long time series.

name: orac-dr-scuba2-data-reduction
description: Use when benchmarking the HDF5-backed HDSv5 library against native HDSv4 on a real-world reduction pipeline — specifically timing the SCUBA-2 orac-dr reduction of an acquisition file that writes bulk data plus table structures in a single operation.

name: orbital-close-approach-time-series-computation
description: Use when you need the finite, positive collision time between two bodies on intersecting Kepler orbits from their orbital elements, or when simulating a Keplerian system where collisions are rare and per-pair analytic collision times enable jumping from event to event.

name: orbital-distance-parameter-sweep
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend the dependence of a giant planet's final atmospheric C/O ratio on its initial formation distance in the SimAb model, e.g. testing how positioning formation inside vs. beyond the CO ice line shifts C/O toward the solar value.

name: orbital-energy-conservation-validation
description: Use when a new or adapted symplectic integrator (isochrone splitting, Leapfrog) must be accepted/rejected based on total-energy drift of a test orbit, or when comparing energy error per unit cost between two drift-kick schemes.

name: orbital-period-measurement-from-transit-epochs
description: Use when raw or detrended light curves from one or more photometric instruments show transits of multiple planets and you need to measure orbital periods and transit depths (radii) jointly rather than per-dataset, e.g. CHEOPS + TESS multi-sector photometry of a system like HIP 29442 (TOI-469).

name: organostannane-molecular-weight-correlation
description: Use when you have extrapolated 20°C vapour pressures and molecular weights for the seven tetraorganostannanes (Me4Sn, Vi4Sn, Et4Sn, Allyl4Sn, n-Pr4Sn, i-Pr4Sn, n-Bu4Sn) and need to test or reproduce the lnP–MW QSPR.

name: organostannane-retention-data-processing
description: Use when corrected capillary-GC retention-time data for tetraorganostannanes (Shimadzu GC-15A/FID, SE-30 column) must be converted to vapour pressures via a reference compound and Clausius-Clapeyron regression, or combined with hydrocarbon literature data into lnP vs intrinsic-molar-volume QSPRs.

name: organostannane-vaporization-enthalpy-recomputation
description: Use when tabulated ΔHvap values and normal boiling points are available for organostannanes and you need to derive ΔSvap = ΔHvap/Tb, assess deviation from Trouton's rule (~90 J/K/mol), or test whether compounds with ≥5 flexible methylene-like links show elevated ΔSvap.

name: oscillation-diagnostics-extraction-from-h5part
description: Use when reproducing a FleCSPH oscillating star test across particle counts, or when validating SPH self-gravity evolution by extracting oscillation diagnostics from H5part simulation output for a diagnostics-versus-particle-number comparison.

name: oscillatory-ode-adaptive-stepping
description: Use when integrating a second-order ODE with a high or rapidly varying oscillation frequency w(t) (e.g. Airy-type w(t)=sqrt(t) on t in [1,100]) where a plain Runge-Kutta solver would need prohibitively small steps to resolve each period.

name: oscillatory-ode-numerical-integration
description: Use when numerically solving a second-order ODE with an oscillatory solution whose frequency w(t) varies slowly relative to the timescale of integration over at least part of the range (e.g. Airy, burst equation, or cosmological perturbation modes).

name: oscillatory-ode-wkb-solver-usage
description: Use when an ODE is highly oscillatory (e.g. Airy, burst, or Mukhanov-Sasaki mode equations) with w(t) and g(t) given as arrays or functions, and standard RK integration would need many steps per oscillation period.

name: oscillatory-spectrum-visualization
description: Use when computed ALP–photon conversion probabilities over the Fermi-LAT energy band must be plotted as probability-vs-energy curves to inspect oscillatory structure for sampled (g_aγ, m_a) points.

name: osprei-input-parameter-table-assembly
description: Use when configuring an OSPREI (ForeCAT/ANTEATR/FIDO) simulation of a specific CME and you must populate every input parameter with documented values and per-parameter source labels from real-time-analogous data rather than fine-tuned fits.

name: overdispersed-population-initialization
description: Use when setting up a multi-chain DE-MC (or similar population MCMC) run and you need starting populations that are wide enough for R-hat-based convergence diagnosis to be informative.

name: overlapping-data-subset-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how strongly parameter constraints from correlated or partially overlapping subsets of a CMB power-spectrum data set (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) agree, via Fisher-matrix covariances rather than full MCMC runs.

name: p3m-force-accuracy-limiter-evaluation
description: Use when reconstructing CONCEPT 1.0's global time-step scheme (e.g. Figure 2) and you need the resolution-dependent Δln a branch driven by particle clustering, for box sizes like L_box ∈ {2, 1, 1/2} × ∛N Mpc/h.

name: palm-proximal-optimization
description: Use when unmixing a hyperspectral (IFU) data cube into a fixed number of physical components whose spectra are provided by a differentiable learned model (e.g. an IAE decoder), and both amplitude and spectral shape must vary spatially under Poisson noise.

name: parallel-tempering-mcmc-sampling
description: Use when fitting Keplerian (or RV+astrometry) models to radial-velocity timeseries whose posteriors are highly multi-modal, and you need posterior sampling plus ln Z/BIC model comparison across increasing planet counts.

name: parallel-tempering-sampler-configuration
description: Use when fitting radial velocity (RV) time series with EMPEROR and multi-modal posteriors or several candidate Keplerian/activity signals (e.g. HD 55693 rotation at ~29.72 d and magnetic cycle at ~2557 d) require adaptive parallel tempering rather than plain emcee/DNS sampling.

name: parallel-timing-data-tabulation
description: Use when benchmarking MPI-parallel spectral PDE solvers across core counts and you need to tabulate per-run wall-clock timings into efficiency and weak-scaling cost tables for validation against reported scaling trends.

name: parameter-bounds-enforcement
description: Use when assembling a CosmoHammer sampling configuration from core/likelihood modules (e.g. CambCoreModule + WMAP) and sampled parameters such as H0 must remain within physically motivated min/max bounds during the chain.

name: parameter-grid-enumeration
description: Use when modelling a transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc (e.g. J1407 or PDS 110) and you need the full set of disc geometries with their theoretical light-curve gradients before applying any rejection step.

name: parameter-recovery-bias-analysis
description: Use when validating a parametric fitting procedure: synthetic data with known ground-truth parameters are available, and you need to quantify fractional bias (recovered minus intrinsic) in parameters like R_eff and M_disc across S/N, resolution, or mass regimes.

name: parameter-space-enumeration-and-filtering
description: Use when you have time-resolved transit photometry attributed to a circumsecondary disc (e.g. J1407, PDS 110) and need to constrain disc size/orientation by rejecting geometrically impossible configurations via light-curve gradient comparison.

name: parameterized-simulation-from-config
description: Use when you need a controlled synthetic time series with a known primary frequency and prescribed noise (SNR) against which a period- or frequency-finding method can be evaluated.

name: parametric-fit-construction-of-eim-coefficients
description: Use when a reduced-basis + empirical-interpolant representation of a waveform family (e.g., (2,2)-mode EOB-LAL over q∈[1,4]) already exists and the m waveform values at the m empirical time points must be fitted across the parameter dimension to produce an online-ready surrogate.

name: parent-child-force-correction
description: Use when reconstructing or testing the coupling stage of a multi-scale hierarchical N-body integrator: you have a parent particle set plus isolated child systems (e.g. planetary systems identified by syst_id > 0) that must be re-synchronised via correction kicks at each bridge time step.

name: parent-radius-parameter-sweep-validation
description: Use when validating Nemesis (or similar bridge-based multi-scale integrators) for secular dynamics: sweep PARENT_RADIUS_COEFF over orders of magnitude and confirm secular traces (e.g. ZKL) are unchanged across settings.

name: parseltongue-aips-scripting
description: Use when automating reduction or flagging of radio interferometric visibility data (e.g. UVFITS files from e-MERLIN L-band 1.3–1.8 GHz or C-band 4–8 GHz) that must be read, modified, and written back within AIPS without manual interaction.

name: partial-wave-convergence-verification
description: Use when a molscat coupled-channel run must be confirmed converged over the JTOT range (e.g. JTOT 10 to 20 step 10) and state-to-state cross sections SIG(j,j') must match reference values at a fixed collision energy such as 1250 cm-1.

name: particle-migration-jump-kick-handling
description: Use when reconstructing or extending a rung-based individual/adaptive N-body time-stepper: after rung re-assignment (acceleration criterion, eq. 42), a particle's rung changes and its kick schedule must be bridged without desynchronising positions.

name: particle-resolution-convergence-analysis
description: Use when a FleCSPH (or similar SPH) simulation must be repeated across multiple particle counts to check how oscillation or hydrodynamic diagnostics converge with resolution.

name: particle-showering-and-hadronization-simulation
description: Use when a dark matter model predicts annihilation into a multitude of final states and continuum photon spectra dN/dE per annihilation are needed for gamma-ray likelihoods.

name: particle-transport-simulation
description: Use when simulating the gas/dust environment (coma) of a comet or active asteroid from a mesh shape model, to produce a volumetric density field for physically based volume rendering in SISPO/Cycles.

name: partition-function-based-thermodynamic-property-calculation
description: Use when you need temperature-dependent specific heats or partition functions for a molecule (e.g. 1H2-16O with the POKAZATEL line list) and have access to an ExoMol/HITRAN line-list folder with states and .def files.

name: partition-function-computation
description: Use when a workflow requires internal partition functions Q(T) for a molecule/isotopologue over a temperature grid (e.g. 1 K steps up to the dataset's Tmax) and a states file with energy levels and degeneracies is available.

name: partition-function-evaluation
description: Use when you hold a molecular line list (e.g. ExoMol 1H2-16O POKAZATEL .states/.trans files) and need temperature-dependent partition function values Q(T) as input to or validation of spectroscopic property calculations.

name: partition-function-intensity-weighting
description: Use when a molecular line list (e.g. ExoMol POKAZATEL .states/.trans/.pf/.def files for 1H2-16O) must be converted into temperature-dependent absorption/emission stick intensities, i.e. when per-line LTE intensity weighting at a specified temperature in K is the analysis goal.

name: passive-tracer-advection-simulation
description: Use when you need to demonstrate reversibility of a low-Reynolds-number flow by advecting tracer fields through a time-dependent wall-driven Stokes solution and comparing initial vs final tracer configurations.

name: pca-loading-nightingale-chart-rendering
description: Use when a user has a multivariate dataset (e.g. astronomical catalogs like SDSS supernova host properties, mock galaxy catalogs, or ZENS) and needs a visual read-out of which variables drive each principal component.

name: pdr-chemical-solver-runtime-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a neural surrogate can substitute a PDR chemistry code: identical density, cosmic-ray ionisation, visual extinction (Av) and radiation-field inputs are available and per-case speedup factors must be tabulated.

name: pdr-chemistry-emulation
description: Use when the goal is to emulate or speed up 3D-PDR chemistry — e.

name: pearson-spearman-matrix-computation
description: Use when a named-column catalog (e.g. galaxy semi-analytic mock data or SDSS supernova host properties) needs pairwise variable-similarity matrices to feed hierarchical clustering under different correlation choices.

name: peculiar-solar-motion-correction
description: Use when kinematic data sets compiled under different Galactic parameters must be converted to a chosen parameter frame, and terminal velocities need the small peculiar-solar-motion correction applied consistently.

name: per-band-error-floor-modeling
description: Use when simulated light-curve flux uncertainties systematically disagree with measured uncertainties and need band-dependent sky-noise corrections plus percentage-level error floors.

name: per-class-f1-score-evaluation
description: Use when a galaxy/QSO/star classifier (e.g. SHEEP's XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost ensemble) has been trained on SDSS DR15+WISE photometry and you need per-class F1-scores to validate against the reported values or to run baseline/ablation comparisons.

name: per-order-rv-weighted-average-combination
description: Use when deriving an RV time series from echelle spectra (e.g., HARPS S2D) with the classical template-matching formulation, or when establishing a per-order baseline to diagnose whether a semi-Bayesian approach is needed.

name: per-pixel-fit-quality-mapping
description: Use when a hyperspectral host model cube has been generated from broadband photometry (e.g. PS1 grizy via CIGALE) and you need to verify per-pixel fit quality before projecting the model into SEDm observation space.

name: performance-comparison-reporting
description: Use when measuring and contrasting elapsed load time and resident memory between two I/O configurations (e.g. anonymous mmap via datMap vs direct HDF5 dataset access) for the same large dataset in one application.

name: periodic-box-domain-decomposition
description: Use when implementing or verifying the short-range pair traversal of a P3M-style N-body solver in a periodic box: you need a tiling scheme that guarantees completeness for all pairs within the cut-off x_r.

name: periodic-variability-signal-recovery
description: Use when you have a sparsely sampled, noisy time series (e.g. magnitudes with uncertainties from a synthetic or observed light curve) and need to identify a periodic frequency and visualize the folded, smoothed light curve.

name: periodogram-frequency-grid-search
description: Use when you need to identify a significant frequency in an astronomical light curve (possibly multiband, with measurement uncertainties, and with as few as ~10-100 observations) by scanning a dense frequency grid with a kernel-regression-based period-finding method.

name: perturbation-k-mode-multithreaded-integration
description: Use when reproducing or measuring the multithreading speedup of integrating many perturbation k-modes in SymBoltz, or when deciding how many Julia threads to allocate for a k-sweep of the linear Einstein-Boltzmann equations.

name: pharmacokinetic-compartment-model-simulation
description: Use when fitting a Bayesian nonlinear mixed-effects PK compartment model (e.g. Theophylline) where one-dimensional updates are inadequate and posterior percentiles of location and variance parameters are needed.

name: phase-calibrator-scan-identification
description: Use when reducing e-MERLIN interferometric visibility data whose phase-calibrator observations include stationary scans from the Lovell telescope, so these system-inherent scans are flagged before AIPS calibration.

name: phase-space-density-thresholding
description: Use when an Eulerian Vlasov or hybrid-Vlasov solver's full 3D–3V velocity grid is prohibitively large (e.g. ~10^18 cells / 4 EiB) and only a small region of velocity space carries non-negligible phase-space density.

name: phase-space-distribution-analysis
description: Use when you have a cosmological simulation particle snapshot and need to test whether the bound and unbound material around a halo form physically distinct components in phase space, virial balance, and radial extent.

name: photo-z-augmented-feature-handling
description: Use when classifying astronomical sources from SDSS and WISE tabular photometry into galaxies, QSOs and stars, and the input table lacks a distance/redshift feature: estimate photo-z first and append it as a classification feature.

name: photo-z-benchmark-comparison-table-assembly
description: Use when reported photo-z quality metrics (outlier rates, bias, rms) must be compared against published benchmark codes, e.g. to reproduce or extend the article's Table 1 comparison.

name: photo-z-estimate-feature-augmentation
description: Use when classifying astronomical sources from tabular photometry (e.g. SDSS DR15+WISE magnitudes/fluxes of millions of sources) and you want to boost classifier accuracy by adding photometric redshifts as an engineered feature before training.

name: photo-z-residual-violin-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually verify that predicted photo-zs from a fitted gamma-family GLM (log link) are non-negative, continuous, and show redshift-dependent residual scatter before reporting quality metrics.

name: photoelectron-azimuthal-distribution-sampling
description: Use when simulating IXPE (or generic X-ray polarimetry) observations and photon events must be assigned photoelectron emission angles consistent with the source polarization degree/angle, so Stokes columns Q and U can be populated in a FITS event list.

name: photoevaporation-model-intercomparison
description: Use when a confirmed planet's radius, mass, density, and host-star irradiation properties are available and you need a present-day atmospheric mass-loss estimate whose robustness against photoevaporation model choice must be tested.

name: photoheating-cooling-temperature-root-search
description: Use when computing self-consistent equilibrium temperatures (and ionization fractions) for hydrogen/helium gas irradiated by a photo-ionizing spectrum, where temperature must be solved so photoheating equals radiative cooling rather than being fixed a priori.

name: photoionization-temperature-profile-verification
description: Use when validating an analytic radiative-transfer code's H/He ionization fractions and equilibrium temperature profiles against a published benchmark (e.g. Iliev Test 2, T_eff=1e5 K blackbody, 1-10 Ryd, L_n=5e48/s) or a Cloudy run.

name: photometric-eclipse-analysis
description: Use when a transit/eclipse light curve is attributed to a circumsecondary disc (e.g. J1407 SuperWASP photometry or PDS 110 eclipse photometry) and you need to constrain the disc's size/orientation parameter space via gradient-based rejection of azimuthally symmetric disc geometries.

name: photometric-feature-engineering
description: Use when building a source-classification or photo-z pipeline from raw SDSS/WISE (or other tabular) photometry downloaded via SkyServer CasJobs and you need engineered features before model training.

name: photometric-flux-uncertainty-calibration
description: Use when simulated light-curve flux uncertainties disagree with measured uncertainties of a survey dataset (e.g. ZTF DR2 g/r/i) and you need per-band sky-noise correction factors plus percentage error floors.

name: photometric-noise-modelling
description: Use when simulated photometric flux uncertainties from a survey simulation framework (e.g. skysurvey) need to be validated against — or tuned to match — the measured uncertainties of an observed sample such as ZTF SN Ia DR2, requiring band-dependent sky-noise corrections and error floors.

name: photometric-redshift-error-metrics
description: Use when predicted photometric redshifts for a galaxy test set with known spectroscopic redshifts must be scored via bias, rms(delta-z), and catastrophic outlier rate (e.g. validating a GLM photo-z fit on PHAT0/PHAT1/SDSS data).

name: photometric-redshift-estimation
description: Use when you have a galaxy catalogue of u'g'r'i'z' (or similar multi-band) magnitudes plus spectroscopic redshifts and need fast, reliable photo-z predictions with gamma-distributed, non-negative output.

name: photometric-redshift-feature-ablation
description: Use when you need to attribute SHEEP's classification performance (F1-scores on SDSS+WISE sources) to the photometric-redshift feature by contrasting a with-photo-z run against a without-photo-z run.

name: photometric-redshift-outlier-fraction-computation
description: Use when comparing photo-z method performance via catastrophic outlier rates — e.g. tabulating GLM vs baseline codes (ANNz, BPZ, Le PHARE, TPZ, BMA) on PHAT0 or SDSS test sets under fixed Δz > 0.10 definitions.

name: photometric-redshift-regression
description: Use when you have SDSS DR15+WISE (or other tabular) photometry of astronomical sources and need per-source redshift estimates to feed as an additional feature into a galaxy/quasar/star classification pipeline.

name: photometric-source-classification-uncertainty-flagging
description: Use when a photometric source catalogue needs class probabilities plus a ranked list of ambiguous/uncertain classifications for follow-up observation selection, and when feature importances are needed to explain the classifier.

name: phylogenetic-style-dendrogram-visualization
description: Use when a correlation matrix (Pearson, Spearman, or MIC) has been converted to correlation distance d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)| and you must visualize the hierarchy of merged clusters as a color-coded dendrogram in one of the AMADA styles.

name: physically-based-path-tracing-rendering
description: Use when you need physically based, photorealistic synthetic images of a small solar system body (e.g. Itokawa shape model, comet nucleus plus smoothed number-density coma) for mission design, instrument characterisation, or computer-vision algorithm testing.

name: pinhole-camera-intrinsic-configuration
description: Use when generating synthetic imaging data for computer-vision benchmarking (e.g. SfM/3-D reconstruction) from a rendered fly-by scenario, and you must specify camera intrinsic parameters and trajectory/light settings so reconstructed poses and geometry can be compared against ground truth.

name: pipeline-control-loop-reconstruction
description: Use when rebuilding or validating a modular scientific pipeline whose stages exchange state through a shared parameter block, or when reconstructing CosmoSIS's module/DataBlock execution loop from the article or repository.

name: pixel-value-surface-plot-visualization
description: Use when point sources selected in a Highcharts scatter plot over a catalog must be inspected visually via image cutouts and surface plots of raw pixel values (e.g. vetting DECam detections across filters).

name: plane-parallel-radiative-transfer
description: Use when you need to verify a plane-parallel hydrogen ionization-front solution on a slab, or benchmark a numerical radiative-transfer solver against a closed-form column-depth solution for monochromatic irradiation.

name: planet-composition-prior-configuration
description: Decision support for choosing and running plaNETic prior options (A1–A3, B1–B3) when modelling internal structure of small planets (0.5–15 Mearth) from observed masses/radii and stellar parameters.

name: planet-host-star-matching-across-simulation-and-synthesis-catalogs
description: Use when you have stellar catalogs (metallicity, age, mass) from a galaxy simulation and need to estimate per-star or per-region planet occurrence rates from a planet population synthesis model such as NGPPS.

name: planet-occurrence-rate-aggregation-per-region
description: Use when you have planet population synthesis grids tied to stellar mass/metallicity and a simulated or observed stellar population with metallicity, age, and position, and need occurrence rates per Galactic region and planet type.

name: planet-occurrence-rate-ratio-comparison-across-galactic-regions
description: Use when occurrence rates of planet types (Earth-like, super-Earths, Neptunians, giants) must be stratified by galactic component (thin disc, thick disc, bulge, stellar halo) and host-star mass to test whether regional contrast depends on stellar metallicity correlations.

name: planet-population-synthesis-execution
description: Use when estimating planet occurrence rates (giants >300 M⊕, Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars, low-mass planets) across Galactic regions (bulge, thin disc, thick disc, stellar halo) by mapping simulated stellar metallicity/age onto planet population synthesis models.

name: planet-sample-tally-aggregation
description: Use when a task requires reproducing an exoplanet yield tally from a published survey's planet tables, assigning each catalogued planet to exactly one provenance/status category and validating counts against reported numbers.

name: planetary-atmosphere-composition-simulation
description: Use when reproducing SimAb experiments on how the initial orbital distance of a protoplanet (relative to the H2O and CO ice lines) sets the final atmospheric C/O ratio, with fixed core mass, planetesimal ratio, and dust grain fraction.

name: planetary-internal-structure-posterior-inference
description: Use when you have observed host-star and planetary parameters (mass, radius, period) for small exoplanets (0.5–15 Mearth) and need Bayesian posteriors of internal structure and composition under multiple prior configurations.

name: planetary-layer-mass-fraction-prediction
description: Use when you need interior structure posteriors (layer mass fractions and thicknesses) for a low-mass exoplanet from only mass, radius, and equilibrium temperature, and require inference in under a second on CPU without a dedicated interior model.

name: planetary-mean-density-computation-from-mass-radius
description: Use when you have published masses and radii (e.g., R_p = 6.25 ± 0.24 R_earth, M_p = 32.7 ± 5.9 M_earth) and need mean densities with propagated uncertainties for hypothesis testing between planet populations.

name: planetary-photoevaporation-modelling
description: Use when a confirmed planet's radius, mass, density, and host-star irradiation properties are available and a present-day atmospheric escape rate is required, especially to test sensitivity to the choice of photoevaporation model.

name: planetary-system-analogue-identification
description: Use when you have observed planetary parameters (radii ~3.41, 1.55, 1.54 R_earth; periods 13.6, 3.5, 6.4 days for HIP 29442) plus plaNETic posterior samples and need to infer formation pathways by scanning a Bern-model synthetic population for system analogues.

name: planetary-system-parameter-file-preparation
description: Use when a new multi-planet system with published radii (e.g. from CHEOPS+TESS joint modelling) and RVs (e.g. ESPRESSO/HIRES) must be set up as input for plaNETic internal-structure posterior runs.

name: plot-file-verification
description: Use when you need to visualise and sanity-check the output of galkin_data.py (output/vcdata.dat and output/posdata.dat) by rendering plots and confirming them against the baseline reference files.

name: plugin-module-registration-pattern
description: Use when building a cosmological (or any) MCMC likelihood pipeline on CosmoHammer and you need to plug in, order, and initialise custom core/likelihood modules with parameter-bound enforcement before sampling.

name: point-cloud-deviation-statistics
description: Use when a reconstructed 3-D model (e.g., an OpenMVS dense point cloud from SfM imagery) must be validated against a known reference surface, and error must be reported as Gaussian mean/std deviation statistics.

name: point-source-aperture-photometry
description: Use when an integrated flux density for a compact, bright point source must be measured from HEALPix I/Q/U map products (e.g., the B-Machine 37.5 GHz destriped maps) and compared to a reference instrument such as WMAP Q-band.

name: point-source-calibration-validation
description: Use when a newly destriped low-frequency microwave sky map needs absolute calibration validation against a known bright point source, or when reproducing the B-Machine '20% in I, 6% in Q' Tau A agreement check.

name: point-source-extended-source-discrimination
description: Use when preprocessing an HSC catalog extract for transient host-galaxy association and you need to retain only extended (galaxy) sources, discarding point-like (star) sources via the extended flag.

name: point-source-injection-simulation
description: Use when you need to quantify the accuracy of a transient spectrum extractor (e.g. HyperGal vs. pysedm) on IFS cubes by injecting sources of known contrast and spectrum, then measuring recovery error per contrast bin.

name: point-spread-function-convolution-mock-imaging
description: Use when generating mock observational galaxy images from radiative-transfer data cubes and need survey-realistic PSF blurring, filter throughput application, and sky background noise injection per band.

name: pointing-matrix-construction-healpix
description: Use when you need to map polarimeter timeline samples (PHI, THETA, PSI angles) onto a HEALPix grid to build the binning operator B or the destriping operator for CMB map-making.

name: poisson-likelihood-cstat-spectral-modeling
description: Use when fitting X-ray spectra (OGIP PHA/ARF/RMF, e.g. XMM-Newton or Hitomi observations) where counts are low and chi-square fitting would bias parameter estimates, or when a differentiable likelihood is needed for Bayesian inference.

name: poisson-likelihood-gradient-and-hessian-computation
description: Use when fitting physical component models to X-ray/IFU data cubes whose noise is Poisson-distributed (photon counts), and you need differentiable likelihood terms for a PALM-style optimization with explicit step sizes.

name: poisson-likelihood-optimization
description: Use when fitting photon-counting (Poisson-noise) hyperspectral X-ray data cubes with fixed, learned per-component spectral models (e.g. IAE decoders) and you need pixel-wise amplitude maps and spatially regularized spectral parameters.

name: poisson-likelihood-spectral-fitting
description: Use when the input is a photon-counting X-ray hyperspectral cube (e.g. Chandra ACIS-S, 375 channels from 3 keV to 8.48 keV) whose counts follow Poisson statistics, and you need per-pixel physical parameters (temperature, redshift, photon index) or unmixed component maps.

name: poisson-noise-signal-synthesis
description: Use when validating or reproducing Marz-style spectral smoothing: you need a noisy exponential-decay test signal with known ground truth to show that the exponential decay filter preserves peak locations better than a moving-average (boxcar) smoother.

name: poisson-pseudo-count-cube-generation
description: Use when an irregularity-based ALP spectral analysis needs null-distribution pseudo counts: input is a -fit ROI model counts map (FITS) and a scanned (ma, gaγ) grid, and output is 50,000 simulated counts cubes per parameter set plus a manifest.

name: polarimetric-spectra-preparation-for-spectro-polarimetric-fitting
description: Use when you have ixpeobssim-simulated (or released) IXPE FITS event lists containing event-by-event Q/U Stokes parameters and W_MOM weights, and need Stokes spectra ready for XSPEC spectro-polarimetric fitting.

name: polychromatic-versus-grey-background-ionization-comparison
description: Use when comparing ionization/temperature solutions of a Lyman-limit slab exposed to an isotropic background where spectral shape matters — i.e. testing grey vs. polychromatic (HM12) treatment of the meta-galactic background.

name: polynomial-basis-conversion
description: Use when a PDE discretization in a Chebyshev T_n expansion must be re-expressed in the U (ultraspherical) test basis via T-to-U conversion, with tau boundary rows and basis recombination producing banded pencil matrices.

name: population-based-multi-chain-mcmc
description: Use when sampling from a high-dimensional real-parameter posterior (e.g. Bayesian analysis) where choosing scale/orientation for a jumping distribution is hard, or WinBUGS one-dimensional updates are insufficient.

name: population-synthesis-model-dependence-assessment
description: Use when occurrence-rate ratios from a planet population synthesis (e.g. thin/thick-disc ratios per stellar host type) must be classified as robust or model-dependent before being reported.

name: positional-data-file-diff-verification
description: Use when validating that galkin_data.py reproduces its published positional data output for a specific Galactic parameter condition (e.g. R0=8.5 kpc) before trusting regenerated rotation-curve data in downstream analyses.

name: post-eruption-arcade-reconnected-flux-estimation
description: Use when a CME case run in OSPREI requires an initial flux-rope magnetic field strength (FRB/beta_M) that must be justified from observations rather than assumed, and post-eruption arcades are visible in AIA 193/304 Å data for the event.

name: post-newtonian-inspired-amplitude-phase-modeling
description: Use when building a reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate for a waveform family and you need cheap parametric fits of amplitude and phase at each empirical time node across a mass-ratio training interval (e.g., q = 1 to 10).

name: posterior-chain-constraint-extraction
description: Use when you have an array of NUTS samples drawn on Fisher-normalised parameters (e.g. from a jax.lax.scan BlackJAX loop) and need marginal means/standard deviations in physical cosmological parameter units.

name: posterior-comparison-across-samplers
description: Use when an MCMC fit (e.g. vis-r on ALMA visibility data such as hr4796.selfcal.npy) must be validated against an alternative sampler, or when an emcee posterior has insufficient independent samples and HMC convergence must be demonstrated.

name: posterior-credible-region-visualization
description: Use when you have converged MCMC posterior samples (e.g. from emcee over a 2-parameter BBN/NP likelihood) and need joint 68%/95% credible regions as a corner plot plus an upper bound value on a physical parameter.

name: posterior-distribution-aggregation
description: Use when grid/accept-reject sample posteriors exist per planet and prior option (e.g. plaNETic *_posterior.npy files) and you need weighted summary statistics (median, credible intervals) of derived quantities such as mass-loss rates.

name: posterior-estimator-computation-from-dead-points
