description: Use when you have a nested sampling run stored as dead points plus the iso-likelihood contours at which they were born (PolyChord >=1.14 'write_dead'=True output), and you need posterior inferences such as logZ or parameter means with standard error estimates on a single run.

name: posterior-mean-rmse-estimation
description: Use when validating or tuning a DE-MC / differential-evolution MCMC implementation on a known target where the true posterior mean is computable, especially the bimodal normal mixture that defeats random walk Metropolis.

name: posterior-predictive-check-visualization
description: Use when a jaxspec MCMC (NUTS) fit of a composite model such as Tbabs()*(Powerlaw() + Blackbodyrad()) to an XMM-Newton spectrum has completed and you must verify the posterior actually reproduces the observed 0.3–12 keV counts before reporting parameters.

name: posterior-summary-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have retained posterior samples from an MCMC run (e.g. CosmoHammer/emcee over WMAP 7 Lambda-CDM parameters) and need means, marginal standard deviations, and a within-tolerance comparison to a reference sampler.

name: posterior-uncertainty-table-generation
description: Use when an EMPEROR/reddemcee parallel-tempering run has finished (sim.autorun) and you need to extract median parameter values with asymmetric +/− uncertainties from datalogs into a publication-ready posterior parameter table.

name: power-law-slope-parameter-estimation
description: Use when analyzing background-dominated regions of public IXPE level-2 event lists (DETX/DETY GPD positions) to characterize the off-axis spatial distribution of the instrumental background via the fitted slope alpha.

name: power-law-walltime-regression
description: Use when benchmarking how wall time of a parallelised sampler (e.g. CosmoHammer with emcee on EC2 or a grid) scales with core count, and you need a fitted power-law exponent alpha to quantify scaling overhead.

name: power-of-two-rounding-granularity-derivation
description: Use when compressing correlated integer visibility/correlator data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder HDF5 visibilities) and you need to quantize values to a power-of-two grid without meaningfully raising thermal noise.

name: power-spectrum-construction-from-transfer-function
description: Use when building the primordial/unnormalised power spectrum from a transfer function as the first step of a halo mass function (HMF) or mass-variance calculation, and when the k-grid must be checked for convergence (k_min*R_max < 0.1, k_max*R_min > 3).

name: power-spectrum-differentiation
description: Use when gradients of cosmological observables (P(k) or D_l spectra) with respect to parameters like (h, Ω_c0, Ω_b0) are needed for Fisher forecasting, gradient-based MCMC, emulator training, or sensitivity analyses, and exact (machine-precision) derivatives are preferred over finite differences.

name: power-spectrum-emulator-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify the wall-clock evaluation cost of an analytic power-spectrum emulator relative to Boltzmann-solver (CAMB) or neural-network emulator (BACCO) references, using identical cosmologies and wavenumbers across k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc.

name: power-spectrum-estimation-from-particle-snapshots
description: Use when you have particle snapshots from cosmological N-body runs (e.g. 512 Mpc/h box, N=1024^3) and need a matter power spectrum on specified k-bins, or a cross-code P ratio (e.g. P_CONCEPT/P_GADGET) up to k ~ 13 h/Mpc.

name: power-spectrum-normalisation-sigma8
description: Use when computing an HMF, mass variance sigma(M), or differential mass function dndlnm from a linear power spectrum and the amplitude must be fixed to the observed sigma_8 (e.g. default hmf cosmology) rather than left unnormalised.

name: power-spectrum-suppression-modelling
description: Use when a CDM linear power spectrum/transfer function must be filtered to mimic warm dark matter (parameterised by m_X, g_X, Ω_X, h), e.g. to predict fewer low-mass haloes than CDM in an HMF calculation.

name: precision-recall-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised binary classifier (e.g. AGN=1 vs SFG=0 from rounded LightGBM output in output/results.csv) must be scored per class with precision/recall and validated against published reference metrics.

name: precision-reduction-rounding
description: Use when processing integrated, post-correlation radio data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder correlator frames stored as 32-bit integers) where controlled precision reduction relative to thermal noise is needed to improve subsequent Bitshuffle/LZ77 compression ratios.

name: predictive-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a learned GP covariance structure against a fixed-kernel GP baseline on time series (e.g. synthetic series with known ground-truth kernel labels), and you need both point-prediction accuracy (RMSE) and uncertainty-calibration (interval coverage) metrics.

name: present-day-mass-threshold-halo-selection
description: Use when validating or characterizing halo mass assembly history fits (e.g., diffmah residuals in dex) and you must restrict the sample to halos above a present-day mass threshold such as 10^11 Msun.

name: prf-flux-distribution-modelling
description: Use when a TESS light curve (SPOC PDCSAP or SAP from TPFs/FFIs) may be diluted by nearby stars, and you need pixel-by-pixel flux fractions, contaminant ranking, CROWDSAP/FLFRCSAP estimates, or to test whether a contaminant could explain a transit/activity signal.

name: primary-beam-correction
description: Use when a chimenea-style pipeline has produced cleaned per-epoch CASA images (from masked and open Cleans seeded by the deep-image source mask) and the epoch images must be primary-beam corrected and exported as FITS files.

name: primary-secondary-locator-annulment-logic
description: Use when implementing or porting an HDS-style API onto HDF5 (as in Starlink/hds-v5) and file-lifetime semantics must depend on distinguishing primary from secondary locators, or when named locator groups (hdsLink/hdsFlush) must be tracked.

name: primat-correction-prescription-implementation
description: Use when BBN neutron freeze-out or helium-4 abundance modeling requires weak n<->p rates beyond the Born approximation, e.g. building or validating a PRyMordial-style n_to_p_weak_rates table.

name: primordial-decoupling-physics
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or predict the four SM BBN abundances (helium-4 mass fraction, D/H, 3He/H, 7Li/H) over the full BBN temperature range and compare them with quasar-absorption and CMB-inferred observations.

name: primordial-light-element-abundance-prediction
description: Use when a task requires computing Big Bang Nucleosynthesis abundance predictions for helium-4, deuterium, helium-3, or lithium-7 that must be compared with quasar absorption or CMB-inferred baryon constraints.

name: primordial-power-spectrum-computation
description: Use when an inflationary background solution is available and the goal is the scalar primordial power spectrum P(k) over a range of perturbation modes k, requiring oscillatory mode integration from Bunch-Davies initial conditions.

name: principal-component-analysis-eigendecomposition
description: Use when a dataset of astronomical objects (e.g., SDSS supernova host-galaxy properties in CSV/TXT with named, space-separated columns) must be reduced to uncorrelated variables to explore its dominant variance directions.

name: prior-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a fitted RV model's Bayesian model comparison (Evidence vs BIC) must be checked for robustness to prior choice, or when reporting recovered activity signals (rotation, magnetic cycle) alongside an ln Z sensitivity assessment.

name: procedural-heightmap-displacement-texturing
description: Use when a plain 3-D asteroid/SSSB shape model (e.g. the 25143 Itokawa mesh) must be augmented with realistic procedural regolith, rock and crater detail for photorealistic fly-by image simulation.

name: process-log-output-parsing
description: Use when driving a command-line scientific tool (e.g. casapy) from Python via pexpect and you need to detect and report errors automatically from the tool's logged output rather than by human inspection.

name: process-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing load-time and peak-memory costs of opening GB-scale HDS/HDF5 datasets in a tool, specifically to quantify the effect of enabling vs. disabling memory mapping (datMap/datUnmap) on the HDS API layer.

name: profile-pixel-extraction-serialization
description: Use when a client needs a pixel-intensity profile (e.g. along lines of constant galactic longitude or latitude) from full bit-depth FITS/tiled-TIFF astronomy data hosted server-side, and the profile must reflect raw science values rather than the gamma/mixing-adjusted display.

name: propagation-step-interleaved-force-coupling
description: Use when a spacecraft trajectory time series propagated with SISPO/Orekit must be augmented with realistic attitude perturbations from dust impacts, atmospheric drag, or gravity-gradient torques that the perfect-attitude-control propagator ignores.

name: proper-motion-kinematic-likelihood-fitting
description: Use when a spherical stellar system mock or dataset has discrete proper motion velocities (in addition to LOS velocities) and the goal is to tighten statistical errors on the recovered density slope at R1/2 via higher-order Jeans fitting.

name: protoplanetary-disc-survey-data-comparison
description: Use when an ALMA disc survey catalog of 12CO integrated fluxes and CO-disc radii must be overlaid with semi-analytical model tracks to test agreement and quantify flux-based vs size-based sample increases.

name: protoplanetary-disk-solid-mass-diagnosis
description: Use when an observed multi-planet system has plaNETic internal-structure posteriors (e.g. xxx_posterior.npy from run_grid) and you need to infer formation history — iceline position and disk solid mass — from a Bern-model synthetic population.

name: pseudo-data-manifest-generation
description: Use when an irregularity-statistic ALP analysis needs Monte Carlo pseudo counts cubes sampled from a -fit ROI model map, plus a manifest tracking the full generated set per ALP parameter point.

name: psf-deconvolution-of-gas-profiles
description: Use when you have annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (optionally spectroscopic temperature and SZ pressure) from XMM-Newton/NASA-style observations and need PSF-deconvolved thermodynamic profiles as input to hydrostatic mass modeling.

name: published-benchmark-comparison-for-source-classification
description: Use when you need to verify that a new astronomical source-classification pipeline outperforms a published baseline (e.g. RandomForest) on an essentially identical photometric data set, using per-class F1-scores for galaxy/QSO/star classes.

name: published-transit-parameter-agreement-verification
description: Use when ground-based or Kepler transit photometry from a published study is available and the goal is to verify that an independent pipeline (e.g. TAP) recovers the published inclination, a/Rs, Rp/Rs, and per-transit Tmid values within 1-sigma.

name: pulsar-mass-posterior-integration
description: Use when a set of candidate equations of state (each with an M-R curve and maximum mass M_TOV) must be weighted by pulsar mass posteriors and NICER mass-radius data to constrain the neutron-star EOS.

name: pvrs-primitive-variable-time-integration
description: Use when solving 1D hyperbolic conservation laws (e.g. special relativistic hydrodynamics) where primitive recovery from conservative variables is costly or algebraically cumbersome, or when benchmarking a scheme's convergence order (~2) on smooth profiles such as a static Gaussian.

name: python-binding-api-exercising
description: Use when a task requires verifying documented semantics of a library object model (e.g. FrameSet as Mapping vs as Frame) by driving its Python binding with scripted mutations and recording pass/fail behaviour.

name: python-bindings-execution
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce AST paper examples (e.g. the Section 4 CmpMap of PermMap([3,1],[2,-1,1],12.2) and ZoomMap(3,4.0)) by running them programmatically via Python rather than building C code by hand.

name: python-c-extension-module-building
description: Use when SWIG-generated C or C++ wrapper sources must be compiled and linked into dynamically loadable Python/Octave extension modules inside an Autoconf/Automake build system.

name: python-c-extension-wrapper-generation
description: Use when a C library's public constants, functions, and classes must be exposed to Python (or Octave) as importable, dynamically loadable extension modules via SWIG wrapper generation.

name: python-interface-wrapping-of-legacy-cli
description: Use when you need to call a legacy or externally-maintained command-line pipeline (e.g. CASA's casapy, AMI-reduce) from Python scripts without modifying the original code, and no native Python API exists.

name: python-reference-counting-verification
description: Use when validating that Python wrappers around single-owner C libraries (e.g. LALSuite via SWIGLAL) free child objects when parents are destroyed and that reference counts behave as expected.

name: python-scientific-module-implementation
description: Use when the goal is to reconstruct or reimplement, as a runnable Python 3.10 module, how SMART assembles its model space from the four radiative transfer library types for ultraviolet-to-millimetre galaxy SED fitting.

name: python-scientific-workflow-execution
description: Use when a task requires running a documented Python program (e.g. PyExoCross) over large spectroscopic line-list data (ExoMol, HITRAN, HITEMP formats) by configuring an input file and validating its generated output tables.

name: python-spectroscopy-data-export
description: Use when a Python (Larch) XAFS workflow has produced chi(k) from autobk background subtraction and you must compute and persist the chi(R) Fourier-transform spectrum plus its window parameters as a reusable CSV artifact.

name: python-subprocess-orchestration
description: Use when a websocket-based web application must execute user-submitted tasks such that variables defined in an earlier task remain in memory for later tasks on the same connection, but each session's state must be isolated from other sessions and from the web server process.

name: pytorch-dataset-interface-design
description: Use when a PyTorch training or inference pipeline must consume a set of astronomical FITS files of varying dimensions/resolutions listed in a filelist, and normalized fixed-shape image tensors are needed as model input.

name: pytorch-module-construction
description: Use when a training pipeline must accept a user-configurable neural backbone, e.g. when input images are small/low-resolution and the full ResNet18 (layer1–layer4) is too deep, or the backbone must be chosen from a config file.

name: pytorch-neural-network-module-implementation
description: Use when you need a customizable PyTorch module for self-supervised BYOL training on unlabeled astronomical images (e.g. FITS files) and want direct control over the optimizer, augmentations, and target-network update rather than a wrapped trainer.

name: qed-radiative-correction-evaluation
description: Use when a BBN freeze-out or neutron-abundance calculation requires weak n<->p rates accurate beyond the Born approximation, or when tabulating corrected rates as a function of T_gamma/T_nu.

name: qspr-property-relationship-fitting
description: Use when you have a small (n≈7–13) compound set with measured or extrapolated vapour pressures plus a molecular descriptor (MW or intrinsic molar volume) and need to fit and validate a linear lnP–descriptor relationship.

name: qspr-transferability-assessment-hydrocarbons-to-organostannanes
description: Use when experimental property data exist for organometallic compounds (e.g. tetraorganostannane vapour pressures) and you must decide whether hydrocarbon-derived estimation methods are adequate, or when extrapolating GC-measured vapour pressures below the measured range.

name: quadratic-subpixel-peak-interpolation
description: Use when cross-correlation of preprocessed spectra against templates produces discrete peak values on a binned (Fourier-space) redshift grid, and redshift estimates must be refined beyond the bin resolution before applying heliocentric and CMB corrections.

name: quantum-bound-state-output-interpretation
description: Use when a BOUND (or bound-basic) run has finished and you need to identify converged bound-state eigenvalues in the program output and verify them against a reference output file.

name: quantum-scattering-output-validation
description: Use when a MOLSCAT calculation delegates potential terms to a user VSTAR routine via negative NTERM entries, and you must verify that the printed POTENL expansion matches the expected radial coefficients before accepting the run.

name: quasar-spectrum-template-matching
description: Use when input is generic FITS spectra (e.g. from AAOmega or any spectrograph following the Marz format) that need automatic redshifts and correlation peaks, particularly for quasars or mixed stellar/galaxy target types, including low signal-to-noise data.

name: quasigeostrophic-flow-simulation
description: Use when reproducing or extending the 3D quasigeostrophic baroclinic instability example, or when studying the statistically saturated state of a sea of compact eddies that form, merge, and break up over several dynamical times.

name: r-function-module-development
description: Use when implementing or exporting a Bayesian MCMC sampler as a reusable R function module, specifically a Differential Evolution Markov Chain (DE-MC) sampler for real parameter spaces.

name: r-weighted-stokes-equation-configuration
description: Use when reproducing low-Reynolds-number (Stokes) flow in a cylindrical annulus with a rotating inner wall, or verifying reversible tracer mixing after a fixed number of wall rotations.

name: radial-density-profile-extraction
description: Use when H5part particle snapshots from a FleCSPH (SPH) hydro run must be reduced to azimuthally/radially averaged density profiles to verify Sedov blast-wave self-similar structure in 2D or 3D.

name: radial-ionization-profile-analysis
description: Use when validating an equilibrium radiative-transfer solver against Cloudy by comparing radial profiles of xH1, xH2, xHe1, xHe2, xHe3 and temperature for a constant-density sphere with a central source.

name: radial-profile-discrete-hankel-transform-modeling
description: Use when you need fast radial-profile fitting of debris-disk (or similar) structure from high-resolution ALMA visibilities and image-plane parametric MCMC is computationally too expensive.

name: radial-profile-model-sampling
description: Use when you have visibilities exported from an ALMA ms file to text/numpy files and need posterior samples of radial-profile parameters (geometry, power/Gaussian profiles) via vis-r, deciding between emcee and stan samplers.

name: radial-profile-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you have visibilities exported from an ALMA ms file (text or .npy) of a disc and need fast posterior estimates of radial-profile parameters with fixed geometry (offsets, PA, inclination).

name: radial-profile-relative-difference-analysis
description: Use when a solved rabacus sphere/slab profile must be benchmarked against a reference ionization or temperature profile (e.g. Cloudy 13.03 Test 1) on a shared radial grid.

name: radial-profile-visibility-forward-modelling
description: Use when fitting parametric radial brightness profiles to ALMA/exported visibilities (numpy or text files from an ms) and you need model visibilities computed without ever gridding or imaging the sky.

name: radial-temperature-profile-validation
description: Use when a Sirko.SirkoAGN (or Thompson) disk model in pagn has been solved (e.g. solve_disk(N=1e4)) and you need to confirm the solution ran correctly via the paper's quick-check criteria before further analysis.

name: radial-velocity-extraction-from-ccf
description: Use when reduced echelle spectra (e.g. CARMENES VIS/NIR FITS) need precise RVs and CCF-based activity-indicator time series, and no pipeline-produced RV product is available.

name: radial-velocity-inventory-tabulation
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a published spectrograph data release inventory, e.g. you have FITS spectra or RV time series from a survey like CARMENES DR1 and must report per-target counts of spectra and RVs.

name: radial-velocity-keplerian-orbit-fitting
description: Use when a transiting planet candidate has a radial-velocity time series (e.g. HARPS measurements) plus transit photometry, and you need masses, eccentricity, and credible intervals via joint Bayesian Keplerian fitting with model selection by evidence.

name: radial-velocity-keplerian-orbit-fitting
description: Use when analysing multi-instrument RV timeseries (e.g. 51peg.vels/LICK, HIP 21850 AAT/HARPS) to detect planetary signals in highly multi-modal posteriors and return the -fitting Keplerian model automatically.

name: radial-velocity-uncertainty-statistics
description: Use when comparing the delivered RV uncertainty (not just scatter) of a template-matching pipeline against a CCF pipeline over a fixed set of spectrograph observations, and the RV files carry separate RV and drift-error columns.

name: radiative-lifetime-calculation
description: Use when you have an ExoMol line list (states and transitions files with Einstein A coefficients) and need radiative lifetimes per energy level as a post-processing product rather than spectra or cross-sections.

name: radiative-transfer-benchmarking-against-cloudy
description: Use when a new or updated equilibrium ionization/radiative-transfer solver needs code verification against an established photoionization reference (Cloudy) using a well-posed benchmark geometry with published parameters.

name: radiative-transfer-equilibrium-solver-execution
description: Use when you need equilibrium hydrogen/helium ionization fractions and temperature profiles from a central point source (e.g. T_eff=1e5 K blackbody, 1-10 Rydbergs, Ln=5e48 s^-1) in a spherically symmetric gas distribution.

name: radiative-transfer-library-combination
description: Use when building or inspecting the composite model SEDs SMART fits — e.g. reproducing how starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust library templates are combined into a single UV-to-mm SED before Bayesian MCMC fitting.

name: radiative-transfer-library-grid-alignment
description: Use when mid-IR spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer IRS spectra) must be included in an SED fit that is driven by pre-computed model libraries whose spectral resolution is coarser than the data, requiring convolution/rebinning with uncertainty propagation before fitting.

name: radiative-transfer-model-library-configuration
description: Use when fitting ultraviolet-to-millimetre galaxy SEDs with SMART and you must configure its four pre-computed radiative transfer libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust), including matching Spitzer spectroscopy resolution to the models.

name: radiative-transfer-spectrum-synthesis
description: Use when you have a converged 1D atmosphere/cloud profile (e.g. layered Mg-silicate clouds over an iron cloud from an ExoLyn relaxation run) and need to synthesize a mid-infrared spectrum to check or constrain cloud particle composition.

name: radio-continuum-flux-frequency-conversion
description: Use when the available catalogue has 1.4 GHz (or other non-150 MHz) radio continuum fluxes but the target classifier expects radiototal/radiopeak at 150 MHz, and native LOFAR 150 MHz data are unavailable.

name: radio-image-clean-deconvolution
description: Use when you have pre-calibrated radio-synthesis measurement sets (e.g. AMI-LA ALARRM datasets) and must produce cleaned epoch images whose background RMS is robustly estimated rather than assumed, or when naive fixed-threshold Clean would bias the residuals.

name: radio-interferometer-performance-ratio-computation
description: Use when comparing RIME simulator performance across problem sizes (7-192 antennas) or float precisions, or when reproducing the paper's reported speed-ups (~250x vs MeqTrees, 7.7x/12x vs OSKAR).

name: radio-interferometric-visibility-fitting
description: Use when fitting parametric radial surface brightness profiles directly to ALMA (or other radio interferometric) visibilities exported from an ms file, especially when image-plane parametric modelling is computationally too expensive.

name: radio-interferometric-visibility-flagging
description: Use when raw radio interferometric visibility data (e.g. e-MERLIN L-band 1.3–1.8 GHz or C-band 4–8 GHz observations) contain RFI-affected visibilities, antenna zero-amplitude dropouts, or Lovell phase-calibrator stationary scans that must be flagged automatically before calibration.

name: radio-interferometry-dirty-image-generation
description: Use when a Python reduction pipeline needs to drive NRAO CASA routines non-interactively — e.g. converting UVFITS to a measurement set and generating a dirty image without deconvolution — from a generic Python process.

name: radio-interferometry-visibility-data-handling
description: Use when processing large radio-interferometer visibility datasets (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder correlator frames in HDF5) that require noise-relative precision reduction to a power-of-two granularity and/or a vectorized-rounding throughput benchmark on x86.

name: radio-neutrino-detector-simulation
description: Use when you need to simulate neutrino-induced radio signals from interaction through trigger with NuRadioMC/NuRadioReco, compare Askaryan emission parameterizations, or compute effective volumes for detector design decisions.

name: radio-signal-ray-tracing-in-ice
description: Use when simulating in-ice radio neutrino detection: you have neutrino-interaction vertex positions and shower parameters from the event-generator stage and need valid ray-path solutions (path length, arrival time, amplitude factor) to each antenna position under a given ice refractive-index.

name: radio-survey-cross-matched-catalogue-handling
description: Use when a flux catalogue cross-matched to a radio survey (LOFAR 150 MHz or converted 1.4 GHz) is being prepared for MBASC classification, or when misclassifications suggest unit, header, cross-match, or waveband problems in the input CSV.

name: radio-transient-data-downsampling
description: Use when dedispersed time series (e.g. AMBER's 5120 DM trials) must be averaged over integration steps (6 in the ARTS survey) to boost single-pulse SNR before thresholding.

name: radio-transient-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when deploying AMBER on new GPU hardware or a new survey scenario (e.g. ARTS: 5120 DMs, 6 integration steps) and the optimal OpenCL low-level parameters per kernel must be measured and written to configuration files.

name: radiometer-equation-noise-estimation
description: Use when compressing correlated radio-astronomy visibility data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder HDF5 visibility stacks) and you must bound rounding-induced noise to a chosen fraction f of the radiometer-equation thermal noise before lossless compression.

name: radiometer-equation-precision-rounding
description: Use when correlator/visibility data (e.g. int32 real+imaginary pairs from instruments like the CHIME Pathfinder) must be shrunk with insignificant scientific impact by rounding precision relative to per-element thermal noise before lossless compression.

name: random-catalogue-construction
description: Use when measuring a two-point correlation function from a galaxy catalogue: a matching random catalogue must first be built using CBL's random-catalogue algorithms before DR and RR pair counting.

name: randomforest-source-classification-baseline-training
description: Use when benchmarking a new source-classification pipeline (e.g. SHEEP) against an established RandomForest classifier on essentially identical tabular photometric data and per-class F1-scores must be reproduced.

name: randomized-initial-condition-sampling
description: Use when you need to map how randomized initial conditions (initial orbital distance, core mass, planetesimal ratio, dust grain fraction) determine a giant planet's final atmospheric metallicity (subsolar vs supersolar, ratio <1 vs >1) or C/O ratio in SimAb.

name: rate-distortion-curve-generation
description: Use when comparing error-bounded lossy compressors on image or volume datasets (e.g., FITS solar EUV images) and you need compression-ratio-vs-distortion trade-off curves to select or rank a compressor.

name: raw-data-normalization-caveat-awareness
description: Use when a workflow reads galkin's raw data products — output/rawdata.dat or galkin/data/data_*.dat — or original published tracer measurements, and must decide whether they can be compared or combined directly with normalized outputs.

name: reaction-network-performance-extraction
description: Use when a paper or figure reports hardware speedups (e.g., Tesla P100 GPU vs. a single Power8 core on Summitdev) for multiple reaction networks across several grid sizes, and the goal is to reproduce/serialize those numbers with their limitations.

name: real-time-pipeline-deployment-reporting
description: Use when a paper states a production deployment of a pipeline (e.g. AMBER in the ARTS survey) in prose — nodes, GPUs, beams, DMs, integration steps — and the goal is to extract and tabulate those exact figures.

name: recombination-radiation-transfer-transport
description: Use when reproducing or validating an isotropic recombination-radiation sphere test (e.g. Raičević et al. 2014 Fig. 8): a uniform-density H cloud with a central point source where diffuse vs. direct photo-ionization rates must be compared.

name: red-noise-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting a transit light curve whose residuals may contain correlated (red) noise, and you need honest parameter uncertainties rather than chi-squared-based errors that assume purely white noise.

name: redshift-binned-classification-evaluation
description: Use when you have classifier predictions plus true labels and redshifts for a test set and need to quantify how classification performance (precision/recall) varies across redshift bins rather than only over the full sample.

name: redshift-cut-sample-selection
description: Use when a catalog of classified SNe Ia must be restricted to a volume-limited subsample, and the redshift limit should be justified by the redshift dependence of SALT2 stretch and colour rather than chosen arbitrarily.

name: redshift-dependence-analysis
description: Use when a simulated or observed SN Ia survey sample needs a redshift limit defining its volume-limited (unbiased) regime, by checking whether fitted SALT2 stretch and colour show redshift trends within the DR2 redshift range.

name: redshift-quality-of-match-grading
description: Use when assigning suggested quality operators (QOP) to automatic spectroscopic redshift matches, e.g. OzDES/AAOmega spectra scored by cross-correlation peak heights, or when reproducing Marz's autoz-style FOM thresholds.

name: redshift-residual-binned-scatter-analysis
description: Use when you have predicted photo-zs and spectroscopic redshifts from a gamma-family GLM (log link) fit on PCs of galaxy magnitudes and need to verify non-negativity and redshift-dependent residual scatter.

name: redshift-residual-validation-against-simulation-truth
description: Use when you have simulated SEDm cubes with known input host redshifts and want to verify that a redshift measured from the HyperGal-isolated host component is consistent with simulation truth.

name: redshift-space-power-spectrum-modelling
description: Use when reconstructing a model redshift-space 2PCF ξ(s) from a power spectrum with RSD, de-wiggled BAO wiggles, and Gaussian redshift errors, e.g. for BAO fitting with CosmoBolognaLib.

name: reduced-3pcf-normalization
description: Use when measuring higher-order clustering of a simulated or observed galaxy/halo catalogue, specifically when ζ and the reduced 3PCF Q are needed as functions of triangle opening angle θ at fixed sides r12, r13.

name: reduced-basis-error-comparison
description: Use when a greedy reduced basis has been built over a waveform training set (e.g., 501 EOBNRv2 waveforms with q in [1,2]) and you must verify that m empirical time nodes reconstruct waveforms to within the greedy error and a guaranteed error bound.

name: reduced-chi2-map-goodness-of-fit
description: Use when you need a goodness-of-fit metric proving that a timestream filtering step (e.g. destriping with 60-second baselines) removed low-frequency correlated noise without biasing the signal, given HEALPix residual maps for I/Q.

name: reference-implementation-consistency-check
description: Use when you have independently derived a rounding granularity g and precision-reduced radio data from Equations 14-16 and must confirm your values match the authors' kiyo-masui/bitshuffle example before trusting downstream compression results.

name: reference-output-comparison
description: Use when a locally built molscat, bound or field variant must be validated against the documentation's example outputs before production use, or when confirming documented values such as eigenphase-sum resonances or bound-state energies.

name: reference-output-consistency-checking
description: Use when a tool is supposed to reproduce known reference outputs (e.g. after re-running a conversion under new Galactic parameters R0=7.5 or 8.5 kpc) and you must confirm the regenerated files match shipped samples.

name: reference-output-diff-comparison
description: Use when a paper prints a human-readable reference listing (e.g. an AST Channel block-structured serialisation) and the goal is to reproduce that exact text with library code and validate it by diff.

name: reference-solution-error-norm-computation
description: Use when comparing implicit ODE solvers or tolerance settings on a stiff system (e.g. the Einstein-Boltzmann background) and you need a quantitative, solver-independent accuracy metric rather than trusting each solver's own tolerance claims.

name: refractive-index-medium-modeling
description: Use when simulating in-ice radio-neutrino detection where signal propagation depends on the medium's depth-dependent index-of-refraction profile, e.g. ray-tracing neutrino-interaction vertices to antennas in NuRadioMC.

name: region-based-mapping-routing
description: Use when a coordinate transformation must vary spatially across the coordinate space, and positions falling in different Regions need to be dispatched to different route Mappings via the Starlink AST library.

name: regression-l2-loss-evaluation
description: Use when comparing neural differential equation models on irregularly sampled time-series regression tasks (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) and you must report test-set L2 loss (mean ± std over seeds) plus training time.

name: regression-verification-against-reported-statistics
description: Use when a paper reports a fitted equation (e.g. lnP = -5.82e-2 MW + 12.27, r = 0.99) together with a small table of raw values, and you need to independently reproduce the fit before reusing its coefficients.

name: regular-gmf-component-modeling
description: Use when computing photon-ALP conversion probabilities for an extragalactic source like NGC 1275 where the propagation chain is dominated by the cluster magnetic field (ICMF, ~1–10 μG, turbulent) plus a regular GMF component.

name: reheating-consistent-parameter-inference
description: Use when you need slow-roll inflationary predictions for a definite single-field model that consistently marginalize over the unknown reheating energy density, e.g. to feed a CMB likelihood or Bayesian model comparison.

name: reheating-consistent-prediction-sweep
description: Use when you need numerical slow-roll predictions (n_s, r) for one specific single-field inflationary model as a function of the reheating energy density, e.g. to fill model tables or feed Bayesian model comparison.

name: rejection-fraction-tabulation
description: Use when you have per-star rejection tables from a BeyonCE gradient-rejection run over azimuthally symmetric disc geometries and need to quantify, per star, what fraction of mapped disc orientations remain viable.

name: relative-deviation-accuracy-analysis
description: Use when validating a physics/chemistry emission model against published reference predictions by comparing per-line emissivities and summarising the maximum relative deviation per spectral series.

name: relative-error-quantification-between-codes
description: Use when validating that a new solver reproduces a reference code's outputs for matched physical quantities on a common grid, and you need per-quantity maximum-error metrics against documented tolerances.

name: relativistic-blastwave-dynamics-integration
description: Use when reconstructing or extending the GRB afterglow forward model for GRB170817A-style data — i.e. when a structured-jet synthetic lightcurve is needed as the EM afterglow component of a simultaneous NMMA analysis.

name: relativistic-hydrodynamics-conservative-variable-formulation
description: Use when solving relativistic hydrodynamics with discontinuous solutions (shock tubes, relativistic Sod problems) where the discretisation must be conservative to converge to the physically correct weak solution.

name: relativistic-hydrodynamics-flux-computation
description: Use when solving hyperbolic conservative PDEs (e.g. relativistic Euler equations) on a finite-volume grid and a per-interface numerical flux f_HLL must be computed from left/right states qL, qR, their fluxes fL, fR, and bounding wave speeds λL, λR.

name: relativistic-hydrodynamics-shock-tube-simulation
description: Use when validating a conservative finite-volume solver for special relativistic hydrodynamics: 1D Sod shock-tube initial states must be evolved at multiple resolutions and L1 errors and convergence order quantified.

name: relativistic-raytracing-pulse-profile-synthesis
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking neutron star pulse-profile synthesis (e.g., Devarshi et al. 2024 scenarios a–d or OS1 test cases) that requires relativistic ray-traced surface integration folded through a detector response matrix.

name: remote-server-image-serving
description: Use when a user needs to view or interact with a very large (>2 Gb) FITS image stored on a remote server or cluster directly in a browser, without downloading the file or installing local visualization software.

name: renormalization-group-coupling-running
description: Use when you have high-energy couplings of DM to SM fields in a vector-mediator simplified model plus a mediator mass, and you need low-energy direct-detection operator coefficients or RG-mixing-corrected cross section bounds.

name: renormalization-group-operator-mixing-comparison
description: Use when translating high-energy couplings of a vector (e.g. axial-vector) mediator to low-energy DM-nucleon couplings, and you need to assess whether operator mixing shifts derived direct detection bounds (e.g. by a factor of two or more for SD cross sections).

name: resolution-convergence-analysis
description: Use when comparing spectral vs. finite-volume accuracy for an instability benchmark, or when determining the minimum grid/mode count (e.g., 2048^2 spectral modes vs. 16384^2 finite-volume cells) needed to suppress unphysical secondary instabilities.

name: resolution-dependent-model-agreement-analysis
description: Use when validating a new or faster galactic kinematic modelling tool against an established code, or when you need to know how beam smearing (PSF FWHM relative to R_eff) affects agreement between two mock-observed rotation/dispersion curve predictions.

name: retention-ratio-vapour-pressure-analysis
description: Use when isothermal GC retention times (40–120°C, 20°C increments) are available for a homologous compound series plus a reference compound with known ΔHv, and relative vaporization thermodynamics are needed.

name: reverse-mode-automatic-differentiation
description: Use when a loss depends on the solution of a neural ODE or neural CDE solve in Diffrax/JAX and gradients w.r.t. y0 or parameters are needed, especially when long time series would exhaust memory with discretise-then-optimise.

name: reverse-mode-automatic-differentiation-implementation
description: Use when a scalar loss function (e.g. weighted χ² over P(k) on a log-spaced k-grid) must be differentiated with respect to many cosmological parameters and forward-mode AD is too slow, i.e. gradient-based MCMC, Fisher forecasting or emulator training in large parameter spaces.

name: reversible-heun-step-implementation
description: Use when a Stratonovich neural SDE or reversible ODE solver needs a step map whose reverse step reconstructs the initial state to machine precision, or when convergence order/stability-region claims must be empirically reproduced.

name: rfi-flag-pipeline-integration
description: Use when reducing e-MERLIN interferometric visibility data where, beyond RFI flagged by SumThreshold, antenna zero-amplitude dropouts or Lovell phase calibrator stationary scans must also be flagged before AIPS calibration.

name: rfi-sumthreshold-flagging
description: Use when processing e-MERLIN (or any radio interferometric array) UVFITS visibility data where RFI contamination — typically <20%-25% at L-band (1.3-1.8 GHz) or <5% at C-band (4-8 GHz) — must be flagged before calibration.

name: rice-coding-compression
description: Use when benchmarking lossless compression ratios and compression times of image/array datasets across FITS Rice (FPACK) and HDF5 filters (LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP) to decide between FITS and HDFITS storage.

name: rime-chi-squared-visibility-computation
description: Reference for computing model visibilities and a single chi-squared value from a radio interferometry sky model (point/gaussian/beta sources) via the RIME, especially when unit-testing a GPU kernel against a numpy CPU reference or feeding likelihoods to Bayesian sampling.

name: rime-ek-kernel-source-loop-extension
description: Use when adding a new source type (e.g. beta profiles, mentioned as future morphology) to Montblanc's EK kernel and you must verify GPU per-antenna terms and chi2 correctness.

name: rime-kernel-pipeline-context-understanding
description: Reference for interpreting Montblanc CUDA kernel profiling (EK and B Sum kernels) on an NVIDIA K40, or when structuring RIME evaluation into per-antenna and per-baseline GPU kernels before collecting occupancy or bandwidth metrics.

name: rime-per-antenna-coherency-computation
description: Use when simulating radio-interferometric visibilities from a sky model of point and Gaussian sources, or when a χ²/likelihood must be computed from model vs observed visibilities for Bayesian inference (BIRO).

name: ring-transit-light-curve-gradient-computation
description: Use when modelling transits of circumsecondary disc systems (e.g. J1407, PDS 110) where all possible disc geometries must be enumerated and a theoretical light-curve gradient per ring crossing the star is needed prior to rejecting configurations.

name: rms-error-computation-against-reference-continua
description: Use when benchmarking spectrum-normalisation output against known reference continua — e.g. deposited test-star spectra (O to G type) or synthetic spectra with trusted continua — to reproduce an RMS-error table.

name: rmse-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a simulated hyperspectral cube with known ground-truth component maps is available and you must quantify whether a new unmixing/fitting method (e.g. SUSHI) reconstructs component spectra more accurately than a baseline (e.g. pixel-by-pixel 1D fit).

name: robust-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when correlated multi-band magnitudes (e.g. PHAT0 u'g'r'i'z' or SDSS DR10 photometry) must be compressed into uncorrelated PCs before fitting a gamma GLM with log link for photo-z prediction.

name: robust-pca-projection-pursuit-estimation
description: Use when a tabular astronomical catalog (e.g., CSV/TXT with named columns) may contain outliers or non-Gaussian structure that would distort standard PCA, and you need dimension reduction with loadings and scores robust to such contamination.

name: robust-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when magnitudes fed into a regression (e.g. photometric redshift GLM) are correlated and you need uncorrelated explanatory variables computed robustly on combined training+test data.

name: rocky-planet-bulk-composition-analysis
description: Use when you have equilibrium condensation simulation results (molecule amounts vs temperature) and host-star elemental abundance patterns, and need to derive condensation temperatures (Tc) and rocky planet bulk compositions/devolatilisation trends.

name: romberg-numerical-integration-convergence-testing
description: Use when a halo mass function or σ(M) calculation must be verified for integral convergence: i.e. when you need to check whether chosen k-bounds and kR ranges capture ≥95% of the window-function integral before trusting the HMF output.

name: rotating-bar-frame-dynamics
description: Use when the goal is a stationary gas-dynamic flow in a barred galaxy: isothermal Euler equations in 2-D with a galactic potential plus a rotating weak bar source term, to be solved in Matlab.

name: rotation-curve-forward-modelling
description: Use when you need to model or fit a 1D galactic rotation curve of a rotationally supported (V/sigma_0 >= 2) axisymmetric disk galaxy, and must correct for beam smearing given a sky orientation and instrumental PSF.

name: rotation-curve-visualization
description: Use when you have galkin output files (output/vcdata.dat and output/posdata.dat) from a galkin_data.py run and need demonstrative figures of tracer spatial distribution and the Milky Way rotation curve.

name: rounding-error-distribution-validation
description: Use when nearly-losslessly rounding integer visibility/correlator data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder HDF5 visibility sets) and you must verify the rounding noise stays negligible relative to thermal noise.

name: runge-kutta-hybrid-step-switching
description: Use when integrating a second-order linear ODE x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 whose frequency is high or rapidly oscillatory on part of the range but slowly varying elsewhere, and standard RK stepping would be prohibitively expensive.

name: runge-kutta-method-of-lines-time-integration
description: Use when a conservative hyperbolic system (e.g. 1D SRHD charges q=(D,Sx,τ)) has been discretised in space with a finite-volume update and needs stable, higher-order-in-time evolution with CFL-safe step control.

name: runtime-benchmark-measurement
description: Use when a new fitting or analysis pipeline's computational cost must be compared against a reference method on a fixed sample, e.g. showing that SMART's radiative-transfer-only fitting of 42 HERUS ULIRG SEDs takes comparable time to popular energy balance methods.

name: runtime-benchmarking-and-profiling
description: Use when measuring how a dependency-aware incremental-update (caching) strategy reduces recomputation time versus recomputing all quantities, e.g. timing hmf's update() cascades.

name: runtime-performance-measurement
description: Use when a paper or README states a concrete runtime figure for an example script and the claim needs independent verification, e.g. vis-r's minimal example completing its MCMC fit in under 10 s.

name: runtime-scaling-analysis
description: Use when you need to empirically verify the asymptotic scaling of a numerical kernel (e.g., FMM vs. direct summation) by sweeping particle count N and a tuning parameter such as the multipole acceptance criterion (MAC) angle.

name: runtime-scaling-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a tool's compute cost (runtime, memory) scales acceptably with dataset size, e.g. before applying gallifrey to large time series from future missions such as PLATO.

name: rv-output-file-parsing
description: Use when you have S-BART output .txt files from ESPRESSO (or HARPS) observations and need to load, correct (SA subtraction, quadrature drift-error propagation), and unit-convert the RV time series before computing median uncertainties or running a GLS periodogram.

name: rv-scatter-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you have RV time series from two extraction methods (e.g., S-BART template matching vs ESO DRS CCF) on the same instrument frames and need a scatter-based precision comparison per stellar type.

name: rv-time-series-precision-comparison
description: Use when you have RV time series from multiple template-matching pipelines (S-BART, HARPS-TERRA, SERVAL) on the same spectrograph dataset and need to compare their scatter/precision quantitatively.

name: salt2-lightcurve-fitting
description: Use when you need per-object SALT2 stretch and colour from multi-band SN Ia light curves, or when you must locate the redshift above which survey selection effects bias fitted light-curve parameters.

name: sampler-stopping-criterion-computation
description: Decision support for stopping or comparing MCMC runs: given autocorrelation times, walker counts, burn-in and sample lengths, determine whether the sample has reached a target error regime (e.g. the 10% level) versus a competing sampler's tuning endpoint.

name: sampling-rate-cost-scaling-analysis
description: Use when comparing wall-clock timing of a fast surrogate waveform evaluation against the standard EOB solver as a function of time-sampling rate, to verify O(mL + m*c_fit) linear-in-L scaling and compute per-rate speedup ratios.

name: saturation-state-evaluation
description: Use when building or extending an ExoLyn reaction network: new condensation reactions must be added to parameters.txt and their Gibbs formation energies sourced so equilibrium vapor concentrations, saturation states, and condensation rates can be evaluated.

name: sbdf2-timestepper-execution
description: Use when a 1D initial value problem with nonlinear terms must be time-integrated with a second-order semi-implicit scheme, e.g. simulating soliton propagation/scattering on a multi-segment graph with coupled Chebyshev segments.

name: scalar-field-cosmological-phase-transition-analysis
description: Use when a scalar-field potential (1D/2D test models, singlet, R2HDM/C2HDM/N2HDM) must be analyzed for cosmological phase transitions and critical temperatures.

name: scale-factor-temperature-relation-computation
description: Use when the analysis requires a first-principles thermal history (T_gamma, T_nu, scale factor a) through the BBN epoch, or a benchmark SM value of the effective number of relativistic degrees of freedom N_eff and Omega_nu h^2 including non-instantaneous neutrino decoupling.

name: scattering-length-curve-analysis
description: Use when a low-energy (e.g. 100 nK) atom–atom collision calculation reports scattering lengths as a function of a scanned external variable such as a magnetic field, and you must locate poles/resonances in the curve.

name: schirmer-aperture-mass-filter-convolution
description: Use when a galaxy positions+ellipticities shear catalog must be turned into an aperture mass map for cluster detection, and an NFW-motivated radial filter (Schirmer 2007) with exponential cut-offs is appropriate.

name: scientific-array-io-performance-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify I/O performance of large multi-dim scientific arrays stored in FITS vs chunked/compressed HDF5, especially for random z-axis slice reads vs full-file reads.

name: scientific-result-extraction-from-article
description: Use when a task card asks to reproduce or enumerate an article's science-results summary (e.g., Figure 6 of Zingale et al. 2018) and requires each qualitative claim tied to a citation location in machine-readable form.

name: scientific-table-structuring
description: Use when a paper reports per-problem-size performance numbers (timings, speed-ups across precisions or configurations) that must be tabulated, computed into ratio columns, and exported for downstream benchmark analysis.

name: sde-solver-configuration-reversible-heun
description: Use when training or sampling a neural SDE (e.g. an SDE-GAN generator) in JAX/Diffrax and you need a memory-reversible stochastic solver matched to the paper's recipe: reversible Heun with unit step size.

name: sdss-sql-catalogue-querying
description: Use when a pipeline needs the SDSS DR10 galaxy catalogue (u'g'r'i'z' magnitudes plus spectroscopic redshifts) as raw input for photo-z estimation, PCA decomposition, or GLM training/testing splits.

name: sdss-wise-photometric-classifier-training
description: Use when classifying astronomical sources into galaxies, quasars and stars from tabular SDSS+WISE photometry (optionally augmented with photo-z) and you need the ensemble-combined classifier rather than a single base learner.

name: sed-component-modeling
description: Use when reconstructing or decomposing a galaxy SED into starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust radiative transfer components, e.g. to reproduce SMART's model space before Bayesian MCMC fitting.

name: sed-fitting-input-preparation
description: Use when SED fitting must combine spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer IRS spectra) with photometry and radiative transfer model libraries whose wavelength grids are coarser than the observed spectra, requiring convolution/rebinning first.

name: sedm-ifu-spectrum-extraction
description: Use when a reduced SEDm (SEDmachine) IFU data cube of a ZTF transient is contaminated by host-galaxy flux near the host core, and a clean SN spectrum is needed for SNID typing.

name: sedm-spectral-rebinning
description: Use when a CIGALE-based hyperspectral host model must be matched to SEDm low-resolution IFS data: the model cube's native spectral grid differs from the SEDm ~26 A/px sampling and [3700, 9300] A domain and must be rebinned before scene-model fitting.

name: selectable-backbone-wrapping
description: Use when building a BYOL-based self-supervised pipeline for astronomical images and you need to choose or substitute the encoder backbone — e.g. trading the full ResNet18 for an earlier truncation like layer2 on small or single-channel FITS images.

name: self-gravitating-hydrodynamics-simulation
description: Use when the task requires evolving 3D hydrodynamic systems with Newtonian self-gravity (e.g., oscillating stars, single/binary stars) via SPH and need reproducible particle evolutions across particle counts.

name: self-gravitating-particle-system-evolution
description: Use when a 3D self-gravitating particle problem (e.g. single/binary stars, Noh 3D) must be evolved under Newtonian gravity with SPH, with initial data generated and snapshots stored in H5part.

name: self-similar-sedov-solution-comparison
description: Use when verifying or benchmarking an SPH/hydro code on a strong point-explosion problem: the goal is to check that a simulated blast wave reproduces the canonical self-similar Sedov density structure in 2D or 3D.

name: self-supervised-byol-embedding-extraction
description: Use when you have a directory of unlabeled FITS images of astronomical objects (e.g. ALMA disks or Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark clouds) and need morphology-based embeddings without manual labels.

name: self-supervised-byol-loss-design
description: Use when you need to pretrain image embeddings without labels from unlabeled astronomical FITS imagery (e.g., ALMA protoplanetary disk images, Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark cloud images), and want a flexible BYOL module rather than a fixed pipeline.

name: self-supervised-byol-training
description: Use when you have a large collection of unlabelled astronomical images (e.g. ALMA protoplanetary disk or Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark cloud FITS files) and need morphology-aware embeddings for clustering, anomaly detection, or similarity-based exploration.

name: self-supervised-embedding-inference
description: Use when a trained astromorph network checkpoint (.pt) exists and you need embedding vectors for a new batch of FITS images — e.g. ALMA protoplanetary disk images — to inspect morphological groupings.

name: self-supervised-encoder-setup
description: Use when preparing BYOL pretraining of an encoder on FITS images (e.g. ALMA protoplanetary disk or Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark cloud data) and you must select a backbone (network_name) or truncate ResNet18 at a chosen stage such as layer2.

name: semi-analytical-disc-structure-modelling
description: Use when 12CO (J=2-1 or similar) line fluxes are needed for population-scale disc samples (hundreds of discs) and running thermochemical codes like DALI per disc would be prohibitively time-consuming.

name: semi-lagrangian-slice3d-advection-remapping
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing a hybrid-Vlasov solver's propagation step: translating a 6D distribution function in configuration space and accelerating it in velocity space, requiring flux-conservative semi-Lagrangian remapping decomposed into 1D shear-column passes.

name: sensitivity-analysis-of-initial-conditions
description: Use when you need to test whether a specific SimAb initial condition (core mass, initial orbital distance, planetesimal ratio, or dust grain fraction) changes the final atmospheric composition (C/O ratio and metallicity relative to solar) while other inputs are held fixed.

name: sequential-monte-carlo-posterior-sampling
description: Use when the input is a time series (e.g. stellar variability or exoplanet transit light-curve time/flux measurements) and the GP covariance function should be inferred from the data rather than specified explicitly by the user.

name: server-side-image-processing-pipeline
description: Use when serving very large (terabyte-scale) floating-point astronomy images to web clients and you need real-time image setting adjustments without shipping full bit-depth data to the browser.

name: session-identifier-keyed-resource-tracking
description: Use when a Tornado-based web application must keep a user's variables alive across sequential tasks sent over one websocket, while preventing other browser windows or tabs from reading that state.

name: shakura-sunyaev-accretion-disk-solving
description: Use when you need a parametric 1D AGN disk model (temperature, surface density, accretion-rate profiles) for a given black-hole mass, Eddington ratio le, and viscosity alpha — e.g. as input for stellar/binary evolution in AGN disks or migration-torque calculations.

name: shakura-sunyaev-alpha-disk-configuration
description: Use when a 1D steady AGN accretion-disk profile (temperature, density, scale height) must be generated under the alpha-disk prescription for embedded-object torque or luminosity calculations.

name: shared-library-linking-against-lalsuite
description: Use when a SWIG second pass (-python or -octave mode) has produced wrapper sources over annotated LALSuite C headers and the next step is turning those sources into importable/loadable modules.

name: shear-decomposed-offset-rotation-subcycling
description: Use when implementing or porting a semi-Lagrangian Vlasov solver in which the velocity mesh must be rotated/offset relative to the configuration-space grid, and the rotation angle per Strang-split step may exceed the stability-preserving limit.

name: sheath-inclusion-in-synthetic-insitu-profiles
description: Use when producing ensemble in situ predictions for CME arrival at a synthetic spacecraft and the validation requires the maximum Kp to occur in the sheath, or when comparing predicted B and Bz extrema against OMNI observations that include sheath structure.

name: sherpa-spectral-model-timing
description: Use when adopting or training a learned spectral surrogate (e.g. an IAE decoder) and you need to justify that a surrogate evaluation is faster than calling the physical look-up-table model (XSpec in Sherpa) per spectral evaluation.

name: shock-compression-ratio-analysis
description: Use when assessing whether a collisionless-shock simulation departs from fluid (MHD) theory at resolutions comparable to the terrestrial bow shock (~1000 km), by comparing compression ratios near ~4x bow-shock intensification across grid resolutions.

name: shock-tube-riemann-problem-setup
description: Use when validating a numerical scheme for 1D special relativistic hydrodynamics (1DRHD) against a known exact solution: a shock tube with a discontinuity at x = 0.5, evolved under the CFL bound lambda*dt/dx < 1 (Eq 40).

name: shomate-parameter-fitting
description: Use when tabulated enthalpy/entropy data contain discontinuities (multi-phase reference states) and you need continuous thermochemical functions S(T), H(T), G(T) for Gibbs free energy minimisation.

name: sigma-clipping-rejection
description: Use when preprocessing AAOmega-format FITS spectra (flux, variance, wavelength extensions) before the automatic matching algorithm runs, and pixel-level outliers such as cosmic rays, NaNs, negative flux/variance values, or a strong continuum need masking, replacement, or clipping.

name: sigma-deviation-significance-computation
description: Use when a refit of transit photometry (e.g. joint CHEOPS+TESS modelling) yields a planetary radius with an uncertainty, and you need to quantify its inconsistency with a discovery-paper value in units of sigma against a threshold such as 3σ.

name: sigma8-as-inversion
description: Use when an analysis needs fast sigma8 <-> As conversion across a sampled LambdaCDM cosmology grid, or when verifying the published 0.1% accuracy of the analytic sigma8 expression against CAMB.

name: sigma8-emulator-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need a fast, closed-form σ8 ↔ A_s conversion for a sampled ΛCDM cosmology and must first verify that the analytic expression matches CAMB to ~0.1% RMS fractional error over the same parameter domain as the Bartlett et al. 2023 P(k) emulator.

name: simd-intrinsic-vectorization
description: Use when a scalar per-element transform (rounding to powers of two per Equation 16, or bit-transpose of typed arrays) is the throughput bottleneck and the target x86 CPU supports SSE2 or AVX2.

name: simulated-versus-measured-lightcurve-residual-analysis
description: Use when simulated light-curve flux uncertainties must be matched to measured survey uncertainties (e.g. ZTF DR2 g/r/i photometry) and you need per-band sky-noise correction factors and error floors validated via residual statistics.

name: simulation-ensemble-generation
description: Use when you need to gauge statistical properties of IXPE polarization estimates—e.g., posterior distributions, pull distributions, or spectro-polarimetric fit biases—by Monte Carlo sampling many realizations of the same observation rather than analyzing a single simulated event list.

name: simulation-field-visualization
description: Use when a Dedalus (or similar spectral-solver) simulation has written HDF5 snapshot files and a 2D physical field such as density must be extracted and rendered as an image to confirm resolved flow features.

name: simulation-halo-catalog-analysis
description: Use when a task requires connecting halo assembly histories from a simulated halo catalog (e.g., TNG) to large-scale environment density, or quantifying assembly bias and model residual correlations.

name: simulation-output-aggregation
description: Use when you have COMPAS (or similar BPS) simulation output for multiple model variants and metallicities and need per-model BBH merger counts, normalized rates, and model-comparison tables.

name: simulation-output-aggregation-across-disc-components
description: Use when you have per-star properties (metallicity, age, Galactic component assignment) from a galaxy-formation simulation and need component-resolved occurrence rates for different planet classes rather than a galaxy-wide average.

name: simulation-output-tabulation
description: Use when the goal is to compare multiple radio-emission models/parameterizations for neutrino-induced showers in NuRadioMC while holding the shower, propagation, and antenna configuration fixed, and the deliverable is one spectrum entry per emission model in a unit-consistent table.

name: simulation-population-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have per-halo growth-history residuals from a model fit to merger trees and need to test whether those residuals are uncorrelated with environmental variables such as local density.

name: simulation-results-table-generation
description: Use when you have standardized outputs from an ensemble simulation (e.g., OSPREI '.ens' runs for CMEs) and need to tabulate which input-output pairs exceed a correlation coefficient cutoff, producing per-case correlation tables.

name: simultaneous-multi-transit-parameter-sharing
description: Use when you have two or more transit light curves of the same planet observed under different conditions (cadence, filter/limb darkening, weather) and want one shared system-parameter set with a free mid-transit time per transit.

name: single-core-throughput-benchmarking
description: Use when measuring single-core write/read throughput (MiB/s) of a rounding or compression routine on radio-telemetry visibility data, or when validating a vectorized (SSE2/AVX2) variant against a scalar baseline.

name: single-precision-reference-validation
description: Use when a GPU/CUDA scientific kernel (e.g. Montblanc's EK, B Sum and reduction kernels) must be verified against an independent CPU reference implementation, especially when outputs are single-precision floats like χ2.

name: single-vs-double-precision-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a GPU kernel pipeline (e.g. Montblanc's EK and B Sum kernels on a K40) and you need to quantify how float vs double precision changes runtime, occupancy, and speed-ups against reference implementations.

name: sky-background-noise-from-limiting-magnitudes
description: Use when generating mock observational images for surveys like CSST, HST, JWST, Roman, HSC (or Euclid, filters only) and you must add per-band background noise to SKIRT ideal data cubes, or derive noise levels from survey limiting magnitudes.

name: sky-background-noise-injection
description: Use when converting an SKIRT IFU-like ideal data cube (skirt_view_(ViewID)_total.fits) into a mock observational image and the output must include per-filter sky background noise consistent with a named survey's throughputs.

name: sky-fraction-correction-of-spectra
description: Use when comparing angular power spectra measured on a masked/partial-sky map (e.g., destriped B-Machine Q/U maps with ~50% sky cut) against full-sky predictions such as the white-noise C_l = Omega_pix * sigma^2 * f_samp / hits.

name: sky-noise-correction-factor-application
description: Use when validating simulated survey light curves against measured uncertainties and residual scatter/means indicate the simulated sky-noise underestimates the observed per-band noise, as seen for skysurvey-simulated ZTF SN Ia DR2 data.

name: slow-roll-observable-prediction-generation
description: Use when theoretical predictions of slow-roll single-field inflation models (spectral observables over a model prior/reheating grid) are needed as a forward model for CMB comparison or Bayesian model selection.

name: small-body-flyby-image-series-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic, physically based fly-by images of an SSSB from an input 3-D shape model with controlled trajectory, light parameters, and camera intrinsics (e.g., to feed an SfM/MVS pipeline or test imaging algorithms).

name: small-body-flyby-scene-rendering
description: Use when you need rapid generation of synthetic spacecraft camera images of a small-body (e.g., asteroid 25143 Itokawa) fly-by, or closed-loop GNC/visual-navigation simulation where per-image render time must be seconds, not minutes.

name: smc-posterior-approximation
description: Use when you need to sample the posterior of a GP model whose covariance structure is itself uncertain — e.g. inferring kernel compositions from noisy time series (stellar variability, exoplanet transit light curves) rather than fixing a kernel a priori.

name: smc-posterior-sampling
description: Use when a time series (e.g. a stellar-variability curve or transit light curve loaded as a JAX array) needs GP regression where the covariance structure should be inferred from the data rather than specified explicitly, and posterior samples with uncertainty estimates are required.

name: smoothed-particle-hydrodynamics-simulation
description: Use when a task requires evolving hydrodynamic particle data for Lagrangian problems (e.g. Sedov blast waves in 2D/3D, Sod shock tubes, Noh tests) and a scalable SPH code with MPI-parallel tree structures is appropriate.

name: sn-type-verification-against-injected-templates
description: Use when validating an automated spectral classification pipeline on simulated data where the true SN type (Ia, Ibc, II) is known per spectrum — e.g. computing typing efficiency per contrast bin and the core-collapse-as-Ia false-positive rate.

name: snia-stretch-colour-parameterisation
description: Use when you have simulated or observed SN Ia multi-band light curves (e.g. skysurvey dset.data with selection-corrected fluxes) and need SALT2 stretch/colour fits plus a redshift-bias assessment to define a volume-limited sample.

name: snid-template-cross-correlation-matching
description: Use when a extracted 1D supernova spectrum (e.g. from SEDm/IFS data) must be spectroscopically typed (Ia, Ibc, II) with redshift and phase estimates, and a quantitative confidence measure such as rlap is needed to flag uncertain classifications.

name: snr-dependence-performance-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether higher SNR in some photometric bands yields a significant boost in MBASC (AGN vs SFG) classification performance, e.g. before deploying the classifier on shallower or noisier survey data.

name: sod-shock-tube-simulation-setup
description: Use when a hydrodynamic validation or benchmark run is needed — e.g. a shock-capturing test case with identical initial conditions across two builds (such as comparing the MPI backend against a Legion or Kokkos backend) using FleCSPH's Sod tube generators and drivers.

name: sodtube-parameter-file-tuning
description: Use when reproducing or scaling the FleCSPH Sod shock tube validation in 1D/2D/3D: you have a compiled FleCSPH build and need to set up or adjust the simulation parameter file and initial-condition particle count.

name: soft-thresholding-proximal-operator-implementation
description: Use when a PALM or other proximal-splitting optimizer needs an l1 proximal step on wavelet coefficients of spatial parameter maps to regularize them while staying close to the previous iterate.

name: solar-abundance-pattern-configuration
description: Use when setting up equilibrium condensation runs that must start from a solar (Solar System) abundance pattern, e.g. to establish a 1e-6 bar baseline Tc before varying pressure, metallicity, or C/O.

name: solar-euv-adaptive-compression-strategy-selection
description: Use when a pipeline must choose between relative- (REL) and absolute- (ABS) error-bounded compression strategies per input, e.g. for Solar Orbiter/EUI FSI or HRI_EUV FITS images with a given bound (e.g. 1e-3).

name: solar-extreme-ultraviolet-image-analysis
description: Use when SDO/AIA 193 or 304 Å post-eruption-arcade observations exist for a CME and a flux-rope magnetic field scaling (β_M) must be estimated observationally instead of assumed by hand (e.g., replacing assumed FRB scalings such as 4 and 2 from Table 1).

name: solar-neighborhood-velocity-distribution-peak-matching
description: Use when fitting a non-axisymmetric Galactic potential (bar + spiral arms) to Gaia DR3 disk-star kinematics, e.g. matching local velocity-space moving groups and phase-space ridges.

name: solar-orbiter-eui-data-handling
description: Use when input data are Solar Orbiter/EUI FITS images (L2 hrieuv174 or FSI observing files) and the goal is error-bounded lossy compression, rate-distortion evaluation, or transmission-time reduction analysis for deep-space downlink planning.

name: solar-system-observer-ephemeris-positioning
description: Use when simulating zodiacal emission as seen by a non-Earth observer (e.g. Mars), or when validating Model.evaluate point values against documented reference intensities in MJy/sr.

name: solar-wind-arrival-time-verification-against-omni
description: Use when ensemble CME in situ predictions (B, Bz, velocity, Kp profiles from FIDO/OSPREI) must be validated against observed solar wind data such as OMNI at 1 AU, including shock arrival time within a tolerance.

name: solar-wind-background-parameter-configuration
description: Use when setting up an OSPREI input text file for ANTEATR-PARADE propagation and you must specify the ambient solar wind state (drag coefficient, speed, density, magnetic field) that the CME propagates into.

name: solid-condensate-opacity-computation
description: Use when you have a converged multispecies cloud profile (layered Mg-silicate clouds over an Fe cloud) and need solid opacities and a mid-infrared spectrum, especially to reproduce or interpret the 8–10 μm MgSiO3/Mg2SiO4 absorption feature.

name: solid-opacity-extinction-calculation
description: Use when you have converged cloud-model output (dominant condensed species per atmospheric layer) and need solid opacities and the wavelength-dependent extinction of the cloud layer for spectra or retrieval.

name: solver-validation-against-reference-outputs
description: Use when a re-implemented level-population or line-emissivity solver must be validated against published HyLight reference values (3p population 1.64e-17 cm**(-3); H alpha emissivity 3.451e-21 erg/(cm**3*s)) at ne=1e2 cm**(-3), nHI=1e-5 cm**(-3), nHII=1e2 cm**(-3), T=1e4 K.

name: space-scene-illumination-and-camera-configuration
description: Use when you need to define lighting conditions, light parameters, and camera intrinsic parameters for a synthetic space-scene render — e.g. simulating fly-by imaging geometry of an asteroid or comet with SISPO/Blender before invoking the Cycles path-tracing render.

name: space-weather-forecast-figure-standardization
description: Use when you have completed an OSPREI run (single simulation or ensemble) and need to convert its systematic standardized output data files into user-friendly figures for space weather forecasting or further custom plotting.

name: space-weather-in-situ-property-averaging
description: Use when an OSPREI ensemble run (nRuns > 1 with a .ens file) must be summarized as spatial maps showing where the CME impacts the satellite, and how averaged in situ properties vary across the lat–lon footprint.

name: spacecraft-attitude-perturbation-modelling
description: Use when SISPO/Orekit trajectory propagations must be augmented with external-force attitude perturbations (dust impacts, atmospheric drag, gravity gradient) that the baseline perfect-attitude-control model ignores.

name: spacecraft-camera-model-configuration
description: Use when building a synthetic imaging pipeline for a small-body fly-by or proximity-operations scenario and camera intrinsics, trajectory, illumination, or renderer (OpenGL vs Cycles) must be set before image generation.

name: sparse-banded-matrix-verification
description: Use when auditing or reconstructing a sparse tau-method linear system: you have Chebyshev T_n differential operators and need to confirm that after T-to-U conversion, Dirichlet basis recombination, and mode-interleaving, the resulting pencil is banded and sparse.

name: sparse-jacobian-sparsity-analysis
description: Use when a large stiff ODE system (e.g. cosmological background+thermodynamics+perturbation equations) is compiled from symbolic equations and you need an analytical sparse Jacobian that is verified to match the true sparsity pattern and numerical derivatives.

name: sparse-targeted-eigenvalue-solve
description: Use when you need targeted eigenvalues or eigenmodes of a linear PDE discretized on a spectral basis, swept over control parameters such as horizontal wavenumber, and the dense spectrum is too large or you only want modes near a known frequency/growth-rate target.

name: spatial-density-distribution-visualization
description: Use when the analysis goal is to inspect how the IPD components of a zodiacal light model are distributed in space — i.e., you have a supported model (e.

name: spaxel-polygon-overlap-computation
description: Use when a monochromatic slice of a host galaxy model cube built on square PS1 pixels (0.50 arcsec after 2x2 rebinning) must be resampled onto the mismatched hexagonal SEDm spaxel grid for scene-model fitting.

name: specframe-attribute-configuration
description: Use when a spectral coordinate must be re-expressed in another system (e.g. heliocentric VRAD at RestFreq=345.8 GHz to LSR frequency in Hz): set up two SpecFrames with differing System/Unit/StdOfRest and convert between them.

name: specific-heat-computation-from-molecular-line-lists
description: Use when you need temperature-dependent specific heats (heat capacities) for a molecule/isotopologue and already have access to an ExoMol (or HITRAN/HITEMP) line-list folder with its .def definition, states, and partition-function files.

name: spectral-analysis-of-field-fluctuations
description: Use when time-resolved electromagnetic field fluctuations on a spatial grid (e.g. from 1D Vlasiator wave-test runs) must be decomposed into ω(k) dispersion curves per propagation angle and validated against analytical linear-theory solutions.

name: spectral-continuum-normalization
description: Use when an extracted SEDm transient spectrum (from HyperGal scene modeling or standard PSF extraction) must be prepared for SNID template typing, or when extraction quality is scored via continuum-divided spectral RMS over 4000–8000 Å.

name: spectral-continuum-subtraction
description: Use when preprocessing 1D FITS spectra (e.g. from the AAOmega spectrograph) before cross-correlation redshifting, so that continuum-dominated flux is removed and only feature information enters the autoz cross-correlation.

name: spectral-coordinate-system-conversion
description: Use when a spectrum's axis is expressed in one spectral system (System, Unit, StdOfRest, e.g. VRAD km/s heliocentric with RestFreq 345.8 GHz) and it must be re-expressed in another (e.g. FREQ in Hz, LSR standard of rest).

name: spectral-cross-correlation-redshift-matching
description: Use when you need automatic redshifts and correlation peaks for generic FITS spectra (e.g. from the AAOmega spectrograph), covering stellar, galaxy, and quasar object types, especially at low signal-to-noise.

name: spectral-cube-monochromatic-slice-projection
description: Use when a square-pixelated hyperspectral model cube (e.g. from photometric SED fitting) must be regridded onto a hexagonal IFS spaxel grid with mismatched pixel geometries, using polygon overlap fractions rather than resampling.

name: spectral-irregularity-analysis
