description: Use when re-analyzing Fermi-LAT AGN observations for ALP-induced spectral oscillations and you need irregularity-based 95% CL exclusion limits around ma ~ 1 neV instead of ALP model fitting.

name: spectral-ivp-benchmark-execution
description: Use when reproducing or extending parallel scaling studies of spectral PDE solvers: you need to run hydro/MHD IVP benchmarks across multiple core counts and compute parallel efficiency from wall-clock timings.

name: spectral-method-pde-simulation
description: Use when a PDE-based physical simulation (fluid dynamics, waves, eigenvalue problems) must be solved at high accuracy with spectral methods, e.g. reproducing resolution-comparison benchmarks or spectral-convergence series.

name: spectral-multidomain-boundary-condition-configuration
description: Use when a PDE must be solved on a graph/network of coupled 1D segments (e.g., optical network dynamics), requiring vertex-matching boundary conditions and spectral time stepping in Dedalus.

name: spectral-order-pixel-rejection
description: Use when building a stellar template from reduced S2D echelle observations and you must decide which frames and which pixels per spectral order are trustworthy enough to enter the co-add, prior to RV estimation.

name: spectral-pde-solver-configuration
description: Use when a PDE initial/boundary-value or eigenvalue problem must be solved with spectral accuracy in Dedalus, e.g. symbolic vectorial equation entry, 2D/3D Fourier-Chebyshev domains, sparse/dense eigen-solves, or shock/eddy-resolving IVPs.

name: spectral-relative-rms-error-analysis
description: Use when validating a simulated SEDm cube extraction where a known input spectrum was injected: comparing extracted vs. input spectra to characterize extraction error as a function of SN-host contrast.

name: spectral-smoothing-filter-implementation
description: Use when preprocessing Poisson-noised quasar/astronomical spectra prior to autoz cross-correlation matching, and you need a smoothing filter that preserves emission-line peak locations rather than flattening them.

name: spectrogram-metadata-verification
description: Use when a GWpy TimeSeries (e.g., L1 strain from GWOSC around GW150914) has been transformed with ts.spectrogram() and the resulting Spectrogram's time/frequency binning (dt, df, shape) must be verified before rendering or further analysis.

name: spectroscopic-line-list-file-handling
description: Use when a task requires acquiring molecular line list files from exomol.com or HITRAN/HITEMP, laying them out in PyExoCross's expected directory structure, or converting between ExoMol and HITRAN formats before running post-processing.

name: spectroscopic-quantum-number-formatting
description: Use when converting ExoMol line lists (e.g. 24Mg-1H__XAB .states.bz2/.trans.bz2) to HITRAN format with PyExoCross and the output must carry molecule-specific quantum numbers instead of placeholder values.

name: spectroscopic-template-matching
description: Use when FITS spectra from a fibre-fed spectrograph (e.g. AAOmega/2dF) need automated redshifts and per-match confidence labels, or when reconstructing/QA-ing an autoz-style cross-correlation matcher and its QOP decision boundaries.

name: spectroscopic-transition-summing
description: Use when you have an ExoMol molecular line list (e.g. H2O 1H2-16O POKAZATEL .trans/.states/.def files) and need a cooling function W(T) on a temperature grid rather than spectra or cross-sections.

name: spectroscopy-data-serialization-to
description: Use when an Athena Project file (.prj, e.g. fe_athena.prj with Fe2O3/Fe3C/FeO XAFS data or cyanobacteria.prj) must be imported into Larch and its per-group spectra and processing parameters extracted into a structured JSON record.

name: spectrum-binning-with-window-functions
description: Use when a forward model produces unbinned C_ell spectra that must be projected onto the binned band powers of a candl likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TTTEEE), or when generating mock data vectors for forecasting or bin-width optimisation.

name: spectrum-irregularity-quantification
description: Use when you have binned count/flux spectra (e.g. from Fermi-LAT) and need to test for ALP-induced spectral irregularity without directly fitting ALP models to the observed spectrum.

name: sph-initial-data-generation
description: Use when a FleCSPH simulation run is blocked because no initial particle data exists: the task names a shipped example problem (Sod tube, Noh, Sedov, oscillating star) and requires generating the lattice/particle setup before invoking hydro_2d/3d or newtonian drivers.

name: sph-neighbor-list-construction
description: Use when constructing per-particle smoothing-neighbor lists from particle data (e.g. a Sod shock tube run) with FleCSPH/FleCSI, especially in a distributed MPI setting where some octree nodes are owned by other ranks and blocking traversal would stall the rank.

name: sph-parameter-file-configuration
description: Use when setting up a FleCSPH simulation run (e.g. Sod tube, Sedov, oscillating star) and you need to select, copy, and edit a .par parameter file to define particle count and match it to the right generator and driver executable.

name: sph-particle-snapshot-analysis
description: Use when a self-gravitating SPH simulation has produced H5part snapshots and you must verify FMM conservation of linear momentum and, at first-order multipole expansion, angular momentum.

name: sph-shock-tube-simulation-execution
description: Use when validating an SPH hydrodynamics code against the Sod shock tube problem, or when you need to reproduce the FleCSPH sodtube_t1 workflow (generator + hydro driver + H5part output) in 1D/2D/3D.

name: spherical-hii-region-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when validating an analytic equilibrium radiative-transfer solver against a reference code for a spherically symmetric gas distribution with a central point source, by comparing radial ionization-fraction and temperature profiles.

name: spherical-isotropic-background-radiative-transfer
description: Use when a task needs radial ionization/temperature structure of a cosmological gaseous halo (e.g. an NFW profile) illuminated by a meta-galactic background rather than a central point source, and multiple background/temperature-treatment models must be compared.

name: spin-dependent-coupling-extraction-at-nuclear-scale
description: Use when a simplified model with a vector mediator requires spin-dependent DM-nucleon coupling extraction at low energy, and RG running/operator mixing between the mediator mass scale and nuclear scale must be quantified for direct detection bounds.

name: spin-independent-spin-dependent-scattering-combination
description: Use when a task requires a direct detection likelihood for arbitrary combinations of spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP scattering processes at one or more benchmark dark matter model points.

name: spitzer-spectra-resolution-matching
description: Use when adding low/medium-resolution space-based spectra (e.g. Spitzer IRS spectroscopy) to a radiative-transfer SED fit whose model libraries are sampled on a coarser wavelength grid, so spectra and models must be resolution-matched before fitting.

name: spline-gradient-interpolation
description: Use when migration-torque coefficients (Jiménez & Masset 2017, Masset 2017, Paardekooper et al. 2010 via Grishin et al. 2023) must be evaluated on a solved pAGN Sirko & Goodman or Thompson disk and the local surface-density, thermal, and pressure gradients are required at each orbital radius.

name: sql-astronomical-catalog-retrieval
description: Use when a pipeline needs raw photometric source data from SDSS (optionally cross-matched with WISE) and the authors provide ready-made SQL queries (e.g. the 'sql_query_casjobs' file) to fetch them via SkyServer CasJobs.

name: sse2-avx2-vectorized-transpose-optimization
description: Use when a lossless compression pipeline needs a high-throughput bit-level transpose of typed arrays (e.g. CHIME 32-bit visibility integers) and naive per-bit looping is too slow.

name: ssh-port-forwarding-configuration
description: Use when data (e.g. >2 Gb DECam FITS images) resides on a remote server and a browser-based viewer must be reached from a local machine without local storage or software installation.

name: standalone-module-workflow-execution
description: Use when a specific GAMBIT module (e.g. DarkBit) must be exercised on a single benchmark point from a yaml parameter file — e.g. computing the thermal freeze-out relic density — instead of launching a full statistical scan.

name: starlet-wavelet-sparsity-regularization
description: Use when fitting spectral parameters pixel-by-pixel on hyperspectral (IFU) data leaves noisy, ill-posed parameter maps that need spatial regularization to stay physically meaningful at fine scales.

name: starlink-test-dataset-generation
description: Use when reproducing the Section 7.1 benchmark datasets of the HDS/HDF5 reimplementation paper, or when concrete HDSv4, gzipped-HDSv4, and HDF5-backend HDSv5 test files are needed for format-comparison experiments.

name: statistical-equilibrium-solver-invocation
description: Use when you need hydrogen recombination line emissivities or excited-state (n, l) level populations for a gas parcel with known electron/proton/neutral-H densities and temperature, e.g. H alpha at ne=100 cm^-3, T=1e4 K.

name: stdofrest-reference-frame-handling
description: Use when a spectral axis must be transformed between systems defined by different StdOfRest, System or Unit attributes - e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (VRAD) to LSR frequency (FREQ) - using AST SpecFrames.

name: stellar-abundance-pattern-scaling
description: Use when you need to test how condensation temperatures (Tc) of planet-building elements respond to a changed disk elemental abundance pattern — e.g. an overall [M/H] offset or one key element ratio (C/O) at a time — using ECCOplanets.

name: stellar-abundance-simulation-input
description: Use when a condensation simulation needs a realistic, non-solar elemental abundance pattern taken from an observed stellar catalogue (e.g. quality-selected Brewer+2016 stars with S/N > 100 and log g > 3.5) instead of Solar System parameters.

name: stellar-activity-noise-modelling
description: Use when an RV time series (e.g. HD 55693 multi-instrument data) shows activity-correlated periodicities that could masquerade as planets, and you must co-fit Keplerians with magnetic-cycle/sinusoid, SAI, or MOAV noise terms before comparing models by ln Z.

name: stellar-age-metallicity-distribution-mapping
description: Use when a simulated stellar population (e.g. a HESTIA snapshot) must be divided into galactic components (bulge, thin disk, thick disk, halo) via age- and metallicity-based classification before assigning planet occurrence rates per region.

name: stellar-background-transit-separation
description: Use when input is transmission-spectroscopy light curve data containing a transit signal superposed on a slowly varying stellar background, and the goal is to isolate the transit at each wavelength and derive a transmission spectrum.

name: stellar-catalog-cross-matching
description: Use when you have a survey's observed target list and an external reference catalog of known objects of the same class (e.g. M dwarfs within 10 pc) and need the fraction of reference objects actually included in the survey, restricted to those observable from a given site.

name: stellar-identifier-resolution-tic-toi-simbad
description: Use when the only available target specification is a TIC number, TOI number, or a stellar name resolvable in Simbad, and downstream steps (Gaia query within a 200 arcsec search radius, TPF/FFI retrieval) require its sky coordinates.

name: stellar-irradiation-calculation
description: Use when a confirmed planet has well-constrained radius, mass, and density posteriors from a joint Bayesian fit, and a present-day atmospheric mass-loss rate must be estimated that requires host-star irradiation as input.

name: stellar-kinematics-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a sophisticated Jeans-based mass model (GravSphere2) recovers masses more accurately than a simple mass estimator on mock galaxies, especially with sparse LOS velocity samples.
tools: Wolf et al.-type simple mass estimator

name: stellar-lightcurve-detrending
description: Use when combining photometry from multiple instruments (e.g. CHEOPS visits plus several TESS sectors) to fit planetary transits, especially when small planets have low per-transit SNR and instrumental trends could bias radius posteriors.

name: stellar-limb-darkening-parameter-fitting
description: Use when fitting transit light curves (e.g. Kepler long-cadence photometry) where limb darkening controls the transit shape and you want per-planet posterior constraints on limb-darkening coefficients alongside Period, Inclination, a/Rs, and Rp/Rs.

name: stellar-mass-dependent-planet-demographics-analysis
description: Use when comparing planet occurrence rates across galactic components (thin disc, thick disc, bulge, stellar halo) stratified by host type (Sun-like stars vs 0.3–0.5 M⊙ dwarfs), or when assessing whether metallicity ([Fe/H]) drives regional differences in planet populations.

name: stellar-orbit-backward-integration
description: Use when fitting Galactic bar pattern speed, spiral-arm amplitude, phase, pitch angle, or pattern speed to Gaia stellar kinematics (moving groups, median Galactocentric radial-velocity maps) via orbit integration in a non-axisymmetric potential.

name: stellar-spectrum-normalisation
description: Use when headerless two-column stellar spectra (wavelengths in angstroms, flux) need continuum normalisation without supervision, or when automating pseudo-continuum prediction across a batch of O–G star spectra.

name: stellar-spectrum-template-mask-construction
description: Use when you have a reduced stellar spectrum template (e.g. a SERVAL template FITS for a CARMENES VIS/NIR, HARPS, HARPN, or EXPRES target) and need a line-list mask for CCF-based RV computation.

name: stellar-template-construction
description: Use when reduced S2D spectra (HARPS or ESPRESSO) must be combined order-by-order into a stellar template to serve as the reference for template-matching RV extraction or to study template-quality effects on RV precision.

name: stellar-variability-gp-modelling
description: Use when a time series (e.g. stellar light curves from the cond_stellar_variability example data) must be modelled and forecast without hand-picking a covariance kernel, and when interpolation/extrapolation accuracy and credible-interval coverage should be quantified.

name: stellar-velocity-space-visualization
description: Use when reproducing or inspecting Milky Way disk kinematic substructure — local velocity-space moving groups or disk-wide median radial velocity maps — from a non-axisymmetric bar+spiral potential, or comparing such plots to Gaia DR3 observations.

name: stellar-wind-mass-loss-parameter-variation
description: Use when assessing how uncertainty in stellar wind mass loss (e.g. LBV winds at low metallicity, Z=0.001) propagates into binary black hole merger populations, or when reproducing parameter-sensitivity checks like the LVT151012 yield test.

name: stiff-ode-solver-work-precision-benchmarking
description: Use when a stiff ODE system must be integrated with an implicit OrdinaryDiffEq.jl solver and you need to choose a solver and tolerance based on quantitative time-vs-accuracy tradeoffs rather than defaults or intuition.

name: stiff-ode-system-compilation
description: Use when a model is specified as symbolic equations and must be solved as a stiff implicit ODE system where an analytical sparse Jacobian and automatic stage separation (background vs perturbations) are needed for performance and differentiability.

name: stokes-parameter-event-binning
description: Use when you have an ixpeobssim-simulated (or IXPE level-2) FITS event list containing photoelectron emission angles and need to recover polarization degree/angle by computing Stokes parameters in energy bins.

name: stokes-parameter-weighted-histogram-binning
description: Use when you have an ixpeobssim-simulated or IXPE level-2 FITS event list and need to produce Stokes I/Q/U count spectra (PHA1 flavors) as XSPEC input for spectro-polarimetric fitting.

name: stokes-spectrum-binning
description: Use when you have simulated or observed IXPE event lists (FITS format, one per detector unit) and need binned Stokes I/Q/U spectra (PHA1/PHA1Q/PHA1U) for spectro-polarimetric fitting or ensemble statistical analysis.

name: strang-split-leapfrog-time-integration
description: Use when implementing or porting a Vlasov/hybrid-Vlasov solver that must advance a 6D distribution function with noiseless semi-Lagrangian propagation, split into translation and acceleration substeps.

name: string-key-normalization-handling
description: Use when implementing or extending an in-memory DataBlock-style store that carries calculation results between pipeline stages and needs deterministic, case-insensitive string keys and typed (int, double, str, complex) scalar or 1-D array access.

name: stromgren-radius-photon-conservation-check
description: Use when you need to benchmark an equilibrium ionization solver against a published Strömgren sphere test, or to quantify how recombination radiation (case A vs case B vs full transfer) alters an H II region's ionization profile.

name: stromgren-sphere-ionization-profile-simulation
description: Use when you need to compute the radial hydrogen ionization fraction (xHII) for a spherically symmetric, uniform-density gas cloud illuminated by a central monochromatic ionizing source, e.g. reproducing the Iliev et al. (2006) Test 1 Strömgren sphere benchmark.

name: strong-scaling-performance-extraction
description: Use when a paper reports strong-scaling results (e.g., Figure 3 of the Castro paper showing Sedov and wdmerger on OLCF Titan) and you need to extract per-problem core-count behavior, threading mix, and compilers into a table.

name: structure-from-motion-reconstruction
description: Use when synthetic or real imagery of a small-body target is available from multiple known/unrecoverable viewing angles and the goal is to recover camera poses, a point cloud, and a fully reconstructed 3-D model whose accuracy must be quantified against a reference mesh.

name: structured-csv-serialization
description: Use when figure/caption data has been read into structured form (e.g. speedup values per network at grid sizes 16^3–128^3) and must be persisted as a row-per-entity CSV with named columns and a limitations field for validation.

name: structured-jet-energy-profile-implementation
description: Use when modeling GRB afterglow emission with an angular jet structure — e.g., fitting the GRB170817A afterglow lightcurve (Troja et al. data set) jointly with GW and kilonova data in NMMA, or generating a synthetic Gaussian-jet lightcurve table.

name: structured-table-serialization-csv-json
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a published parameter table — e.g. bar pattern speed 37 km/s/kpc, two-armed spiral 13.1 km/s/kpc (~25% contrast), three-armed 16.4 km/s/kpc (~9% contrast) — as a machine-readable CSV/JSON artifact.

name: super-neptune-composition-interpretation
description: Use when a confirmed transiting super-Neptune has published Rp and Mp (e.g. TOI-5005 b: 6.25 ± 0.24 R⊕, 32.7 ± 5.9 M⊕) and you must interpret its density, core/metal fraction, or compare it against the savanna vs ridge population regimes.

name: supernova-remnant-mass-prescription-selection
description: Use when a population-synthesis result (e.g. heavy BBH formation channels, fallback fractions, remnant masses) rests on a supernova engine choice and you need to demonstrate the pathway finding is robust to switching between the delayed and rapid Fryer prescriptions.

name: supernova-remnant-spectral-parameter-reconstruction
description: Use when a Poisson-noised IFU/hyperspectral cube (e.g. Chandra X-ray) with a known number of physical components must have temperature, redshift, and photon index maps reconstructed and benchmarked against per-pixel 1D fits.

name: supernova-spectral-classification
description: Use when a low-resolution (e.g. SEDm/IFS) extracted transient spectrum needs automated SN typing, or when quantifying classification confidence via rlap and top-10 template agreement.

name: supernova-template-simulation
description: Use when a task requires generating synthetic transient (e.g. SN Ia) light curves as they would be observed by a survey such as ZTF, LSST, DES, SNLS, or Roman, including realistic fluxes and per-photopoint uncertainties.

name: surrogate-fit-error-validation
description: Use when building or auditing a reduced-basis surrogate where waveform amplitude/phase values at each of m empirical time nodes must be fit across a parameter grid (e.g. mass ratio q = 1 to 10) and the fit errors must be quantified and bounded.

name: surrogate-model-speed-comparison
description: Use when a learned surrogate model (e.g. an Interpolatory Auto-Encoder decoder) is claimed to be faster than the physical spectral model it was trained to mimic, and the speed-up ratio must be measured and reported.

name: surrogate-online-evaluation-benchmarking
description: Use when a reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate has been built offline (m basis waveforms, m empirical time nodes, c_fit spline coefficient fits) and you must evaluate it at generic parameter values and quantify fidelity-vs-speedup against the fiducial solver.

name: surrogate-regression-testing
description: Use when a built or updated GW surrogate model must be validated: sample parameters randomly (e.g., 1,000 mass ratios in [1,2]), evaluate the surrogate, and check error magnitudes and their parameter dependence against published thresholds.

name: surrogate-vs-fiducial-timing-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how much faster a surrogate waveform model evaluates than the fiducial solver (e.g., EOB-LAL) across sampling rates, or to verify linear-in-L surrogate prediction cost.

name: survey-classification-merging-rules
description: Decision support for assigning suggested quality-of-match (QOP) classes to automatic redshift matches from autoz-style cross-correlation peaks, or for deciding which classification disagreements require manual merging.

name: survey-detection-completeness-correction
description: Use when estimating planet occurrence rates from RV survey data where detections are completeness-limited: you have RV time series per star, planet detections in M pl sin i / P orb space, and need detection-completeness-corrected rates.

name: survey-instrument-calibration
description: Use when simulating survey photometry of transients under real observing conditions and you must match simulated flux uncertainties to measured survey uncertainties (e.g. ZTF g/r/i sky-noise and error floors).

name: survey-sample-statistics-comparison
description: Use when comparing semi-analytical disc-evolution model predictions against an ALMA disc survey catalog (flux- or size-based) to determine under which initial-condition assumptions (e.

name: survey-selection-effect-assessment
description: Use when a flux-limited transient sample must be truncated to an unbiased volume-limited subsample, and you need to identify the redshift above which selection effects bias fitted light-curve parameters.

name: survey-target-catalog-summarization
description: Use when a public survey data release (e.g. CARMENES DR1) must be inventoried: counting raw/pipeline-processed spectra, unique targets, or derived time-series products to reproduce or audit the release's headline numbers.

name: survey-volume-subregion-partitioning
description: Use when estimating error bars or a covariance matrix C_ij on a two-point correlation function measurement, and the survey volume can be subdivided into N spatially distinct sub-regions for delete-one or with-replacement resampling.

name: swig-interface-file-authoring
description: Use when wrapping a C library (e.g. LALSuite) with SWIG and you need to automate annotation of public constants, functions, and classes to produce full SWIG interface files for Python or Octave wrappers.

name: swig-interface-pipeline-operation
description: Use when building Python or Octave wrappers for a C library (e.g. LALSuite) and you need a machine-readable syntax tree of the library's exported public API to drive automated SWIG interface annotation.

name: swig-preprocessor-header-authoring
description: Use when building SWIG bindings for a C library and you need shared wrapper-integration code split into common, language-specific, and library-specific preprocessor headers included by the SWIG interface files.

name: swig-wrapper-compilation
description: Use when SWIG has already generated language wrapper sources (e.g. -python C code or -octave C++ code) and they must be compiled and linked into dynamically loadable modules installable alongside a C library.

name: swig-wrapper-generation-for-c-libraries
description: Use when a C library's public constants, functions, and classes must be made callable from Python or Octave, and header files exist that SWIG can parse and annotate automatically.

name: swig-xml-syntax-tree-parsing
description: Use when building language bindings (e.g. Python/Octave) for a C library where manual SWIG interface annotation is impractical, and you need to enumerate every public constant, function, and class from header files programmatically.

name: swiglal-preprocessor-directive-integration
description: Use when wrapping C library headers (e.g. LALSuite) with SWIG and you need to automate annotation of the interface with SWIGLAL preprocessor directives before the second SWIG pass in -python or -octave mode.

name: switchmap-selectormap-construction
description: Use when input positions must be transformed differently depending on which disjoint Region of a coordinate space they fall in, and AST Mappings must be composed into a piecewise transform.

name: symbolic-cosmology-model-specification
description: Use when building or adapting an Einstein-Boltzmann solver from symbolic equations and you need automated stage separation plus analytical sparse Jacobians instead of approximation-switching schemes and finite-difference Jacobians.

name: symbolic-emulator-usage
description: Use when a pipeline needs As from sigma8 (or vice versa) for LambdaCDM cosmologies and needs sub-percent accuracy without running CAMB, e.g. setting initial conditions from sigma8-matched simulations.

name: symbolic-expression-term-decomposition
description: Use when you have a fitted symbolic expression (e.g. artifact_pk_expression from symbolic_pofk) and need to determine whether individual terms map onto physical features like the turnover scale, spectral index, acoustic/damping features, or baryonic signatures.

name: synchrotron-power-law-spectral-fitting
description: Use when the data cube contains a single synchrotron (non-thermal power-law) component with no unmixing needed, and reliable spectral parameters are required at spatial scales finer than what re-binned per-pixel 1D spectral fits achieve.

name: synthesized-beam-pixel-correlation-bias-correction
description: Use when estimating the background noise level of a dirty/cleaned residual map from radio-synthesis data (e.g. AMI-LA via chimenea) to set a Clean threshold, because cleaned-beam sidelobes correlate neighbouring pixels and deflate naive sigma-clipped RMS estimates.

name: synthetic-benchmark-image-generation
description: Use when you need reproducible synthetic test data with controlled value ranges (bit depths N = 7, 15, 23, 31) to benchmark lossless compression ratios and read speeds between FITS and HDF5 formats.

name: synthetic-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when a fitted model (e.g. a GP background model or transit parameter fit) must be validated against injected ground truth in a synthetic dataset such as the cond_transmission_spectroscopy example shipped with gallifrey.

name: synthetic-lightcurve-fitting
description: Use when the input is a time series (time stamps + flux measurements, e.g. a synthetic transit light curve) and the goal is to separate a transit/background signal while recovering parameters with reliable posterior uncertainties.

name: synthetic-lightcurve-frequency-recovery
description: Use when benchmarking a period-finding/frequency-identification algorithm against a baseline on synthetic time series with a known injected primary frequency, SNR, and number of observations.

name: synthetic-lightcurve-generation
description: Use when a joint GW170817/AT2017gfo/GRB170817A analysis requires a forward-modeled afterglow lightcurve from a structured (Gaussian) jet, e.g. to fit the Troja et al. GRB afterglow data set alongside GW and kilonova data.

name: synthetic-oscillator-data-generation
description: Use when you need synthetic irregularly-sampled time series with known ground-truth dynamics (e.g. to train or benchmark latent ODEs or extrapolation-capable neural differential equation models) and want normalised, controllable data per the thesis specification.

name: synthetic-radio-visibility-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking the paper's compression pipeline (precision reduction with granularity parameter f, then Bitshuffle) and no real correlator dump is available — construct a synthetic (64, 136, 1024) visibility array instead.

name: tabular-data-source-registration
description: Use when you need to make a local or remote CSV/text table available to a Toyz web workspace as a data source before creating Highcharts plots or linked-selection tiles bound to its columns.

name: tabular-result-aggregation-and-export
description: Use when multiple response-function tables from /data (DarkARC output) must be reduced to one comparative summary, e.g. ratios of new vs. known atomic responses per DM-electron operator and target.

name: task-based-runtime-backend-integration
description: Decision support for choosing between FleCSI runtime backends (MPI vs Legion vs Kokkos) for FleCSPH particle simulations, when the goal is a controlled timing comparison using the same parameter file and particle count on each backend.

name: task-parsing
description: Use when building or extending a websocket-based scientific server that must accept, validate, authenticate, and queue task-execution requests (e.g. send_task messages with module/task/parameters) from browser clients.

name: tau-method-boundary-row-construction
description: Use when reproducing or extending Dedalus-style sparse spectral pencils for a 1D boundary-value problem (e.g. Chebyshev Poisson on x in [-1,1]) where you need the staged tau-augmented, recombined, and interleaved banded matrices, not just a solution vector.

name: telescope-filter-throughput-application
description: Use when an ideal SKIRT data cube (skirt_view_(ViewID)_total.fits) must be converted into survey-specific mock images, or when custom filter throughput (.fil) and PSF (numpy array) data need to be folded into a mock observation.

name: temperature-grid-tabulation
description: Use when you have an ExoMol (or ExoAtom/HITRAN/HITEMP) states file with energy levels and degeneracies and need Q(T) values on a fine temperature grid, e.g. as input to spectra or thermodynamic property computations.

name: template-matching-radial-velocity-estimation
description: Use when extracting RV time series from echelle S2D spectra (HARPS or ESPRESSO) and you need a statistically principled per-spectrum RV posterior instead of a per-order weighted average of template-matching shifts.

name: template-matching-rv-extraction
description: Use when extracting RV time-series from ESPRESSO or HARPS S2D echelle spectra and you need a template-matching alternative to CCF methods with lower RV scatter (e.g. ~10% for M-type stars).

name: tensorboard-embedding-visualization
description: Use when astromorph's inference script (pipeline_02_inference.py) has produced embeddings for a set of FITS images (e.g. ALMA protoplanetary disk or Spitzer/Herschel infrared dark cloud images) and you need to inspect morphological structure via TensorBoard.

name: terminal-emulation-subprocess-control
description: Use when a mature, externally-maintained pipeline (e.g. casapy/CASA routines, AMI-reduce) accepts only command-line input and must be incorporated into a fully automated Python reduction pipeline without altering the original code.

name: terminal-velocity-data-normalization
description: Use when kinematic measurements (e.g. terminal velocities from gas tracers) were published under different Galactocentric parameter assumptions (R0, solar motion) and must be made consistent before combining into a unified rotation curve.

name: tess-aperture-flux-contamination-quantification
description: Use when analyzing TESS SPOC PDCSAP or TPF/FFI photometry of a target where nearby Gaia sources may dilute the aperture, or when judging whether a transit/activity signal could originate from a contaminant rather than the target.

name: tess-contaminant-flux-ranking

name: tess-discovery-photometry-radius-comparison

name: tess-photometric-aperture-flux-fraction-computation

name: tess-pixel-response-function-modelling

name: tess-prf-interpolation-and-placement

name: tess-target-pixel-file-handling

name: thermal-history-evolution-bbn

name: thermal-history-network-integration

name: thermal-migration-torque-calculation

name: thermochemical-database-querying

name: thermodynamic-unit-consistency-checking

name: thermonuclear-explosion-modeling-terminology

name: tidal-deformability-computation

name: tiled-image-pyramid-serving

name: tiled-image-rendering-in-web-clients

name: time-series-extrapolation-visualization

description: Use when analyzing Chandra/IFU hyperspectral data cubes where a fixed number of physical components can be assumed and each has a spectral model, and per-pixel 1D fits lack the spatial resolution or low-S/N robustness needed for parameter maps.

name: x-ray-spectral-model-quality-assessment
description: Use when one or more IAE spectral models have been trained (one per physical component) and their generalization must be checked on the 30% held-out validation split before using them as surrogates in SUSHI unmixing.

name: x-ray-spectral-model-simulation
description: Use when building a learned spectral surrogate: you need many synthetic spectra spanning a physical-parameter grid (e.g. temperature, redshift) in a defined energy band, convolved with an instrument response, to train a generative spectral model such as an IAE.

name: xafs-background-subtraction
description: Use when a raw X-ray absorption spectrum (e.g. energy and mu arrays from an ASCII XAFS file such as fe.060) must be background-subtracted to yield chi(k) before Fourier transform or Feff fitting.

name: xafs-fourier-transform-analysis
description: Use when a chi(k) array from background subtraction (autobk) must be converted to a chi(R) spectrum, or when comparing FT window choices (hanning vs parzen/welch/kaiser/gaussian, dk=1 vs 5) for EXAFS data.

name: xafs-spectra-array-ingestion
description: Use when input is a raw ASCII XAFS data file (energy, it, i0 columns) or an Athena .prj project file that must be loaded into Larch Groups before normalization, XANES fitting, or feffit analysis.

name: xafs-spline-spline-parameter-tuning
description: Use when a raw XAS/XAFS spectrum (e.g. energy vs. mu arrays from an ASCII data file such as fe.060) must be converted to chi(k) by background subtraction, or when autobk spline parameters like rbkg=1.0 and kweight=2 need adjustment.

name: xanes-normalization-pre-edge-processing
description: Use when a raw mu(E) XAS spectrum (e.g., ASCII Fe K-edge foil data like fe.060, or an Athena .prj project) must be edge-located and normalized before autobk background subtraction, EXAFS Fourier transforms, or XANES fitting.

name: xml-syntax-tree-generation
description: Use when building language bindings (Python/Octave) for a C library and you need a machine-readable enumeration of its exported public constants, functions, and classes before annotating headers for a second SWIG pass.

name: xray-spectral-model-composition
description: Use when an X-ray spectrum in the OGIP standard must be fitted with a composite model (e.g. absorption times sum of continuum components) and parameters need to be inferred with Bayesian samplers such as NUTS.

name: xray-sz-joint-bayesian-profile-modeling
description: Use when you have X-ray surface brightness, spectroscopic temperature, and/or SZ pressure profiles for a galaxy cluster and need hydrostatic mass or thermodynamic profile reconstruction with posterior uncertainties.

name: xspec-apec-lookup-table-model-evaluation
description: Use when a learned spectral surrogate (e.g. an IAE decoder) needs a baseline computational-cost comparison against the physical look-up-table model it was trained to replace, in an X-ray spectroscopy workflow.

name: xspec-polarization-response-keyword-configuration
description: Use when binned ixpeobssim PHA1/PHA1Q/PHA1U Stokes spectra must be fed into XSPEC for spectro-polarimetric fitting and the per-file XFLT0001 Stokes keyword (Stokes:0/1/2) needs to be set or verified.

name: zenodo-dataset-ingestion
description: Use when a task requires retrieving raw training data from a Zenodo deposit (e.g. 10.5281/zenodo.7310832 or 10.5281/zenodo.15688233) and staging it in the repository layout before header-processing scripts run.

name: zinc-k-edge-chik-extraction
description: Use when raw Zn K-edge (or analogous edge) XAS absorption data — mu vs energy from an ASCII file or Athena project — must be converted to chi(k) via autobk background subtraction before Fourier transforms or Feff-path fitting.

name: zodiacal-emission-extrapolation-beyond-model-validity-range
description: Use when you need zodiacal emission forecasts for a future experiment whose observing bands fall below 1.25 µm or above 240 µm (or below 30 GHz / above 857 GHz), outside the DIRBE/Planck model ranges built into ZodiPy.

name: zodiacal-emission-timestream-binning
description: Use when you have a simulated zodiacal emission timestream for a scanning observer (e.g. DIRBE) and need a binned HEALPix sky map for comparison with calibrated individual observations.

name: zodiacal-light-emission-evaluation
description: Use when you need to compute or verify zodiacal emission intensities (MJy/sr) for specific sky coordinates, observation times, and a solar system observer position, in the DIRBE infrared 1.25-240 µm or microwave 30-857 GHz range.

name: zodiacal-light-model-instantiation
description: Use when simulating zodiacal emission or interplanetary dust number densities for an arbitrary Solar System observer, and a supported zodiacal light model must be initialized at a defined infrared wavelength (1.25–240 µm) or microwave frequency (30–857 GHz).

name: zodiacal-light-timestream-simulation
description: Use when a task requires forward-simulated zodiacal light timestreams or binned zodiacal emission maps for a Solar System observer (e.g. DIRBE-like pointings/times), or when validating a zodiacal light model against DIRBE ZLP reference output.
tools: COBE DIRBE Zodiacal Light Prediction Software

name: ztf-survey-simulation-validation
description: Use when validating that a transient survey simulation reproduces measured light-curve flux uncertainties as a function of observing conditions, or when calibrating simulated sky-noise and error floors per photometric band against real survey data.
